items.title: Fix four metering/tracing defects, and colour the CLI without changing piped output
items.body:
Four defects in metering and tracing, three earlier runtime fixes, and a CLI restyle that provably does not change piped output.

**1552 passed, 12 deselected, 0 failed** · `ruff check .` clean · all 8 `demo` stages + `plan` + `models` green.

## What was wrong

Each of these was reproduced before being fixed, and each now has a test that fails without the fix — confirmed by stashing the source and watching it go red.

| Defect | Cost while open |
|---|---|
| Unreachable `max_seconds` poisoned the deadline guard | `setitimer` raised *after* the SIGALRM handler and process-wide slot were taken, leaking both. A 0.3s ceiling was honoured at 0.30s, then at **5.00s** for the rest of the process — falling back to the mechanism that cannot unwind a blocking syscall |
| Every `async def` node double-charged token re-reports | Ledger keyed by thread ident, but `on_llm_end` is sync and runs on a worker thread under `ainvoke`. Nodes reported **double** their real spend and hit `max_tokens` at half their allowance |
| A bracket in model prose hijacked JSON extraction | `Analysis (note [1]): {"supported": false}` returned a valid **`[1]`** — a fabricated value substituted for the verifier's actual answer |
| Fan-out inflated per-node tokens | Workers absorbed siblings' concurrent spend: 3 workers × 8 tokens traced as **24/16/8**, and `metrics`/`cost` reported 48 for 24 tokens — doubling the estimated bill purely for running in parallel |
| `grapharc plan` trace was missing most of itself | Shipped registry withheld the recorder from `PlannerNode` and `Materializer`: **no `plan` event and no `start`/`end` pair for any executed node**. Three nodes ran; none appeared |
| Planner spend counted twice | The `round` event repeated the `plan` event's tokens, and both are summed on top of node totals. Meter 1979, `metrics` 2558 |
| `RoundRecord.iterations` always `0` | Declared and never assigned; `_charge_back` read the figure and discarded it |

The shipped `plan` trace went from `{admission: 2, round: 2, stop: 1}` to `{plan: 2, admission: 2, round: 2, start: 3, end: 3, stop: 1}`.

A `round` is now treated as an *envelope*, not a measurement — its figures moved to `state_delta` as `round_tokens` / `round_iterations` / `round_duration_ms`, where no reader sums them, so what a round spent stays answerable from the file without being double-counted.

## CLI

Colour hierarchy on a terminal; **byte-identical output when piped**. Styling is decided at print time from the stream's own `isatty()`, which is why no expected block needed touching — `tests/test_readme.py` and `tests/test_cookbook_models.py` byte-compare CLI output against the docs, and both harnesses present a non-tty stdout.

Verified: 50/36/32/18 escapes on a pty for `plan`/`models`/`models --check`/`demo`; **zero** on every piped stream; ANSI-stripped tty output identical to piped output. `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, `--no-color` and `--json` each yield zero escapes.

Contracts re-checked by hand: `--json` is one parseable document with 0-byte stderr; a text-mode failure leaves stdout empty with `error: …` on stderr; `viz` stays raw pasteable Mermaid; `replay`/`diff` emit only the engine formatter's text.

New `grapharc/cli/style.py` is **stdlib only** — no dependency added, since `rich` is not in the lock and the README markets a four-package runtime dep list. No glyphs, boxes or rules even on a terminal, deliberately: README and two cookbook pages print these blocks verbatim, so tty-only decoration would make what a user sees diverge from what the docs show.

## Also included

- README status section records each closed defect and what it cost.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.md` pins the seven-section format used by issues #1–#10. **This only takes effect once merged to `main`.**
- `uv.lock` is a stale-lock refresh (`pyproject` already said `0.1.1`, lock said `0.1.0a0`), not a dependency change.

## Known gap

The natural regression test for the CLI work — *escape-stripped tty output equals piped output* — is proven ad-hoc but **not committed**. Without it, a future change could leak an escape into piped output and no test would catch it. Worth adding before or shortly after merge.

items.title: fix(ocp): converge Lane A reference to 1e-10 for machine-precision parity
items.body:
## What

The King Air three-lane example showed a small residual TOFL gap (Lane A
`3054.61 ft` vs Lane B `3054.64 ft`, ~9e-6 relative). This closes it.

## Why

The gap was **not** a model difference. The upstream
`run_kingair_analysis` stops its Newton solver at `atol=rtol=1e-6`
(`maxiter=10`), which under-converges the balanced-field takeoff by
~0.03 ft. The OCP builder (Lane B) drives to `1e-10`. So the reference
itself was the loose side.

Lane A now re-converges the upstream problem to `1e-10` after
`run_kingair_analysis` returns. With both lanes tight, all four reported
metrics agree to machine precision:

| Metric | rel. diff (before) | rel. diff (after) |
|--------|------:|------:|
| OEW | 0 | 0 |
| Fuel burn | 1.5e-8 | 1.7e-13 |
| MTOW | 0 | 0 |
| TOFL | 9.4e-6 | 1.1e-10 |

## Changes

- `lane_a/full_mission.py` -- tighten Newton to `1e-10` and re-run the model
- `shared.py` -- `TOL_TOFL` `2e-3` -> `1e-6` (the old value only existed to
  absorb the reference's under-convergence)
- `tests/test_parity.py` -- `test_b_matches_a` is the lane comparison check;
  it now asserts all four metrics including MTOW, mirroring `compare.py`
- `compare.py` / `README.md` -- refresh expected numbers and the explanation

## Verification

```
uv run python -m pytest packages/ocp/examples/kingair_mission/tests/ -v --rootdir=.
# 3 passed

uv run python packages/ocp/examples/kingair_mission/compare.py
# OEW 0.00e+00 | Fuel 1.69e-13 | MTOW 0.00e+00 | TOFL 1.06e-10
```

items.body:
## Description

Beszel `2.0.1`. This update repairs the system detail panel, which regressed against recent Beszel agent versions.

Recent Beszel agents omit several `info` fields the extension previously treated as guaranteed (hostname `h`, kernel `k`, CPU cores `c`, CPU model `m`) and report network throughput via `bb` (bytes) instead of the deprecated `b` (MB). As a result the detail view rendered `undefined` for Network, Chip, Kernel, and Hostname.

Changes:

- Network reads the current `bb` field and displays a human readable rate
- Hostname falls back to the connection host when the agent does not report one
- Chip and Kernel render only when the agent provides them
- Added GPU, load average, temperature, battery, and extra filesystem metrics when reported by the agent
- Updated the `get-system` AI tool to the same field mapping
- Bundled with a dependency upgrade to latest and a migration to the ESLint flat config

## Screencast

items.title: docs: rewrite the metrics against the current gate, widen mypy
items.body:
## Why

`RESUME_METRICS.md` reported baseline MRR near **0.88**, from the gate #37 replaced. The system now measures **0.41–0.48**. Anyone who read the doc and then ran the pipeline would have got numbers that did not match — on a portfolio document, the worst kind of wrong. The README carried the same stale claims plus pre-fix latency.

## The adaptation numbers are not scattered

Ordered by training-set size, the four runs are monotonic up to the two large ones:

| training samples | improvement |
| ---------------- | ----------- |
| 124              | +0.62%      |
| 250              | +0.87%      |
| 400              | +9.86%      |
| 450              | +8.29%      |

The adapter looked unreliable because the drift window captured different amounts of data each run, not because the adapter is unreliable. Four points cannot establish a threshold and the doc says so.

Also now recorded: **NDCG@10 fell on the run that gained 8.29% MRR** — the adapter sharpens the top of the ranking without improving the graded ordering below it.

## Latency, re-measured

Batch 32 p50 went from 7504–14208 ms to **1603–3356 ms** across three runs, after the serving CPU limit went 0.50 → 2.00 and fixed 256-token padding became dynamic. Batch 1 is now 27–71 ms, inside the spec target; the remaining gap is throughput under batching.

## ADRs

ADR-003 is marked superseded rather than rewritten — its analysis of the degenerate diagonal is why two views exist at all. ADR-006 records the supervised-pairs objective that replaced dropout views.

## mypy 12 → 16 modules

Adding the linguistic worker caught a real defect: `DocumentForAnalysis.occurred_at` is `datetime | None`, so deriving window bounds from it could evaluate `None + timedelta`. The column is NOT NULL and no run had hit it, which is why it survived review and the tests. Bounds now come from `min`/`max` over the timestamps that exist.

182 passed, mypy and ruff clean.

items.title: Fix baseline map fire cutoff after early August
items.body: ## Problem On the **2024 Peak Fire Baseline**, map fires rendered through ~Aug 4 then went blank, while the UI (slider / header) still reported fires present. The Render access logs only show `GET /api/metrics/viewport?... 200` — that path is fine and **does not** explain the blank map. Metrics and the map use different data sources. ## Root cause (confirmed on production) `GET /api/timeline-data?mode=baseline` returned exactly **20,000** fire points (silent `.limit(20000)` with no `ORDER BY`): - Cumulative coverage effectively ends around **2024-08-03** (~19,966 rows); almost none after Aug 4 - `daily[].fire_count` and `/api/metrics/viewport` are uncapped → UI says fires exist - Mapbox filtered `timeline.fires` by date → empty markers after the truncated window - `/api/points?date=2024-08-05` already returns the full day (5,126 fires); Sep 11 returns 8,806 ## Fix - Stop dumping fire points from `/api/timeline-data` (keep `daily` aggregates + `fires_total`) - Map loads the playhead day via `GET /api/points` (AbortController while scrubbing) - Document the split in README / API header ## After deploy Scrub baseline past Aug 4 into September; map markers should match daily / viewport fire counts.

items.title: Enforce deterministic CI budgets and fix the defects they surfaced
items.body:
## Description

Closes the integrity gap from the audit: the CI **documented** performance/bundle budget enforcement but neither actually gated (`continue-on-error` on Lighthouse; the bundle check only `echo`ed warnings). Turning them on surfaced two real defects the disabled gate had been hiding — both fixed here.

## Defects the gate was hiding (fixed)

1. **Homepage hero double-loaded (558KB).** A global `<link rel=preload>` pulled `performance.webp` (159KB) on **all six pages** (wasted on the five that don't show it), while the hero background loaded the 399KB **JPEG**. The hero now serves **WebP only** (159KB), preloaded from `HomeView` via a new `usePageHead({ preloadImage })` option — so only the home route pays for it, and it's not double-loaded.
2. **A 404 on every page.** A broken font `<link rel=preload>` + inline `@font-face` pointed at a non-existent jsdelivr `.woff2`, throwing a console error site-wide. Removed both; the font still loads via the working async `@fontsource` CSS.

## Enforcement

- **Bundle size** now **fails CI** if any JS file > 200KB or CSS > 50KB (per file, uncompressed). Current: JS 124KB, CSS 29KB — comfortable headroom.
- **Lighthouse** drops `continue-on-error`. Enforced (deterministic quality): **accessibility ≥ 95, best-practices ≥ 90, no console errors, JS/CSS resource sizes, text compression**. Advisory (`warn`, reported not gating): performance/SEO scores, timing metrics (FCP/LCP/CLS/TBT/SI), and image/total transfer weight — these vary with the CI runner or with image-rich portfolio content.
- **README** updated to state exactly what is enforced vs advisory.

## Verified locally
Lighthouse assertions pass (exit 0), 320 unit tests + coverage floor, production build, bundle sizes within budget, and the home hero renders (screenshot-checked).

## Heads-up for review
The enforced Lighthouse gates (a11y/best-practices/console-errors) load the site's font from jsdelivr, so they depend on that CDN being reachable during the CI Lighthouse run. GitHub runners have reliable internet, but **this PR's own Lighthouse job is the real test** — if it's green, enforcement is validated.

## Not in scope — a decision for you
Enabling the gate revealed deeper perf debt that involves **design decisions I've deliberately left to you** (see PR discussion): the site pulls **~3.5MB of fonts** (Iosevka Aile, all three weights) from a third-party CDN, and the **/works** and **/about** gallery pages load **1.4–1.8MB of images**. Options range from subsetting/self-hosting the font to tuning image lazy-loading — all product/design calls.

items.title: Re-audit fixes: per-class metric attribution + coordinate single-sourcing + doc/dead-code sweep
items.body:
## What this does

Re-audit polish for nyc-real-estate-predictor: three MEDIUM findings + a five-item LOW sweep.
No model retrain, no artefact change. Net -36 lines (deletion-first).

### MEDIUM

- **Single-source the landmark coordinates.** `run_training.py` carried a third hardcoded copy
  of the reference coordinates (config.py defines them, features.py builds `REFERENCE_POINTS`
  from that, and run_training re-declared the same literals and trained on them). Import the
  canonical dict instead, so a coordinate edit can't silently skew training against serving.
  Values are byte-identical, so artefacts are unchanged.
- **Drop a dead artefact-contract helper.** `tests/test_artifact_contract.py::_feature_row` had
  no caller (every probe goes through `_api_payload`) and constructed features the repo's own
  doc-gates blocklist as removed (LOG_SQFT, DIST_NEAREST_SUBWAY, PROPERTY_CATEGORY). Delete it +
  its now-unused imports, and fix the module docstring that still described a label encoder /
  predicted class index the sealed one-regressor doesn't have.
- **Correct the MODEL_CARD stratification claim.** It said the split was "stratified on price
  zone" / "on PRICE_ZONE"; the code stratifies on pooled price quartiles (`pd.qcut(PRICE, 4)`)
  as a balancing key, with served zone labels coming from train-derived cut-points. Aligned with
  the code and the README.

### LOW sweep

- Delete dead `CV_FOLDS` / `OPTUNA_TRIALS` from config (zero uses; README declares "Tuning: none").
- Pin the pre-split imputation as a **verified no-op** on the shipped snapshot (BEDS/BATH/
  PROPERTYSQFT arrive complete) with a spy test, and disclose that if those columns ever arrive
  with NaNs the pooled fill would cross the train/test split, so it must then move to the
  train-only fit/apply family. No retrain.
- README testing row: drop the rot-prone "88.27%" coverage snapshot; keep the enforced 78% gate.
- Document the drift threshold, fairness min-group, and health `n_min` as chosen monitoring
  operating points, not derived bounds.
- explain.py ships only a single-output regressor, so the multi-class SHAP branches (and the
  synthetic test exercising them) were unreachable; delete them and justify the TreeExplainer
  fallback's broad except in one line.

## Verification

Local, Python 3.13: ruff / ruff format --check / mypy (src+api+benchmarks) / bandit all clean;
`pytest` 211 passed, 87.93% coverage (gate 78); `scripts/verify_gates.py` all 23 mutations caught.

---

### Added during pre-push re-audit (post-validation)

An independent re-audit found the committed metrics artifact misattributed its per-class rows.
`evaluate_classifier` passed the semantic-order labels as `target_names` while sklearn ordered
the report/confusion-matrix rows alphabetically, so `reports/training_metrics.json` reported
e.g. Low F1 = 0.604 when the true Low was 0.814. Macro/weighted F1 and every headline number
are order-invariant and were unaffected; only the per-class attribution was wrong.

- Fix: pass `labels=` to both `confusion_matrix` and `classification_report`, plus a regression
  test that fails on the old alphabetical swap (`50b3e33`).
- Regenerated the artifact by re-running training from a clean tree under the pinned environment
  (Python 3.12.13 / numpy 1.26.4 / sklearn 1.8.0): every model file reproduced **bit-identical**
  (same SHA-256), only the metric rows re-keyed (`c3fc915`).
- Also purged dead env-var surface (`GEOAPIFY`/`GOOGLE_MAPS`/`API_HOST`/`API_PORT`, zero
  consumers) and corrected the HF Dockerfile comment that called the shipped model a "classifier"
  (it ships one regressor).

Branch is now 5 commits (`fafc4df`, `48f63e6`, `7857741`, `50b3e33`, `c3fc915`). Gates re-run:
212 passed, ~88% coverage (gate 78), 23/23 mutations caught, ruff/format/mypy/bandit green.

items.title: Fix model quality, restore working explainability, add test suite and CI
items.body:
Two sessions of work on model correctness and test coverage. Three commits, each independently reviewable.

## Summary

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Churn ROC-AUC | 0.795 | **0.879** |
| Churn F1 | 0.776 | **0.838** |
| Churn Brier | 0.185 | **0.138** |
| CLV Spearman | not measured | **0.588** |
| CLV top-decile lift | not measured | **3.63×** |
| Tests | 0 | **60** |
| XGBoost in report | never ran | runs on all tasks |

## Three bugs fixed

**1. XGBoost never ran.** `try/except Exception` around the import swallowed a real failure, so no XGBoost run ever reached the training report despite being pinned in requirements and advertised in the README. Root cause was a missing OpenMP runtime (`libomp.dylib`) on macOS — not a version incompatibility. CI now installs `libgomp1` and asserts the import, so this cannot silently return.

**2. Per-customer SHAP returned all zeros.** `predict.py` passed a single row to `shap.Explainer`, which used that same row as its own background distribution — explaining a point against itself. Every contribution cancelled to zero while the dashboard's "Why this prediction?" panel kept rendering confident-looking output with arbitrary country dummies as top features. Fixed by persisting a 200-row background sample per model.

**3. Recorded best model could diverge from the saved pipeline.** `_train_churn_model` selected on Brier score while `train_all_models` recorded the max-ROC-AUC name. Latent (both picked LogisticRegression), now structurally impossible — the trainers return the selected name.

## Churn: Recency restored

`Recency` was excluded with the comment "avoid direct label leakage: ChurnLabel is derived from Recency threshold." That comment was stale — the label is now a future-window indicator, so history-side Recency is legitimate, and it was the strongest available signal. This accounts for most of the ROC-AUC gain.

## CLV: the metric was the problem

Candidates now fit on `log1p(revenue)`, plus a two-stage zero-inflated model (57% of customers have zero future revenue).

**R² and RMSE barely moved, and that is the finding.** The single largest holdout customer contributes **81% of the total sum of squares** and is larger than anything in training, so squared-error metrics rank models mostly by their fit to one unlearnable point. Selection now uses Spearman correlation, reported alongside top-decile lift — the metrics that match how CLV is actually consumed here (VIP flagging, priority ordering, targeting).

Honest limitation, documented in the README: all four candidates land within Spearman 0.53–0.59. The ceiling is the feature set, not the algorithm.

## Tests

60 tests on synthetic frames, so expected values are hand-computed rather than copied from current output. Both regression guards were **mutation-tested**:

- Removing the SHAP background reproduces the bug at exactly `0.000000`
- Switching `build_churn_dataset` back to the full frame fails with `got 5100.0, expected 100.0`

Coverage 62% overall; 100% on `recommendation_engine`, 82% on `feature_engineering`. Integration tests skip cleanly when artifacts are absent.

## Also

5-fold CV on both tasks, `__pycache__` and `.coverage` untracked, README corrected (Python version, output-field contract, real metrics).

## Note for reviewers

CI checkout pulls the 80 MB committed CSV on every run, so builds are slow. Moving that to a download step is worth doing separately.

items.title: Stage 2: make the numbers right — DSP correctness fixes
items.body:
## Summary

Stage 2 "make the numbers right" — a sweep of DSP correctness fixes so the metrics reported by `analyze` and `compare` reflect real signal properties rather than measurement artifacts. Each fix is backed by a deterministic regression test (new pink-noise and mix-like fixtures) and several were surfaced by Codex adversarial review.

## DSP correctness fixes

- **DC offset** removed at load and reported; RMS/crest/bands are no longer skewed by a DC pedestal.
- **Sample peak** measured on the *raw* waveform (before DC removal) so DC-heavy files don't under-report headroom and suppress clipping/headroom warnings.
- **Crest factor** measured per channel — panned content no longer reads ~3 dB too healthy.
- **Band energies** normalized relative to broadband density; reference band diffs no longer conflate loudness (schema_version bumped to 2).
- **Tilt-ratio band metrics** (`band_ratios`) drive level- and normalization-independent muddy/harsh/thin diagnostics, replacing meaningless fixed absolute thresholds.
- **Correlation grading** retuned for full commercial mixes (pass ≥ +0.5, warn +0.1–0.5, fail < +0.1) so real mono-loss risk isn't graded as "pass".
- **Detuned pattern** uses absolute deviation so flat mixes can trigger it.
- **Brightness/warmth proxy** is now always authoritative; timbral-model scores are namespaced under `timbral_*` so diagnostics don't break when the perceptual extra is installed.
- **compare** warns when the reference sample rate differs from the mix (per-band diffs are unreliable across rates; resampling deferred to Stage 3).

## Docs

- README Example Output regenerated from a real `analyze` run (dB-rel units, DC Offset, schema_version 2).
- Metric docs, MetricDoc registry entries, and CHANGELOG (unreleased 0.2.0) swept for Stage 2 accuracy.

## Testing

Deterministic pink-noise + mix-like fixtures added; new/expanded tests across audio, loudness, spectrum, perceptual, diagnostics, rules, CLI, and report. Run: `uv run --extra dev pytest -q`

## Known follow-up

`tmp_mixlike_wav` fixture measures `low_mid_minus_mid=10.8 dB` (above the 8.0 muddy threshold), so `muddy_mix` fires on it. Flagged for follow-up rather than retuning provisional thresholds ad hoc.

items.title: Prepare research artifact for review: exp_005 metrics, reproducibility, and dossier cleanup
items.body:
## Summary

This branch is a non-functional polish pass to make the repository review-ready as a research artifact (GRA / graduate-application submission). It reconciles all reported metrics to the canonical `exp_005` evaluation, makes the repo runnable after a fresh clone, adds open-science metadata, and softens overstated framing in the technical dossier. **No training, inference, preprocessing, Grad-CAM, ONNX-export, or model-architecture logic was changed.**

6 commits, grouped by concern:

| Commit | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `ca34a6ed` | Repo polish: LICENSE, CITATION.cff, tracked model artifacts, `.gitignore`/hygiene |
| `909a4d69` | README citation section + frontend documentation (JSDoc) |
| `75b3d436` | Research dossier aligned to `exp_005`; operational framing softened |
| `64fa2080` | Canonical metrics in README, API stats, experiment JSON, results CSV |
| `3d21e10e` | Reproducible plotting + Grad-CAM artifacts (seed=42, plotting scripts, figures) |
| `15bfc3ed` | Landing-page metric display |

### 1. Documentation & reproducibility polish
- Added **`LICENSE`** (MIT) and **`CITATION.cff`** (DOI left commented, pending Zenodo); added a Citation section to `README.md`.
- Pinned `auralis-back/requirements.txt` to the documented training baseline as the full dev/training environment; `requirements.api.txt` remains the lean runtime.
- Added Google-style `Args/Returns/Raises` docstrings to `prepare_dataset.py` and JSDoc to the landing components.
- Hygiene: untracked `.DS_Store`, removed a stray backend `package-lock.json`, removed a stale `helios_v3_final.pth` ignore rule.

### 2. Canonical exp_005 metric alignment
All reported metrics reconciled to the single source of truth (`exp_005`, MC Dropout T=20, seed=42, 353-sample hold-out):

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| MAE (log-SI) | 0.1048 |
| RMSE (log-SI) | 0.1272 |
| R² | 0.8634 |
| MAPE | 6.07% |
| Accuracy proxy (100−MAPE) | 93.93% |

Aligned across `README.md`, `RESEARCH_DOSSIER_MASTER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, API `main.py` (`/api/stats`, `/api/benchmark`), `exp_005_v3pro_augmented.json`, `results_comparison.csv`, and the landing page. Repo-wide scan for the superseded values (`0.1076 / 0.1284 / 0.8608 / 6.22% / 93.78`) returns **0 hits**. The regenerated `results_comparison.csv` independently recomputes to mean |error| = **0.1048** over **353** rows.

### 3. Tracked model artifacts & inference readiness
- The promoted artifacts are now **version-controlled** so the project runs after a fresh clone:
  - `auralis-back/models/best_coronium_v3_pro_augmented.pth` (~833 KB)
  - `auralis-back/models/best_coronium_v3_pro.onnx` (~87 KB, with its `.onnx.data`)
- `.gitignore` updated to allow-list exactly these two while generic `*.pth`/`*.onnx` stay ignored.
- End-to-end inference smoke test passes against the tracked checkpoint (see Testing).

### 4. Research dossier cleanup & softened framing
- Removed stale Git-state metadata (dropped a misleading commit hash/message block).
- Documented the **log-only** target normalization (`log(SI + ε)`); removed a contradictory "Log + Z-Score" active-normalization claim.
- Softened overstated framing to match the project's "academic/technical demo" identity:
  - "Mission-Critical Reliability" → **"High-Activity Regime Robustness"**
  - "Class-X / solar storms" → **"high-activity regime (SI > 2.0)"**
  - "operational / production / validated satellite deployment" → **"evaluated on hold-out data / executed locally / potential future resource-constrained deployment"**
- No forecasting, flare-prediction, geomagnetic-storm, or operational space-weather claims remain.

### 5. Regenerated figures & plotting scripts
- New poster-grade plotting scripts: `plot_architecture_diagram.py`, `plot_gradcam_overlay.py`, `plot_r2_diagnostic.py`.
- Added optional `GRADCAM_SAMPLE` targeting to `explain_model.py` (legacy first-file fallback preserved).
- Regenerated/added figures: architecture diagram, Grad-CAM overlay + max-activity sample, scatter, R² diagnostic.

---

### Testing

Lightweight checks run locally (no retraining):

- ✅ **Python byte-compile** — all `auralis-back/src/` and `scripts/` files compile (no syntax errors).
- ✅ **ONNX graph load** — `best_coronium_v3_pro.onnx` loads via ONNX Runtime; signature `input[batch, 2, 512, 512] → output[batch, 1]`.
- ✅ **End-to-end inference smoke test** — `scripts/test_inference.py` runs against the tracked `.pth` over the 16 sample magnetograms and produces predictions.
- ✅ **Reproducibility** — `evaluate_final.py` now fixes `seed=42` (torch / numpy) so MC-Dropout metrics are deterministic.
- ✅ **Metric consistency scan** — canonical values present on every surface; superseded values return 0 hits repo-wide.
- ⚠️ **Frontend typecheck** — not run (`typescript` not installed in `node_modules`); the three frontend edits are presentational string-literal value changes only.

Not run (heavier / out of scope): full MC-Dropout evaluation, model training, `npm install`/build.

---

### Notes for reviewers
- Functional code is untouched apart from two **additive** reproducibility/tooling changes (`evaluate_final.py` seeding, `explain_model.py` optional sample targeting).
- `main` is unaffected; this branch is documentation, metadata, results data, and figures.

items.title: Release 0.1.3: eleven closed defects
items.body:
Prepares 0.1.3, carrying PRs #72–#77.

**Version moves in lockstep** — `pyproject.toml`, `grapharc.__version__`, `uv.lock`, the README status line, the basics page's `--version` transcript, the serving cookbook's two `/healthz` transcripts, and the tripwire test that forces those page updates. (0.1.0 shipped with pyproject and `__version__` disagreeing, and PyPI is immutable, so the lockstep is the point.) `CHANGELOG.md`'s *Unreleased* section becomes `## 0.1.3`.

## What this release closes

Found by an adversarial sweep across the runtime, planner/policy, session/server and CLI/Slack surfaces, each reproduced before it was filed and re-verified against a live repro before its fix was merged.

**Fail-open, silent — the ones that mattered most**
- **#66** a policy's `resource = "node"` rules were compiled by nobody, so a document denying a node kind still ran it — and the shipped `example.toml` uses exactly that form.
- **#61** repeating `--registry` walked a Slack user past the agent opt-in *and* the forced approval gate.
- **#59** a deny rule naming a tool literally failed open when the name contained fnmatch metacharacters, and `visible()` advertised the tool to the model.
- **#67** fan-out payloads bypassed deep-copy isolation: two parallel workers received the same live object.

**Contract and audit integrity**
- **#68** `invoke`/`stream` silently dropped unknown input keys, running the whole graph on defaults.
- **#70** a Ctrl-C'd sync node left no terminal trace event, and `metrics` then reported zero errors.
- **#63** unreadable input escaped as a traceback in four places that promise an exit-2 document.
- **#62** `plan --approve --json` printed prose ahead of the document, so the output would not parse.

**Server**
- **#65** an unauthenticated non-ASCII token crashed `/live` with a 500 instead of a 401.
- **#69** the `/live` index listed and parsed symlinked traces the reader itself 404s.
- **#64** a NUL byte in a Slack path raised out of `handle_text`, so the bot answered with silence.

## Verification

`pytest` → **1843 passed, 12 deselected** (was 1754 at 0.1.2). `ruff check grapharc tests` → clean. Every fix was additionally confirmed against a live repro — real server for the `/live` fixes, real `grapharc plan --policy` for the node gate, real `Harness.call` for the permission gate.

Still open and deliberately not in this release: #60 (a budget-stopped run reports 0 tokens) and #71 (worst-case iteration under-count for acyclic plans), both of which want design decisions rather than patches.

items.title: fix(stella-observatory): share the self-driving fold and thresholds with stella-core (#1613)
items.body:
## Problem

Since #1548 the delivery loop.s decision logic lives in `stella-core::self_driving`, but `crates/stella-observatory/src/self_driving.rs` kept **private copies** of the run fold and the signal thresholds, written when the only other implementation was shell.

Two Rust copies of the same fold drift — and two already had:

| | `stella-core` | `stella-observatory` |
|---|---|---|
| **NOISY** | `2 * new_findings < n` | `new_findings < n / 2` (integer division) |
| **signal text** | "3 consecutive zero-fix cycles" | "three consecutive zero-fix cycles" |

For `n=5, new=2` the first is `4 < 5` — **true** — and the second is `2 < 2` — **false**. The dashboard and `stella self-driving metrics` reported **different health for the same loop** on every odd cycle count at the boundary. All four signals also carried differently-worded copies of their own explanation, so the two surfaces printed different sentences for the same finding.

A **third** copy of the 900-second staleness default sat in `stella-cli`, under a comment asking a future reader to keep it equal by hand — the same arrangement that let the NOISY threshold drift in the first place.

## Change

`stella-core::self_driving` gains:

- `DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_SECS` — the one copy of `900`.
- `liveness()` → `Live` / `Orphaned` / `Stale`. The two ways a `running` record can be wrong have different causes, so they are named rather than collapsed into a bool.

Core's **own** `fold_runs` now routes through `liveness()`, so this is one implementation and not "one implementation plus an extraction nobody uses". The observatory calls `liveness`, `metrics` and `starved`; `stella-cli` reads the constant.

The observatory keeps its own JSON assembly and its own **tolerant parsing** — `ledger.jsonl` is an open, append-only file that may predate any given field, and a reader that dropped a run because one line came from an older build would be worse than useless. What is shared is the *decision*; what stays local is the *parsing*. `/api/self-driving`'s shape is unchanged, signal order included (STUCK, STARVED, NOISY, FRAGILE, named explicitly rather than left to the fold's emission order).

## The dependency question

The issue flags this as a maintainer call, so stating the reasoning rather than deciding it silently: this adds `stella-core` to a crate that deliberately linked only `stella-home`.

**That rule is about the write path, not the dependency count.** The observatory re-reads artifacts instead of linking the crates that produce them — which is why it opens `store.db` with `rusqlite` rather than linking `stella-store`, whose `Store::open` creates `.stella/` and runs migrations. `stella-core::self_driving` is the opposite shape: pure decision logic over owned data, **no I/O by invariant 2**, with the clock passed in as a parameter. It opens nothing.

The alternative — a new leaf crate holding the fold — would move `CycleRecord`, `Calibration`, `Metrics`, `Signal` and the folds out of `stella-core` and leave it re-exporting them, churning the CLI and its tests for a boundary that invariant 2 already guarantees. **If you would rather have the leaf crate, say so and I will do that instead**; the shared surface is small and the move is mechanical.

The crate README's "exactly one `stella-*` dependency" claim is corrected in the same commit rather than left to rot.

## Witness

`the_page_and_the_terminal_agree_on_the_same_ledger` asserts the two surfaces produce the **same signal list** for a five-cycle / two-finding fixture — the exact boundary the copies disagreed on — and separately that the fixture *really raises* NOISY, so the equality assertion cannot be satisfied by both surfaces staying silent.

Asserting against `stella_core::self_driving::metrics` rather than against the literal `"NOISY"` is the point: a future threshold change now has to move both surfaces or fail here, which is the property the duplicate implementation could never have.

Verified the artisanal way — with core's predicate reverted to the observatory's old integer-division form:

```
thread 'self_driving::tests::the_page_and_the_terminal_agree_on_the_same_ledger' panicked:
the fixture must actually raise the signal under test, or the assertion above is
satisfied by both surfaces staying silent: []
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

Restored: `test result: ok. 1 passed`.

**All 84 pre-existing observatory tests and all 25 core self_driving tests pass unchanged** — the issue's stated constraint. `cargo clippy -p stella-observatory -p stella-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo check -p stella-cli` clean.

## CI note

#1764 has since merged, so `main` is green again.

Closes #1613

## Summary by Sourcery

Align self-driving liveness and signal evaluation across stella-core, stella-observatory, and stella-cli by sharing core decision logic and constants instead of maintaining duplicate implementations.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure the observatory dashboard and `stella self-driving metrics` report the same self-driving signals and NOISY threshold decisions for a given ledger.
- Unify the default staleness timeout for self-driving runs across CLI, core, and observatory to prevent drift.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a reusable liveness classifier in stella-core to distinguish live, orphaned, and stale self-driving runs and reuse it in both core and observatory.
- Refactor observatory’s self-driving metrics to reuse stella-core’s typed metrics, cycle records, and STARVED signal logic while preserving tolerant ledger parsing and stable signal ordering.
- Add tests that assert the dashboard and CLI produce identical self-driving signal codes for the same fixture to guard against future drift.

Documentation:
- Update stella-observatory README to document its dependency on stella-core and clarify the isolation rule as focusing on write paths rather than dependency count.

Tests:
- Add a cross-surface test ensuring the observatory and stella-core metrics agree on emitted signals for the same ledger, including NOISY at the previous boundary case.

3. **`fit()` after `tune()` logs an optimistic-bias warning.** Reusing the identical deterministic CV splits used for param selection makes the reported OOF metrics optimistically biased (documented user-side policy, BLUEPRINT §11.6, previously unenforced at runtime). One `event='fit.post_tune'` warning is now emitted per such fit. Log-only.

items.title: fix(launchd): keep TCC responsible-process chain on /bin/bash for external-volume reads
items.body:
## Problem
On macOS, the scheduled `ai.tokometer.daily` launchd job silently read **zero files** from `/Volumes/workspace` (an external/removable volume): `git_metrics` and `gh_metrics` reported `no repos under /Volumes/workspace`, while `session_logs` (a direct child of `daily.sh`) only caught boot-drive logs. Interactively everything worked (93 repos).

## Root cause
TCC's *responsible-process* chain. The plist ran `daily.sh` via its `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang, and `daily.sh` called `harvest.sh` the same way. The `/usr/bin/env` indirection inserts an **ungranted** binary into the chain, so the python collectors lose the `/bin/bash` Full-Disk/removable-volume grant. It is **not** a missing grant on python (and not the version-pinned Homebrew python the path even resolves to).

## Fix
- `install.sh`: plist `ProgramArguments` → `[/bin/bash, daily.sh]`
- `daily.sh`: invoke `harvest.sh` as `/bin/bash harvest.sh`
- `README`: document the `/bin/bash` Full Disk Access requirement for external scan roots

## Verification
Live on studio-3: `git_metrics` 0 → **93 repos / 287 commits** under the scheduled launchd run; `gh_metrics` 84 PRs; all collectors green.

items.title: Spec-driven VT100/ECMA-48 conformance suite with basis-graded metrics (#13)
items.body:
## What this is

Workstream 1 of the terminal test program (epic #14): the **data core** of a fully-automated, spec-derived VT100/ECMA-48 conformance suite for the Apple IIe terminal firmware. Closes #13.

Cases are declarative JSON authored **from the spec** (ECMA-48 / VT100-UG / xterm ctlseqs), decoupled from the firmware, and graded **entirely by machine** — no human review, no reference emulator. Every case is checked against headless MAME through three oracle channels:

- **Video-RAM probe** — the 80-column glyph plane + inverse-attribute plane.
- **State-variable probe** — firmware globals (cursor, attr, scroll region, DEC mode flags) read by symbol address from the linker label file.
- **Wire read-back** — the terminal's own replies (DSR/CPR, DA).

## Framework (`client/conformance/`)

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `model.py` | `Case`/`Screen` model, input mini-decoder, per-key expectation checker, strict corpus loader/validator |
| `runner.py` | corpus × target → classify (esctest `knownBug` xfail model) → metric suite + `build/conformance.json` |
| `target_mame.py` / `target_base.py` / `target_fake.py` / `transport.py` | render-target interface, MAME boot + windowed-lossless sender + probes, offline fake |
| `probes/conformance_probe.lua` | glyph plane, inverse plane, and state vars |
| `selftest.py` | offline (no-MAME) guard for the machinery — CI-suitable |
| `corpus/*.json` | 186 cases across 15 categories |

## Honest compliance metrics (the key design decision)

A single `status=supported` label was conflating four different meanings, so the headline percentage moved when a case was *relabelled* rather than when *behaviour* changed. This PR separates a case's **`status`** (drives pass/fail) from an orthogonal **`basis`** (drives how a pass is counted):

| `basis` | A pass proves… |
|---------|----------------|
| `spec` | strict VT100/ECMA-48 behaviour a reference terminal would also produce |
| `profile` | a visible, documented Apple IIe degradation (DEC line-draw → ASCII fold) |
| `tolerance` | an unimplemented sequence absorbed as an observable no-op (colour/bold; SO/SI) |
| `degenerate` | passes only because a default coincides with the tested direction |
| `unobservable` | effect not probeable (DECTCEM) → scored **SKIP**, never counted |

Reported metrics: **behavioural compatibility** (`(PASS+UPASS)/scored`, *relabel-invariant* headline), **spec conformance**, **profile conformance**, completeness, correctness. UNEXPECTED PASS no longer auto-promotes — it requires a discriminating companion test first.

## Baseline vs MAME

```
151 PASS · 0 REGRESSION · 33 XFAIL · 2 SKIP · 0 ERROR   (exit 0)
behavioral compat 82.1%   spec 79.5%   profile 80.5%   correctness 100%
```

## Firmware / infra hooks (no behavioural change)

- **Makefile** — emit `build/vt100.lbl` (`ld65 -Ln`) for the state probe.
- **screen80.c / vt100.c** — un-static cursor/attr/scroll/mode state vars so the probe can read them by symbol (comments cite #13).
- **bench.py** — `Terminal.peek()` for non-destructive wire read-back.

## Docs

- New **docs/CONFORMANCE.md** — standards map, external-suite survey (vttest/esctest2), probe methodology, the `basis` taxonomy, metric definitions, and the promotion workflow.
- **docs/TESTING.md** / **README.md** — updated for the runner and the offline selftest.

## How to run

```bash
python client/conformance/selftest.py            # offline machinery guard (no MAME)
python client/conformance/runner.py --target mame # full grade against headless MAME
python client/conformance/runner.py --target mame --strict  # also fail on UNEXPECTED PASS
```

## Deferred (as planned)

- pyte differential oracle (#18); real-world app scenarios (#17); optional `SerialTarget`. The corpus **records** the tracked gaps (#2/#3/#8–#12) as XFAIL; it does not fix them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

items.title: docs: fix references to configuration keys that do not exist
items.body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

No issue filed; this is a docs cleanup found by sweeping every tracked markdown file for `spark.comet.*` keys and validating them against `CometConf.scala`.

## Rationale for this change

Several docs reference configuration keys that do not exist. A user copying these into a `spark-submit` command gets a silently ignored setting, which is worse than an error because the doc implies the setting took effect.

The largest group is the expression opt-in prefix. The real namespace is `spark.comet.expression.*` (`COMET_EXPR_CONFIG_PREFIX` in `CometConf.scala`), but the contributor guide, the versioning policy, and two expression-audit pages all use `spark.comet.expr.*`. Those same places also describe a global `allowIncompatible` key, which has never existed: the opt-in is always per-expression or per-operator.

While verifying the remaining `spark.comet.expression.<Name>.*` references against the serde registry, three of them turned out to name something that is not a valid expression config, and the surrounding prose was stale in the same way, so those claims were corrected too.

## What changes are included in this PR?

Wrong config prefix, corrected to `spark.comet.expression.*`:

- `contributor-guide/adding_a_new_expression.md` (3 references, plus removal of the nonexistent global key from the `Incompatible` description)
- `about/versioning_policy.md`
- `.claude/skills/audit-comet-expression/SKILL.md`
- `contributor-guide/benchmarking_macos.md`, which passed `spark.comet.expression.allowIncompatible=true`

Explode is gated at the operator level, not the expression level, so `expression-audits/generator_funcs.md` now points at `spark.comet.operator.GenerateExec.allowIncompatible`.

Config keys naming an expression that does not exist:

- `spark.comet.expression.regexp.allowIncompatible` (`predicate_funcs.md`, `string_funcs.md`). There is no `regexp` expression; the real keys are `RLike` and `RegExpReplace`.
- `spark.comet.expression.Upper.allowIncompatible` / `Lower.allowIncompatible` (`string_funcs.md`). Case conversion overrides the opt-in key via `nativeOptInConfigKeyOverride`, so the key is `spark.comet.caseConversion.enabled`.

Correcting those four also meant correcting the claims around them, which predate the codegen dispatcher: `rlike`, `regexp_replace`, `upper` and `lower` are `Compatible` by default now, with the native regexp / case-mapping path opt-in, not "unconditionally `Incompatible`". The `regexp_replace` entry also cited `RegExp.isSupportedPattern`, a symbol that no longer exists.

Renamed or never-registered keys:

- `spark.comet.metrics.detailed` (`user-guide/latest/metrics.md`) was never registered; those metrics are always reported
- `spark.comet.memoryPool.fraction` to `spark.comet.exec.memoryPool.fraction` (`benchmark-results/tpc-ds.md`, `tpc-h.md`)
- `spark.comet.shuffle.write.buffer.size` to `spark.comet.shuffle.native.writeBufferSize` (`native_shuffle.md`)
- `spark.comet.exec.shuffle.enableFastEncoding` and `spark.comet.exec.shuffle.fallbackToColumnar`, both removed, dropped from `benchmarking_macos.md`
- `spark.comet.exec.all.enabled`, removed, dropped from `benchmarking_spark_sql_perf.md` and `benchmarks/README.md`
- `spark.comet.columnar.shuffle.enabled` to `spark.comet.shuffle.mode=jvm` (`benchmarking_spark_sql_perf.md`)
- `spark.comet.cast.allowIncompatible` to `spark.comet.expression.Cast.allowIncompatible` (`benchmarks/README.md`)

Deliberately left alone: `docs/source/changelog/*`, which records historical PR titles mentioning since-removed keys, the `docs/comet-0.1x/` version archives, and placeholder forms such as `spark.comet.exec.<yourOperator>.enabled`.

## How are these changes tested?

Docs only, no code changes. Verified by extracting every `spark.comet.*` token from all tracked `.md` and `.rst` files and diffing that set against the keys registered in `CometConf.scala`, expanded for the dynamic `expression.<Name>.*`, `operator.<Name>.*` and `exec.<name>.enabled` patterns. Every expression name appearing in a config key was checked against the `classOf[...]` entries in `QueryPlanSerde.scala`, and each corrected claim was read back against the relevant serde. After the change the only unmatched keys are the three changelog entries noted above. `prettier` reports no formatting changes.

items.title: Add board_metrics task, executive domain, and group tasks by domain
items.body:
Builds `board_metrics`, the last `PLANNED` roadmap item, opens the **executive operations** domain, and resolves the deferred task-grouping decision. After this, the engineering and executive domains are both built out.

## What it does
Monthly, after month-end close, assembles the board metrics pack — financials from **NetSuite**, growth and product metrics from **Looker**, and OKR progress from **Jira** — measures it against the executive standard, compares to last month, writes a board-ready document, and posts the summary + board-attention pointer to a private leadership channel.

OKRs are incorporated as the framing for the **strategic-progress** section (objectives, KRs with target/actual/health/trend, quarter-to-date), with a separate hard-numbers metrics section. Not OKRs-all-the-way-down: financial/operational metrics are reported as metrics, and only contextualized against KR targets where it makes sense.

## Changes
- **Regroup (commit 1):** tasks moved from flat `tasks/<task>/` to `tasks/<domain>/<task>/`, mirroring `standards/`. The four engineering tasks now live under `tasks/engineering/`, internal path references rewritten. Output stays flat at `output/<task>/`; `tasks/_task_template/` stays at the `tasks/` root. README layout, CONTRIBUTING, the `add_task`/`add_domain` commands, and PROJECT_CONTEXT all updated; the grouping decision is recorded as resolved. Also fixes `.gitignore` (`tasks/*/config.md` → `tasks/**/config.md`) — the old pattern no longer protected local configs under the nested layout.
- **Standard (commit 2):** `standards/executive/board_metrics.md` — metric catalog, monthly cadence with quarter-to-date OKRs, KR health by pace-to-target (achieved / on track / at risk / off track / not started), month-over-month trend, a needs-board-attention escalation lens, and Looker/NetSuite/Jira query patterns. Reuses `shared/style.md`.
- **Task (commit 3):** `tasks/executive/board_metrics/` (task, pack template, README, config.example), plus the same-commit three-place update: README catalog, `CHANGELOG.md` 2.0.0, PROJECT_CONTEXT status, and `connectors.md`.

## Design notes
- **Trend** is stateless-first: this month from source, last month read from the prior run's saved `output/.../latest.md`, degrading to "no prior month to compare" on a first run.
- First task to read a **BI layer and a finance system**, and the first that does **not** use the shared `config/config.md` — its values (look ids, NetSuite report refs, OKR project/fields, targets, fiscal start, runway floor, board channel) live in the task's own gitignored `config.md`.
- `2.0.0` because the task tree structure changed.

## Verify
- All five catalog rows match the five tasks in the tree; no flat-layout references survive; no `_planned_` rows remain; no `{{...}}` in standards or task logic; `config/` staging guard clean; local `config.md` ignored at every nesting level.
- **Build-surface caveat:** artifacts ready to install and test in Cowork, not verified-working.
- **Connector gap (most likely first-run blocker):** Looker and NetSuite are not in the default connector set and must be added in Cowork (possibly custom/MCP) before the task runs. Both are read-only here.

items.title: fix(metrics): publish savings against the targeted-read baseline
items.body:
## Stack

Stack-Id: `r2-truth-in-claims`
Base: `main`
Position: 1/3

1. `fix/r2-savings-targeted-read-baseline` -> this PR
2. `docs/r2-cross-tool-baseline-semantics` -> upstack
3. `refactor/r2-required-file-completeness-rate` -> upstack

Depends on: (none - root)

Milestone R2 (truth-in-claims correction), `.docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` §6 Section A.

## What changes

Two published claims are corrected. Nothing about how any number is computed changes, and no artifact is deleted.

**1. The savings headline re-points at the targeted-read baseline.** `archex metrics summary` has always reported two labeled savings numbers, but the published headline pointed at the full-file-paste figure. That baseline models pasting every returned file in full, which is not a strategy any agent uses, and it runs an order of magnitude above the honest number. On a representative single-`query` ledger row from this repository the two read 90.1% (vs full-file paste) against 14.9% (vs targeted read). README and `docs/LOCAL_METRICS.md` now name `savings_pct_vs_targeted_read` as the figure to quote and demote the full-file number to a secondary compression measure.

The same change records a limitation that was previously invisible in the published text: `record_query_usage` populates the targeted-read baseline from returned chunk line spans, but `record_scout_usage` does not pass one at all, and the summary's `COALESCE(..., 0)` renders a scout-only ledger as `Savings vs targeted: 0.0%`. That is an absent baseline, not a measured zero, and both docs now say so.

**2. The self-repo row is withdrawn from every quoted cross-tool figure.** archex's own generic keywords (`index`, `query`, `config`) match across its entire source, so the naive grep/read baseline reads a median of 32.5 units per self-repo task against 3.0 on the two external corpora. The published range was dominated by that keyword density rather than by archex. The two `self` rows are dropped from the cross-tool table in `docs/LOCAL_METRICS.md` and the README range is restated as 95.4%–97.2% over the external corpora, with the naive grep/read agent named as the baseline in the same sentence.

`benchmarks/cross-tool-efficiency/cross-tool-comparison.json` is untouched — all 16 self-repo comparisons remain in the artifact; only the published figures change.

## Verification

```text
$ grep -rn "downstream_success_rate\|445×\|673×\|99\.78\|99\.64" README.md docs
(no output)

$ uv run ruff check .
All checks passed!

$ uv run ruff format --check .
499 files already formatted
```

Gate check for the milestone, run before the headline was re-pointed: an isolated-`HOME` live run (`ARCHEX_USAGE_METRICS=on uv run archex query …`) wrote one `usage_events` row with `tokens_targeted_read=4337`, `tokens_saved_vs_targeted_read=648`, `savings_pct_vs_targeted_read=14.94` against `savings_pct=90.14`. The field is populated on the live ledger write path.

Every figure quoted here was recomputed directly from the checked-in artifact: 52 comparable tasks (self 16, external-comprehension 16, external-localization 20); self median 32.5 units read per task, external median 3.0.

## Risks

Docs-only. Rollback is a revert; no data is destroyed and no code path changes.

---

## Review round 1 — corrections applied

- **"Withdrawn from every quoted figure" was false.** `CHANGELOG.md`'s shipped `0.15.0` entry still quotes the self-inclusive 95.4%–99.8% range and points at `docs/LOCAL_METRICS.md` for it. Rewriting a released entry would breach the no-deletion constraint, so the claim is narrowed to *currently published* figures and both docs record that the `0.15.0` range is superseded.
- **The CLI still led with the demoted number.** `archex metrics summary` printed savings-vs-full-file first and labelled neither line, while the docs told readers to quote the targeted-read figure. The two lines are reordered and labelled `(headline, vs realistic targeted read)` and `(compression, vs full-file paste)`; values and baselines are unchanged and the CLI test pins the order. Reordering and labelling output is inside R2's constraint — it changes how a number is published, not how it is computed.
- **`docs/WHY_ARCHEX.md` headlined 83–99% "Savings" under "Measured, Not Claimed".** Those four figures are illustrative sketches against a whole-file read — the baseline R2 demotes. Each now names its baseline in the same line, and the section says it illustrates rather than measures.

Re-verified after the fixes: `uv run pytest -q` 4473 passed, coverage 91.55%; ruff and pyright clean; CI green.

items.title: docs: fix drift in SECURITY, CONTRIBUTING, and the sourceEpochUnixMs API comment
items.body:
Fixes documentation that drifted out of sync with the code.

## Verified against the code and fixed

- **SECURITY.md — supported versions.** The table listed `0.1.x`; the current release is `v0.7.0`. Updated to `0.7.x: Yes`, `< 0.7.0: No`.
- **SECURITY.md — Secret RBAC.** It claimed `secrets:get;list;watch`. Both controllers actually declare `+kubebuilder:rbac:groups="",resources=secrets,verbs=get` (an uncached, per-request read), and the generated `config/rbac/role.yaml` grants `secrets: [get]` only. Corrected to `secrets:get`.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md — Go version.** Prerequisite said `Go 1.25+`; `go.mod` requires `go 1.26.5`. Updated to `Go 1.26.5+`.
- **`sourceEpochUnixMs` field comment.** It said `0` means the source epoch "could not be parsed (treated as unknown, not stale)". That is no longer true: the producer skips satellites whose epoch it cannot parse (surfaced via the `SourceEpochRejected` condition) instead of emitting a `0`, and the consumer now treats a `0` epoch as the 1970 instant subject to the normal staleness bound (the CHANGELOG's "0 no longer bypasses the freshness gate" change). Corrected the field doc and regenerated the four CRD copies (`config/crd`, `dist/chart`, `bundle`, `nephio`) and `docs/api-reference.md`. The `bundle-verify-sync` / `nephio-verify-sync` drift gates pass.

## Verified but intentionally not changed

- The README Grafana section already reads **"9 custom metrics"**, not "6" — the reported `all 6` text does not exist, so no change was needed.
- `docs/whitepaper/*` carries the same `Go 1.25` / `secrets:get;list;watch` drift, but that file is skip-worktree-pinned (co-founder content) and is left untouched here.

Docs + generated-CRD only; no controller logic changed.

items.title: Audit: fix max-drawdown baseline, FF missing-value sentinels, single-bucket guard
items.body:
Full-repo audit driven by executing the pipeline against a fresh data pull
rather than reading it. Every number in the README's results section
reproduced exactly. Three genuine bugs found; none changed a reported
statistic, which is why all three survived two prior reviews.

- metrics.max_drawdown seeded its running peak at the first observed equity
  value instead of the starting capital, so a series already under water at
  month 1 reported 0% drawdown until it exceeded its own opening point.
  max_drawdown([-0.50, +1.00]) returned 0.0 instead of -0.50. quantstats --
  this project's declared independent cross-check -- prepends the baseline,
  so the two would have silently disagreed on any series whose deepest trough
  precedes its first new high. Dormant here only by luck: the in-sample curve
  does open down (-5.79%, curve 0.9421) but recovers above 1.0 well before the
  2008-09 trough that sets the reported -41.11%.

- data._parse_ff_monthly_text masked only -99.0 as Ken French's missing-data
  sentinel. The files' header reads "Missing data are indicated by -99.99 or
  -999" -- neither was caught, so a missing month would have become a -99.99%
  or -999% factor return. The unit test had baked in the same wrong sentinel
  (-99.00, a code the files never emit) and so tested nothing. Verified latent:
  all three live factor files re-parsed with zero sentinel rows.

- signal.assign_buckets with n_buckets=1 labelled the entire cross-section -1
  (top and bottom masks both cover everything; the bottom mask wins), leaving
  the long-only engine holding nothing and reporting flat 0% months with no
  error. Now rejected explicitly.

Verified sound, no change needed: the engine is lookahead-free under two
adversarial probes on the real panel -- truncating data at 2015-12-31
reproduces every prior month bit-for-bit, and scaling all prices after
2015-12-31 by 3x leaves earlier months byte-identical. No entry open equals
the close it was ranked on (0/318). Weight, turnover, and cost invariants hold.

Tooling: CI now runs black --check (configured and claimed but never
enforced); [tool.black] gained an extend-exclude mirroring ruff's, since
black checks .ipynb only when its optional [jupyter] extra is installed --
a gate that passed or failed on dependency luck. pytest moved to
requirements-dev.txt, matching that file's own stated split.

Docs: README now discloses that the last in-sample holding month exits at the
2018-01-02 open (open-to-open convention); marking it to the 2017-12-29 close
instead moves the IS Sharpe 0.3548 -> 0.3536 and nothing else at 4 decimals.
Test count corrected 80 -> 91. ROADMAP addendum #3 records the audit.

91/91 tests pass; ruff and black clean; README results re-reproduced unchanged.

items.title: [codex] Fix mobile nav overflow
items.body:
## Summary
- Fix the mobile horizontal overflow by compacting the phone nav and making the GitHub CTA icon-only below 600px while preserving its accessible label.
- Add a Playwright mobile overflow regression test covering 375px, 393px, and 430px viewports.
- Document the new `pnpm test:mobile` guardrail in the README and ignore Playwright report artifacts.

## Root cause
After the main nav links were hidden on mobile, the remaining brand + GitHub + booking CTAs still required more width than common phone viewports. That widened the document and allowed Safari to pan sideways, matching the screenshots.

## Validation
- Red test reproduced the bug before the CSS fix: `pnpm test:mobile` failed with page overflow of 133px at 375px, 115px at 393px, and 78px at 430px.
- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm test:mobile`
- Visual sanity screenshots at 393px and 1440px, with browser metrics confirming `scrollWidth === clientWidth`.

items.title: Restructure into an installable, tested ECA-LDNet package
items.body:
## Summary

This PR restructures the project from a flat collection of notebooks, checkpoints, and result artifacts into a **proper, installable, and tested research-software repository**, and extracts the model code out of the notebooks into an importable Python package — without changing the model itself or any reported results.

## What changed

### New `eca_ldnet/` package (faithful extraction from the notebooks)
- `layers.py` — `ECABlock`, `PixelAttention`, `PhysicsCorrectionLayer` (+ `CUSTOM_OBJECTS`)
- `blocks.py` — depthwise-separable conv, residual, encoder/decoder blocks
- `model.py` — `build_eca_ldnet()` (reproduces the exact **1,481,871-param** model) and `load_pretrained()`
- `losses.py` — Charbonnier / SSIM / edge / FFT / VGG-perceptual losses + PSNR/SSIM/MAE metrics
- `data.py` — dataset discovery, preprocessing, and the `tf.data` pipeline
- `callbacks.py` — warmup-cosine LR schedule + CSV logging
- `train.py` / `evaluate.py` / `inference.py` — command-line entry points

### Tests (`tests/`, pytest)
Parameter count (1,481,871), I/O shapes, output range, presence of dual-attention + physics modules, save/load round-trip, and loss/metric correctness. **All 9 tests pass locally.** They skip gracefully if TensorFlow is absent, and run on CI.

### Packaging & docs
`README.md` (architecture, benchmark tables, usage), `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml` (with `eca-ldnet-train/eval/dehaze` console scripts), `LICENSE` (MIT), `CITATION.cff`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, and a GitHub Actions CI workflow.

### Tidy layout
`notebooks/`, `checkpoints/`, `results/`, `docs/` — all existing artifacts preserved (moved via `git mv`, history intact).

## Fix included
The released `.keras` checkpoints require **Keras ≥ 3.9** to deserialize; the Keras 3.0.x bundled with TensorFlow 2.16 fails with `Unrecognized keyword arguments passed to Dense: {'quantization_config': None}`. This is now pinned in `requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml` and documented. Verified both stage-5 checkpoints load and run inference end-to-end.

## Verification
- `pytest -q` → 9 passed
- All package modules import cleanly
- `checkpoints/stage5_final_ema_model.keras` and `stage5_best.keras` load (1,481,871 params) and produce valid `[0,1]` output

No model architecture, weights, or reported metrics were modified.

items.title: E03: implement the TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline
items.body:
## Summary

Implements the TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline for T-003 / FR-002 / AC-002 as the
scope-freeze checkpoint: the first complete train → save → reload → measure path.

- `src/intentguard/metrics.py` — pure versioned metrics, `METRIC_VERSION = 1`, `zero_division=0`, zero-support classes reported rather than dropped.
- `src/intentguard/artifacts.py` — immutable bundle: content-derived `run_id`, SHA-256 manifest per file, staged atomic publish, refuse-to-overwrite. Imports no ML framework, so loading cannot fit.
- `src/intentguard/baseline.py` — TF-IDF + logistic regression from stock scikit-learn estimators, ten explicitly frozen hyperparameters.
- `scripts/train_baseline.py` — orchestration wired to `make baseline`.
- `configs/default.toml`, `src/intentguard/config.py` — the typed `[baseline]` contract.

## Measured results

Test split, computed from the **reloaded** artifact (`evaluated_from: reloaded_artifact`), read exactly once:

- `run_id`: `intentguard-baseline-1fb62b1bb463-059ee4b12214`
- Accuracy: `0.8652597402597403`
- Macro-F1: `0.8654495069109515`
- Weighted-F1: `0.8654495069109515`
- Examples: `3,080` across `77` classes, support `40` per class
- Dataset: `PolyAI/banking77@1fb62b1bb4635df59a8e1b2f2bc5e0643b2856c8`
- Split fingerprints: train `faa6e54113411eb78729549d8a2834230af9402830a00e67129537a3be337739`; validation `69b9e8dce8ea810aac5bc8e0ed5f98dc2b32aea3ae2e9f74f27c6bdf8c753104`; test `efdbdac3186d8ea78af3b64c69f82e09a5435ea323571c791f2464a095cc6958`
- Label-map hash: `0a3f622029033ef1cfe378833a431fc243d7c9d856b50717c479f95c0b8ca5d2`
- Test example ID hash: `6e741100846e0831b065da5317d11ca36ff2252c7daaa96d39ea69f714171d81`
- Report: `reports/baseline/<run_id>/metrics.json` (`metric_version: 1`, `schema_version: 1`, seed `42`)

Macro-F1 equals weighted-F1 because the canonical test split has uniform support of exactly 40 examples per class, which makes the two averages mathematically identical — not a defect. Because this split alone cannot detect a macro/weighted swap, the regression fixture in `tests/fixtures/metric_regression.json` is deliberately imbalanced with three distinct exact rationals (accuracy `5/7`, macro-F1 `85/126`, weighted-F1 `107/147`).

Validation macro-F1 measured `0.8432895814916537`. It informed the `class_weight="balanced"` choice and must not be read as a headline result.

## Leakage control

Structural, not procedural: hyperparameters were frozen before any test read, the TF-IDF
vocabulary is fitted on train text only, and `prepared.test` is first touched at
`scripts/train_baseline.py:255` — after the artifact is sealed and reloaded. The in-memory
pipeline is deliberately not reused. Verified independently: the vocabulary is exactly the
21,450 train features, a strict subset, with 0 of 3,486 test-only features present.

## Validation

- `uv run --locked ruff check .` — Passed
- `uv run --locked mypy src scripts tests` — Passed, no issues in 23 source files
- `uv run --locked python scripts/validate_foundation.py` — Passed, 10/10
- `make lint` — Passed (exit 0)
- `make test` — Passed, `138 passed`
- `uv run --locked pytest -q -W error` — Passed, `138 passed` with warnings fatal
- `make baseline` — exit 0; second run reused the bundle with byte-identical metrics
- `git diff --check` — Passed

Coverage 93% (`metrics.py` 100%, `baseline.py` 95%, `artifacts.py` 92%); every uncovered line is a defensive `raise` guard.

Independent probes beyond the test suite: the reported metrics were recomputed from the
on-disk artifact and match bit-for-bit; the D3 fixture was hand-derived from confusion counts
with exact rational arithmetic; a deliberate macro/weighted swap in `metrics.py` made the
fixture fail, confirming it is load-bearing; a refused overwrite left the original bundle
byte-identical; a single flipped byte in the payload was detected on load, and the
`make baseline` reuse path refuses a tampered bundle (exit 2) rather than reporting from it;
reload parity showed a maximum probability difference of exactly `0.0`.

## Divergences

Three deliberate departures a reviewer should confirm rather than assume:

**D1 — `make baseline` writes test metrics.** `REQUIREMENTS.md` AC-002 requires the measured
baseline test result, while `ARCHITECTURE.md:51` implies evaluation writes it. Per the
repository's precedence order, `REQUIREMENTS.md` outranks `ARCHITECTURE.md`, so the baseline
command produces the measurement. This is safe only because leakage control is structural, as
described above. `ARCHITECTURE.md` is deliberately left unchanged.

**D5 — content-derived `run_id` instead of a timestamped directory.** `ARCHITECTURE.md:99`
describes a timestamped artifact directory. The `run_id` is instead derived from the dataset
revision and a hash of the configuration, so an identical run always names the same bundle and
artifact identity stays reproducible. The creation timestamp is recorded inside
`provenance.json`, where it cannot make identity irreproducible.

**D8 — two Gate-A validator rules relaxed.** Both asserted that no generated output *exists*
under `artifacts/` and `reports/`, which made a *successful* `make baseline` fail `make lint`;
one also crashed with `UnicodeDecodeError` when the placeholder scan read the binary
`model.joblib`. Both now assert the real repository contract — generated output must never be
**tracked** — via a `git ls-files` check that degrades safely when no repository exists. The
duplicate assertion in `tests/contract/test_repository_contract.py` was updated in lock-step and
a positive `test_generated_output_is_never_tracked` was added.

## Limitations

- CI has never run against this code; this PR is its first exposure to GitHub Actions.
- The figures above are single-environment CPU measurements on scikit-learn 1.9.0 / NumPy 2.4.6 / Python 3.11.15 with joblib 1.5.3. Exact reproduction on other releases or platforms is not promised.
- `make baseline` reuses an existing bundle when configuration and dataset revision are unchanged. Correct given the content-derived ID, but it means the command does not re-fit unless one of those changes.
- Strict MVP remains unmet: E04–E08 are unimplemented. No transformer artifact, threshold, calibration, selective-prediction, latency, or serving evidence exists yet.

## Review findings repaired

Ten reviewer comments were raised on `4a74155`; **six were confirmed by probe and none
was refuted**, and all six are fixed in `36f8d31`. Each fix is pinned by a test proven
to fail without it (verified by reverting each fix and confirming the pinning tests
fail, then restoring the file and checking it byte-identical).

| # | Finding | Fix | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Run identity omitted `seed` and `validation_fraction`, so a changed seed silently reused the stale bundle — and the report attached the current config's provenance to the old model | `_run_identity_payload` now covers `seed`, `validation_fraction`, and the split fingerprints; `validation_fraction` recorded in provenance so the ID stays recomputable from the bundle | `tests/unit/test_run_identity.py` — 7 tests, incl. one asserting the payload's field set |
| F2 | `fit_pipeline` coerced float and boolean labels (`0.9` became label `0`); `metrics.py` already rejected them, so the two modules disagreed and the stricter one was not the one that trained | `metrics._label_array` promoted to public `label_id_array` and reused by `fit_pipeline`, making it the single definition of the contract; `MetricError` re-raised as `BaselineError` | 6 tests in `tests/unit/test_baseline.py` |
| F3 | `build_pipeline` docstring claimed no hyperparameter was left to a library default; 25 estimator params are at defaults | Narrowed to the ten *selected* hyperparameters, pointing at recorded dependency versions as what makes a result reproducible; same correction in `reports/README.md` | documentation only |
| F4 | Manifest `payload_files` entries unvalidated, so a non-string entry escaped as an unrelated `TypeError` from path joining | Entries validated as non-empty strings present in `files`, raising `ArtifactError` | 4 parametrized cases in `tests/unit/test_artifacts.py` |
| F5 | Held-out token diagnostic tokenised with `str.split()`, reporting terms the vectorizer never offered the model | New `baseline.analyzer()` exposes the vectorizer's own analyzer; the diagnostic uses it | `test_analyzer_matches_the_fitted_vocabulary` |
| F6 | `_positive_float` accepted `nan`/`inf` (`nan <= 0.0` is false, `inf` is positive); label-coverage message said "exactly once each"; `reports/README.md` said `E03` for `U03` | `math.isfinite` required; message corrected to "at least once"; `U03` fixed | 2 cases in `tests/unit/test_config.py` |

`_fraction` was checked and deliberately left alone: `0.0 < nan < 1.0` is already false.

Declined Sourcery's `ProvenanceSpec`/`Manifest` refactor — behavior-neutral, and
`rules/engineering-and-validation.md` forbids unrelated refactoring.

### The run_id changed; the model did not

Widening the identity input means `make baseline` now produces
`intentguard-baseline-1fb62b1bb463-059ee4b12214`, superseding
`intentguard-baseline-1fb62b1bb463-e9a2b14657e6`. **All three test metrics are
byte-identical across the two runs** — accuracy `0.8652597402597403`, macro-F1
`0.8654495069109515`, weighted-F1 `0.8654495069109515` — which is the evidence that the
repair changed identity rather than the fitted model. The Measured results above are
therefore unchanged and now name the ID this branch actually produces. The new ID was
verified recomputable from `config.json` + `provenance.json` alone, and a second
`make baseline` reported `reused_existing_artifact: true`.

### The F5 diagnostic count moved 882 to 2158

Expected, not a regression. The analyzer emits bigrams and `str.split()` cannot:
**2028 of the 2158 are bigrams**, and zero analyzer terms drawn from *training* text
fall outside the fitted vocabulary — which is the property
`test_analyzer_matches_the_fitted_vocabulary` pins.

### Three figures above are superseded by this commit

- `make test` now reports **157 passed**, not `138`. The `138` figure remains accurate
  for `4a74155`, which is what CI measured on that commit.
- `mypy` now covers **24 source files**, not `23` — `tests/unit/test_run_identity.py` is new.
- The Leakage control section's `scripts/train_baseline.py:255` is now **line 285**. The
  ordering it describes is unchanged: the test split is still first touched only after
  the artifact is sealed and reloaded.

Re-executed locally on CPU before pushing: `make lint` exit 0 (ruff clean, mypy clean,
foundation 10/10), `make test` exit 0 with 157 passed, `make baseline` exit 0. CI had not
yet run against `36f8d31` when this body was written.

Closes #6

Implements #18, #19, #20

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline training pipeline with immutable artifacts, versioned metrics, and configuration-driven hyperparameters, wired to `make baseline` and covered by regression and contract tests.

New Features:
- Add a configuration-backed TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline pipeline and CLI script that trains, persists, reloads, and evaluates the BANKING77 baseline.
- Introduce an immutable, checksum-verified artifact bundle format with content-derived run IDs for storing baseline models and metadata.
- Define a pure, versioned classification metrics module and JSON payload schema for baseline evaluation reports.

Enhancements:
- Extend foundation configuration to include generated output roots and a typed baseline hyperparameter section with strict validation.
- Update repository and foundation validators, Makefile, and README contracts so generated artifacts and reports may exist on disk but must remain untracked in Git.

Build:
- Wire the `baseline` Make target to the new `scripts/train_baseline.py` command and add a joblib dependency for model persistence.

Tests:
- Add unit tests for configuration validation of baseline hyperparameters and paths, artifact bundle behavior, baseline pipeline determinism and structure, and metric semantics.
- Introduce a metric regression fixture and tests that lock aggregate and per-class metrics, ensuring future changes are versioned and deliberate.
- Add repository-contract tests that enforce generated output roots and Makefile command wiring for the baseline lifecycle.
