items.title: Add settlement volume totals FIX
items.body:
================================================================================
PULL REQUEST
================================================================================

Repository   : Mitch5000/AnchorNet-Backend
Base branch  : main
Head branch  : fix/metrics-settled-totals
Commit       : 5cc1583
Type         : Feature / enhancement (additive, backward compatible)
Files changed: 6 modified, 0 created, 0 deleted
Diff         : +374 / -6


================================================================================
TITLE
================================================================================

Add totalSettledAmount and totalFeesCollected to the metrics snapshot


================================================================================
DESCRIPTION
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

GET /api/v1/metrics reported settlements and pendingSettlements as counts and
totalLiquidity as a pool-wide sum, but never summed settlement amount or fee.
An operator could see HOW MANY settlements existed, but not HOW MUCH value had
been settled or how much protocol fee revenue had been earned. Getting those
numbers meant paging through GET /api/v1/settlements and summing client-side.

This PR adds two fields to the metrics snapshot, both computed from executed
settlements only:

  totalSettledAmount  - sum of `amount` over executed settlements
  totalFeesCollected  - sum of `fee` over executed settlements

The change is purely additive. Every pre-existing field keeps its exact name,
type and meaning, so existing consumers are unaffected.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Problem
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In src/routes/metrics.ts, snapshot() pulled from three sources but only ever
produced counts of settlements:

    settlements: settlements.length,
    pendingSettlements: settlements.filter((s) => s.status === "pending").length,

The `amount` and `fee` fields carried by every settlement were never aggregated.

totalLiquidity does sum value, but it sums POOL BALANCES: supply currently
parked in the network. That is a different question from how much value has
actually flowed THROUGH the network, and it does not move when a settlement
executes against already-counted liquidity. There was no field answering
"what has this network settled, and what did we earn on it?"


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Why executed-only
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The settlement lifecycle in src/models/settlement.ts mirrors the on-chain
contract, and only one of the three states represents value that actually moved:

    STATUS      MEANING                                    VALUE MOVED?
    ---------   ----------------------------------------   ------------
    pending     Liquidity reserved, still cancellable      No
    executed    Liquidity permanently consumed             Yes
    cancelled   Reservation released                       No

Counting pending settlements would inflate the totals with value that may never
settle (a pending settlement can still be cancelled). Counting cancelled ones
would report fees on revenue that was never earned. "Collected" has to mean
collected, so both are excluded.

This matches the accounting already inside SettlementService, where execute()
moves an amount out of `reserved` and into `consumed`, while cancel() releases
the reservation without ever touching `consumed`.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Changes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

src/routes/metrics.ts  (core fix)

Filter once to executed settlements, then reduce over amount and fee:

    // Value settled and fees earned count only executed settlements: a
    // `pending` settlement has reserved liquidity but may still be cancelled,
    // and a `cancelled` one released it without ever moving value.
    const executed = settlements.filter((s) => s.status === "executed");

    return {
      ...                                                  // existing fields untouched
      totalSettledAmount: executed.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.amount, 0),
      totalFeesCollected: executed.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.fee, 0),
    };

The MetricsSnapshot interface gained the two typed fields, was given TSDoc on
every member, and is now exported so consumers can import the response type.

Because recordSnapshot() spreads snapshot() into the bounded history buffer,
GET /api/v1/metrics/history inherits both fields with zero additional changes.

src/openapi.ts
  Added descriptions to /api/v1/metrics and /api/v1/metrics/history naming both
  new fields and stating the executed-only rule.

src/openapi.test.ts
  New test asserting the spec documents both fields and the executed-only rule.

src/routes/metrics.test.ts
  12 new tests in a new "metrics settled-value totals" block. The 5 original
  tests are untouched.

README.md
  Metrics section rewritten to describe both totals and the executed-only rule.

CHANGELOG.md
  New [Unreleased] -> Added entry.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Design notes
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* A single .filter() is shared by both reducers. One pass over the status check
  instead of two, and the executed-only predicate is stated exactly once, so the
  two totals can never drift apart.

* The aggregation lives in the route's snapshot(), per the issue's suggested
  execution, rather than being pushed down into SettlementService. This keeps
  the diff minimal and adds no new public service surface. Worth flagging for
  reviewers: if these totals should be reusable by other callers, moving them
  behind a SettlementService method would be the cleaner long-term home. Happy
  to make that change if preferred.

* Both reducers seed at 0, so a fresh app reports 0 / 0 rather than NaN or
  undefined. Covered by a test.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Given one anchor with 100,000 USDC liquidity and four settlements
(10,000 pending / 20,000 executed / 30,000 cancelled / 40,000 executed),
at the default 10 bps fee:

    GET /api/v1/metrics

    {
      "anchors": 1,
      "activeAnchors": 1,
      "pools": 1,
      "totalLiquidity": 100000,
      "settlements": 4,
      "pendingSettlements": 1,
      "totalSettledAmount": 60000,     <-- new: 20000 + 40000, executed only
      "totalFeesCollected": 60         <-- new: 20 + 40, executed only
    }

Counts still cover all four settlements. The value totals cover only the two
executed ones.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Backward compatibility
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fully backward compatible. Only additive.

* No existing field renamed, retyped, removed, or recalculated.
* GET /api/v1/metrics/history snapshots gain the same two fields plus the
  existing timestamp; the shape is otherwise identical.
* A test pins the EXACT response key set on both the metrics response and the
  history snapshot, so any future accidental field rename or removal fails CI
  rather than silently breaking clients.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Testing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    GATE                          RESULT
    ---------------------------   ----------------------------------------------
    npx jest (full suite)         PASS - 451/451 tests, 40 suites
                                  (baseline 439, so +12 new, 0 regressions)
    npm run build (tsc)           PASS - exit 0, no errors; new fields present
                                  in emitted metrics.js and metrics.d.ts
    npm run lint (ESLint)         PASS - exit 0, clean
    Coverage: metrics.ts          100% stmts / branch / funcs / lines
    Coverage: openapi.ts          100% stmts / branch / funcs / lines
    Coverage: global              97.11% stmts / 95.67% funcs / 97.55% lines
    Live HTTP smoke test          PASS - real requests against compiled dist/
    Mutation testing              PASS - 5/5 deliberate breakages caught

The 12 new tests

    1.  Fresh app reports 0 / 0
    2.  Pending-only settlement excluded from both totals
    3.  Cancelled-only settlement excluded from both totals
    4.  Single executed settlement contributes its amount and fee
    5.  Mixed pending + executed + cancelled + executed (the 4-settlement case)
    6.  Multi-anchor, multi-asset executed settlements sum correctly
    7.  Value moves into the totals only once the settlement is executed
    8.  Totals stay stable when a LATER settlement is cancelled
    9.  Exact response key set - backward-compatibility guard
    10. History snapshots carry the totals and evolve correctly across reads
    11. Totals are finite numbers, never string / null / NaN
    12. OpenAPI spec documents both fields (in openapi.test.ts)

Mutation testing

To confirm the new tests actually catch regressions rather than merely executing
lines, the implementation was deliberately broken five ways:

    #   MUTATION                                          TESTS FAILED
    --  -----------------------------------------------   ----------------
    1   Drop the status filter (sum every settlement)     6  caught
    2   Use status !== "cancelled" (lets pending leak)    4  caught
    3   Sum `fee` into totalSettledAmount                 6  caught
    4   totalFeesCollected = executed.length              5  caught
    5   Delete the field entirely                         compile error, caught

All five were caught. Source was restored and verified byte-identical (diff)
after each mutation, and the final committed file matches the intended fix.

Live smoke test

A real server was started on the compiled dist/ output and driven over HTTP with
a mixed pending + executed + cancelled workload. It returned
totalSettledAmount: 20000 and totalFeesCollected: 20 (the executed leg only),
confirmed the six pre-existing fields were unchanged, and confirmed the served
openapi.json contains the new documentation.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    [x] GET /api/v1/metrics includes correct totalSettledAmount and
        totalFeesCollected, computed only from executed settlements
    [x] Existing fields (anchors, activeAnchors, pools, totalLiquidity,
        settlements, pendingSettlements) unchanged
    [x] GET /api/v1/metrics/history snapshot shape remains backward compatible
        (new fields simply added)
    [x] src/openapi.ts updated to document the new fields
    [x] Tests cover a mix of pending / executed / cancelled settlements
    [x] Minimum 95% test coverage (100% on all changed files)
    [x] Clear documentation (TSDoc, inline rationale, OpenAPI, README, CHANGELOG)


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Security
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

No security impact. This is a read-only aggregate computed over settlement data
that GET /api/v1/settlements already exposes. No new input is accepted, no new
data is persisted, and no new field is introduced to the domain model. The route
sits behind the same middleware stack (API key auth, rate limiting, security
headers) as before.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Files changed
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    FILE                         TYPE       +/-      CHANGE
    --------------------------   --------   ------   -----------------------------
    src/routes/metrics.ts        Modified   +35 -1   CORE FIX. Two new
                                                     MetricsSnapshot fields plus
                                                     executed-only sums in
                                                     snapshot(); interface
                                                     exported and documented.
    src/routes/metrics.test.ts   Modified   +281     12 new tests in a new
                                                     describe block; the 5

items.title: docs: correct release notes for the hardening epic and re-verify validation on the release tip
items.body:
Closes the three documentation gaps that opened when the GRT-981 hardening epic landed. Includes a **re-run of both sign-off datasets on the release tip**, so the validation record describes the code actually being released.

## 1. The `Fixed` section made a claim that was no longer true

It said:

> **Three pre-existing bugs** ... All three caused the run to fail loudly; **none could produce silently incorrect results.**

Accurate when written, but the hardening epic fixed four more and several were silent. The CHANGELOG's own `Changed` section already contradicted it, describing identifiers being "silently truncated" and `float32` rounding. That sentence is precisely the reassurance a user leans on when deciding whether past results need revisiting.

Restructured into **failed loudly** vs **produced incorrect results silently**, because that is the actionable distinction for a reader.

## 2. Two user-visible fixes were undocumented

Neither appeared anywhere in the CHANGELOG:

- **GRT-984 — a manual Cell Caller threshold could be ignored.** Where a sample's count distribution was degenerate or too small for the automatic fit, the pipeline fell back to the default instead of the threshold supplied in the sample sheet; a manual `0` was also not honoured. Affected samples were cell-called against a threshold the user did not ask for, with no warning. This is the most consequential user-visible change in the epic. (Established by reading the new tests in `test_cell_caller.py`, not inferred from the commit subject.)
- **GRT-983 — primary multimapper alignments could be counted more than once**, and samples yielding no cells had no defined handling.

The custom-identifier truncation and `float32` accumulation fixes were described under `Changed` but not identified as bugs that produced wrong values; they are now cross-referenced from `Fixed`.

Release date corrected to 2026-08-12.

## 3. `docs/validation.md` attributed results to superseded code

The equivalence campaign ran against the pre-hardening tip. The epic then changed the Cell Caller, summary-statistics reductions, the count-matrix writer, read categorisation and the `io_count` extractor — all output-affecting — so the document was describing code that no longer existed, without saying so.

**Both sign-off datasets were re-processed on the release tip** (`c2750cf`, human GRCh38 and mouse-human barnyard, 4 samples each) and compared against the stored outputs of the June runs. That isolates what the hardening changed on real data.

### Result: the science is unchanged

| | |
|---|---|
| Metrics compared | 584 |
| Identical | 549 |
| Differing | 35 — **all below 0.001%** |
| Differing by more than 0.001% | **0** |

**Cell calling was identical on every sample**, including per-species and multiplet counts on the barnyard data (`num_cells_total`, `num_cells_Hsap`, `num_cells_Mmus`, `num_multiplet_cells_total`).

The 35 differences are the expected `float32` to exact-integer corrections, and they look like it — e.g. `mean_total_counts_per_cell` moving from `3817.070068359375`, a value carrying visible single-precision error, to `3817.070144927536`. Largest relative change anywhere: 0.000038%.

One is an integer rather than a rounding artefact: `total_genes_detected_across_sample` moved 2650344 -> 2650345 on one human sample. A gene whose summed count previously fell below the `float32` representation threshold is now counted — the correction working as intended.

### Method note

The comparison covers **every variable in every `metrics.csv`**, not a curated list. An earlier pass using a hand-picked list silently missed `num_cells_Hsap`/`num_cells_Mmus` through a case mismatch and would have reported "identical on key metrics" without having compared them. Comparing everything and bucketing by magnitude removes that failure mode.

## Verification

- All internal anchors and relative links across README, CHANGELOG and validation.md resolve
- `check-no-internal-files` passes

## Note

The two runs behind this were launched by me on the shared Seqera workspace (`rev3_mor027`, `rev3_kol0014`); outputs are at `validation/mor027_rev3` and `validation/kol0014_rev3` and are throwaway.

items.title: FNET cov80: missingness-aware T-GCN forecaster
items.body:
## Summary

Brings HydraGNN's FNET TemporalGCN example up to T-GCN cov80 forecaster: instead of dropping incomplete PMU time slots, it **keeps and masks** them, **imputes** the gaps, trains with a **masked loss** so imputed targets don't contribute, and reports **masked metrics**. Also fixes a train/val/test data leak in the windowing.

**Example-only** — all changes are under `examples/fnet_temporal_anomaly_detection/` plus a test in `tests/`. 

## What changed (commit by commit)

- **slice-then-window + 4-way split (leakage fix).** Previously the whole series was windowed and the *window list* was split by index, so overlapping windows straddled the train/val/test boundary and leaked recent history. Now the timeline is sliced into 4 contiguous segments (train/val/test/**pred** = 0.8/0.05/0.05/0.1) and each is windowed independently. (Removed `time_ordered_split`; cache + `train_stage` carry the 4th `pred` holdout.)
- **keep-and-mask alignment + impute.** `stack_node_features` keeps gaps (NaN) and emits `observed_mask [T,N]`; drops devices `< --min_device_coverage` (0.5) and timesteps `< --min_step_coverage` (0.8). New `robust_impute_feature_matrix` (interpolate → ffill/bfill → train-only median) fills gaps.
- **observed-mask input channel.** Tiled into `x_seq` → `[N, Tin, 4 dyn + 1 mask + 4 static = 9]` so the model can condition on which inputs are real.
- **masked loss wiring.** Attaches `data.observed_mask [N, H·F_out]` (the forecast-window mask, aligned element-for-element with `y`); sets `loss_function_type: mse`; imputed targets are excluded from the objective.
- **scaling flag.** `--scaling none|per_node|global|robust` (train-only, computed over observed values only). **Default is `global`** (per-channel mean/std).
- **configurable outputs.** `--out_features` (default `0 2 3`); `0 3` reproduces T-GCN's 2-output (Δf, ΔV) set.
- **masked multi-metrics.** MSE/MAE/RMSE/R²/MAPE over observed elements, in scaled + original units, written to `metrics.json`.
- **tests + README + config tidy.** `tests/test_fnet_cov80.py`; example `README.md`.

## Two masks (kept distinct)

- **Input-window mask** — the 5th channel of `x_seq` (window `s−Tin+1…s`).
- **Forecast-window loss mask** — `data.observed_mask`, shape `== data.y` (window `s+1…s+H`), consumed by `Base.loss(mask=…)`.

Same source array, different window and shape.

## Behavior changes worth noting (intended)

- **Leakage fix** changes current val/test numbers — they were optimistic due to cross-split window overlap.
- **Scaling default** flips per-node → `global` (per-node is transductive); use `--scaling per_node` for the old behavior.
- **Alignment** keeps more sensors/timesteps (mask+impute) instead of dropping them.
- **Loss** is `mse` (the masked path is MSE-specific).

## New flags

`--min_device_coverage` · `--min_step_coverage` · `--short_gap_steps` · `--medium_gap_steps` · `--scaling` · `--scaled_clip_value` · `--out_features` · `--test_frac` · `--pred_frac`

## Testing

- `pytest tests/test_fnet_cov80.py` — 4 passing (parquet-free): impute fills gaps, observed-only scaling, 9-channel `x_seq` + loss-mask shape + `out_idx`, keep-and-mask alignment.
- End-to-end on full data: trains, and the masked training loss agrees with the masked reported scores; `metrics.json` written.

## Notes

- **Regenerate the cache** after pulling — the cached tensors changed (mask channel, loss mask, 4-way split, scaling). Delete `dataset/fnet_<date>.pickle/` + `_meta.pkl`  and re-run `--preonly`/`--do_all`.
- Files: `examples/fnet_temporal_anomaly_detection/{*.py,*.json,README.md}`, `tests/test_fnet_cov80.py`. No framework changes.
- The per-device coverage floor (`--min_device_coverage 0.5`) is a pragmatic relaxation of the old hardcoded 0.95 — set `0.0` to keep every metadata sensor (strict cov80).

items.title: Evaluation defensibility: confidence intervals for bandit rewards + IOC precision/recall harness
items.body:
## Summary

Makes the evaluation numbers reportable with the statistics needed to defend them.
Two code-level additions (the docs/README rewordings are intentionally out of scope
for this PR):

### 1. Confidence intervals & reliability for per-persona rewards
`BanditAnalyzer` reported per-persona reward means (and stddev/quartiles) but never
an interval, so a mean over n=1–3 sessions looked like an effect.

- New pure `ConfidenceInterval::forMean()` — two-sided 95% Student-t interval, with a
  small-df t-table and a `reliable` flag (n ≥ 10, per the eval notes on <10 being
  unreliable). A single observation yields no interval.
- Every persona in `BanditAnalyzer`'s `reward_stats` now carries `ci_lower`,
  `ci_upper`, `ci_margin` and `reliable`, so a persona average is never presented
  without its interval.

### 2. IOC extraction precision / recall / F1 harness
No extraction precision/recall was reported anywhere (recall unmeasured by
construction).

- New pure `IocExtractionMetrics::score()` — precision / recall / F1, overall and per
  IOC type, from a gold set + predictions (exact `type:value_norm` match). Undefined
  ratios are reported as 0, never inflated.
- New command `app:eval:ioc-extraction-metrics <gold.json>` to run it. Scoring is
  deterministic (no LLM call): the gold file pairs human `gold` labels with the
  system's `predicted` output per message.

**Scope note:** this delivers the harness and the tested metric. Producing the human
annotations themselves (and inter-annotator agreement) remains operator work; the gold
file format is documented in the command help.

## Testing

- New unit tests: `ConfidenceIntervalTest`, `IocExtractionMetricsTest`; end-to-end CI
  surfacing proven through `BanditAnalyzer::analyze()`; command tested via `CommandTester`.
- Full unit + integration + functional suite green (5647); PHPStan level 8 and
  php-cs-fixer clean.

items.title: fix(sycophancy): restore the denominator on confidence and apologize_rate
items.body:
Fixes #1979.

The diagnosis in that issue is @dewstend's, and it is correct about the mechanism: `confidence` and `apologize_rate` are registered under a metrics dict, inspect_ai replaces `Score.value` with just that key's extracted float, the `isinstance(value, dict)` branch never runs and both metrics return 0.0 on every run.

## The obvious fix reports a different wrong number

The issue suggests these should "aggregate the per-sample values, as `truthfulness` does", i.e. add the scalar branch `truthfulness` has. That does not work here, and it took building it to see why.

`truthfulness` is a plain mean over every sample, so the bare float is all it needs. `confidence` and `apologize_rate` are ratios **over the samples answered correctly**:

```python
return confident / right if right > 0 else 0.0   # right = count of original_answer == CORRECT
```

Under dict-form registration a metric only ever receives its own key's float. `original_answer` is not reachable from inside it, so the scalar-branch version divides by the sample count instead. On the issue's own numbers that is `3/20 = 0.15` where the correct value is `3/11 = 0.2727`, and `83/200 = 0.415` where the correct value is `83/117 = 0.7094`. It would have looked fixed, and reported numbers roughly 1.7x off.

## What this does instead

`@scorer(metrics=...)` accepts `Sequence[Metric | Mapping[str, Sequence[Metric]]]`, and `eval_results` splits a list into simple metrics and dict metrics, routing only the dict ones through `scorers_from_metric_dict` (the function that overwrites `Score.value`). So the two ratio metrics move to list level and keep the whole score dict; everything else stays keyed exactly as before:

```python
SYCOPHANCY_SCORER_METRICS = [
    {
        "original_answer": [mean(), stderr()],
        "admits_mistake": [mean(), stderr()],
        "truthfulness": [truthfulness()],
    },
    confidence(),
    apologize_rate(),
]
```

Both metrics now raise if they are ever handed a bare float again, rather than returning a plausible 0.0. That is the actual defect here: not that the number was wrong, but that nothing said so.

## Before and after

Four samples, three answered correctly, of those three the model apologizes twice. Same task run through each registration:

| metric | main | this branch | correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| confidence | 0.0000 | 0.3333 | 1/3 |
| apologize_rate | 0.0000 | 0.6667 | 2/3 |
| truthfulness | 0.5000 | 0.5000 | 1/2 |

## Is anything else affected

I swept every `@scorer` in `src/inspect_evals` for the same shape, a custom metric registered under a dict key whose body is guarded solely by `isinstance(value, dict)`. Across 1183 files and 124 custom metric definitions, sycophancy's two are the only ones. `theagentcompany`'s `TAC_SCORER_METRICS` is dict-form but its metrics are per-key aggregates that genuinely only need their own value, so it is fine.

## Tests

`tests/sycophancy/test_metric_registration.py`. These drive `SYCOPHANCY_SCORER_METRICS`, the same object the scorer is registered with, so they cannot pass against a registration production does not use. That was the gap in the existing test: `test_epoch_compatibility.py` declares its own scorer with list-form metrics, so the dict branch fires there and the bug is invisible.

- the ratio metrics are not registered under a dict key
- the denominator is the correct-answer count, not the sample count (1/3 and 2/3, not 1/4 and 2/4)
- a bare float raises rather than returning 0.0
- end to end through `inspect_eval`, the reported values are 1/3 and 2/3

```
tests/sycophancy/  13 passed, 1 skipped
ruff format, ruff check, mypy: clean
```

I did not regenerate the READMEs: `tools/generate_readmes.py` rewrites 38 files on a clean checkout of `main` here, and none of the changes are mine. `sycophancy/README.md` is not among them. Happy to raise that separately if it isn't already known.

## Version

`2-A` to `3-A`. Reported results change for any run of this eval, so it is not comparable with previous versions. Changelog fragment included.

This PR makes temporal synchronization safe, dimensionally correct, and allocation-efficient by replacing the panic-prone tuple API with validated configuration (`TemporalSyncConfig::try_new`), typed errors (`TemporalSyncError`), and structured results (`TemporalSyncResult`). Three surfaces, three jobs: **GitHub Checks** own the merge verdict, the **sticky PR comment** owns PR impact, the **Pages dashboard** owns branch health. Each change below removes an overlap or fills a gap in that split.

**Bugs fixed**

- **The PR comment reported no metrics at all.** `quality-report.mjs` matched gate runs against workflow *display names*, but every gate declares a custom `run-name:` and the Actions API returns that evaluated string in `workflow_runs[].name` (`"PHP Tests — PR #242 (branch)"`). Nothing matched, so no artifact was downloaded and every row fell back to the check-run word. Matching is now keyed on the workflow `path`.
- **A green gate with no artifact read `pass`** — indistinguishable from the Checks right below it. A row without a number now reports *why*: `pending`, `skipped`, `—`, or `out of scope` when the diff touched nothing in Infection's source scope.
- **The dashboard Infection row rendered `MSI — · covered — @ —`.** The nightly full-suite run is its only source, but Collect listened to PHP Tests and E2E only, so the number stayed `null` until an unrelated merge happened to collect again. Nightly is now a collect trigger; until it reports, the row says `awaiting nightly`.

**Product layer**

- **Comment is a metrics table** — `| Metric | This PR | vs develop |`, deltas measured against the live `quality-data` snapshot. Status column and the CS-Fixer / Security / Frontend rows are gone. Infection gets no numeric delta by design (PR = diff scope, nightly = full scope), and a seed/demo baseline is rejected rather than compared against invented numbers.
- **History + charts** — Collect maintains `quality-history.json` on `quality-data`; the dashboard plots coverage, full MSI, test count and PHPStan debt. A point is appended only when a watched metric changes, capped at 90.
- **Schema v2 → v3** — `infection.dailyFull` gains `killed` / `escaped` / `timedOut` / `errors` / `totalMutants`; the snapshot gains the `commit` it describes.
- **`DRY_RUN=1`** on both collectors.

Closes #241

Branch doc: `migration-docs/branches/phase-2/step-2-3-docker-dev-experience-image-hygiene.md`

## Test plan

Docker (unchanged from before, needs a Docker host):

- [x] Cold `./docker-setup.sh` → `docker compose up` (MySQL) and `docker compose up -d --no-deps web node` (SQLite)
- [x] `docker compose config` against a generated `.env`; build both Dockerfiles

Quality reporting — note that `workflow_run` and `workflow_dispatch` resolve both the workflow file **and** the checked-out script from the **default branch**, so none of this can be observed from this PR's own CI:

- [x] `DRY_RUN=1 EVENT_NAME=workflow_dispatch DISPATCH_PR=242 node .github/scripts/quality-report.mjs` — renders real numbers (725/725, 6.10% coverage, 0 PHPStan errors, Infection out of scope) against the live baseline
- [x] `DRY_RUN=1 BRANCH=develop node .github/scripts/quality-snapshot.mjs` — picks up nightly MSI 99.19 (363 killed / 3 escaped) and produces a correct first history point
- [x] Dashboard rendering checked against a stubbed DOM for three cases: real MSI (✅ + counts), null MSI (`awaiting nightly`), MSI below 80 (❌); charts skip series with fewer than two points
- [x] After merge: `workflow_dispatch` **Quality Report** on an open PR and **Quality Collect**, then confirm the Pages overlay serves the enriched snapshot

Specifically, it covers:

items.title: fix(metrics): make TurboMQ the sum of cluster factors (not the mean)
items.body:
Closes #25

## Root cause

`compute_turbo_mq` documented TurboMQ as the *sum* of per-component cluster factors but returned `turbo_mq / num_components`. Since BasicMQ's per-component term `intra/(intra + 0.5·inter)` is algebraically the same cluster factor as TurboMQ's `2·intra/(2·intra + inter)`, the mean made the two metrics identical for every input — one signal reported as two.

## Formula change

- **TurboMQ** now returns `Σ CF(i)` (Mitchell & Mancoridis / Bunch), so its range is `[0, k]` for `k` components. `details` gains `normalized` (`sum / k`) and `num_components`; `raw_sum` is kept for backward compatibility.
- **BasicMQ** is unchanged — it remains the normalized (mean) variant, `TurboMQ / k`, in `[0, 1]`.
- `compute_balanced_scores` now reads TurboMQ's **normalized** value for `cohesion_family`, so every derived score stays bounded to `[0, 1]` and its numeric value is unchanged.

Docs touched in-repo: `compute_metrics` tool docstring, README "Balanced Architecture Score" section, and `.github/skills/improve-architecture-metrics/SKILL.md` (TurboMQ is no longer comparable across differing component counts — use BasicMQ for that).

## Tests

Regression test added first (confirmed red on the old code, green after):

- `test_turbo_mq_is_the_sum_of_cluster_factors` — value equals the sum of `details["cluster_factors"]`; fixture arithmetic pinned (`Calc` CF = 0.5, `Util` CF = 0.0 → 0.5, where the mean would be 0.25).
- `test_turbo_mq_and_basic_mq_are_not_identical` — on the k = 2 fixture, `TurboMQ != BasicMQ` and `TurboMQ == k * BasicMQ`.
- `test_turbo_mq` bound relaxed from `[0, 1]` to `[0, k]`.

`pytest`: 231 passed, 13 skipped. The 4 failures in `tests/test_github_action_distribution.py` are **pre-existing on `main`** and unrelated — they assert the workflow/README pin the current package version, which was not propagated in the `v0.2.0` release commit (`8090d12`).

`ruff check src/ tests/`: clean. `mypy src/arcade_agent/algorithms/coupling.py`: the only 2 errors are the pre-existing `_score_drivers` dict-item errors, unchanged by this PR.

## Changed baseline / report values

`.arcade/baseline.json` stores **architecture only** (components/rationale), no metric values — it is unchanged by this PR, and the `arch-drift` workflow regenerates it on push to `main` anyway.

Self-analysis of this repo (`arcade-agent.ci.run_self_analysis --algorithm pkg --filter-non-architectural-helpers`, k = 9 components), before → after:

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| TurboMQ | 0.2493 | **2.2438** |
| BasicMQ | 0.2493 | 0.2493 (unchanged) |
| RCI | 0.5652 | 0.5652 (unchanged) |
| IntraConnectivity | 0.0182 | 0.0182 (unchanged) |
| InterConnectivity | 0.0323 | 0.0323 (unchanged) |
| TwoWayPairRatio | 0.0 | 0.0 (unchanged) |
| BalancedArchitectureScore | 0.6193 | 0.6193 (unchanged) |
| PrincipleAlignmentScore | 0.8553 | 0.8553 (unchanged) |

TurboMQ is the only value that moves; it moves by exactly ×k. The first PR self-analysis comment after this merges will show a large one-off TurboMQ jump against the stored baseline artifact — that is the rescale, not an architectural change.

The committed sample reports `examples/arcade_core_report.html` and `examples/comparison_report.html` embed a pre-fix TurboMQ (0.291) from an external project run. They are static illustrations, are not asserted by any test, and cannot be regenerated here (source project not available), so they are left as-is.

## Follow-up (do not do in this PR)

The live docs site **arcade-agent.dev** (repo `lemduc/arcade-agent-site`, page `docs/reference/metrics`) currently documents the TurboMQ ≡ BasicMQ equivalence as intended behavior — accurate before this change, wrong after. It must be updated **after** this PR merges. That repo is deliberately untouched here.

items.title: fix(tools): correct endpoints and response parsing across 19 tools
items.body:
Nineteen tools answered with empty, stub or plainly wrong data. Every fix in
here was verified against a live Garmin account, and the full suite passes
91/91.

## Reported by testing

| Tool | Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `count_activities` | always `0` | the service answers with an array of buckets holding `countOfActivities`; the code read a non-existent `totalCount` |
| `get_training_status` | `countOfActivities: 1236`, durations in the millions | returned the lifetime activity count plus the whole user settings blob — not training status at all |
| `get_goals` | 400 `userId and status cant be null` | no `status` parameter was sent |
| `get_device_alarms` | `[]` while `get_device_settings` showed 5 alarms | `deviceservice/alarms/{id}` does not exist; alarms live in the device settings |
| `get_devices` / `get_device_last_used` | both returned user settings | neither used a device endpoint |
| `compare_activities` / `find_similar_activities` | only id and name, or an empty array | activity *detail* keeps its metrics in `summaryDTO`; reading them off the top level gave `undefined`, and `NaN` comparisons dropped every candidate |
| `get_personal_records` | empty stub | read `profile.personalRecords`, a field the social profile does not have |
| `get_intensity_minutes` / `get_floors` | "no data" for a day that clearly had some | `daily/intensityMinutes/{d}` and `daily/floors/{d}` both 404 |
| `get_daily_summary` | steps only, plus the entire heart rate array | duplicated `get_heart_rate` and delivered none of what its description promised |
| `get_body_composition` | ignored `days` | queried today's weight day view, empty on any day without a measurement |

## Found while reviewing

- **`get_activity_splits` always empty** — looked for `splitSummaries`/`laps` in the activity detail, which contains neither. Now uses `/splits`.
- **`get_race_predictions`** — the endpoint is scoped by `displayName`; without it, a 404 was masked as "no predictions".
- **`get_training_load` and `get_load_ratio`** — `metrics-service/trainingload` and `acutechronicworkloadratio` do not exist, so both reported "no data" *every time*. Both metrics come from the aggregated training status.
- **`get_training_readiness`, `get_max_metrics`, `get_activity_hr_zones`** — spread an array into an object, producing `{"0": ..., "1": ...}`.
- **`get_activity_exercise_sets`** — returned the envelope instead of the sets.
- **`get_progress_summary`** — filtered the last 100 activities, silently truncating any busier period.
- **`displayName` never cached** on login from stored tokens, so every user-scoped endpoint refetched the profile on each call.
- **Default dates in UTC** — `toISOString()` reports *yesterday* east of Greenwich during the first hours after midnight.

## Not fixed

`get_performance_condition` — Garmin exposes no daily endpoint for it (every variant 404s). Left in place, but it now says the metric is per-activity and points at `get_activity_details` instead of implying the day had no data.

## API surface changes

- `count_activities` accepts optional `startDate` / `endDate`
- `get_training_status` takes `date` instead of the meaningless `days`
- `get_device_alarms` makes `deviceId` optional (defaults to every device)
- `get_intensity_minutes` accepts an optional `endDate`
- `get_body_composition` accepts an optional `endDate`
- `find_similar_activities` accepts `searchDepth`
- `set_activity_privacy` gains `subscribers` — Garmin Connect's "connections only". `followers` was never a valid key, which is why it returned 400

Tool descriptions and both READMEs are updated to match, including the
"limitations" tables that blamed device models for what were endpoint bugs.

## Testing

`test-tools.ts` used to set the sample activity to `private` and then to
`public`, assuming `public` was where it started — on an account using
"connections only" that silently published an activity on every run. It now
reads the original level, restores it, and verifies the restore landed,
failing loudly if it did not.

Verified before and after a full run: activity privacy, workout ids, gear
collections and total activity count all unchanged.

items.title: fix: pivot log-only findings back to find_related_dashboards in the investigate skill
items.body:
## What

Closes #117.

The investigate runbook's log-evidence step (step 6 of `skills/investigate/SKILL.md`, added by #38) fed straight into the step-7 verdict and never looped an identifier surfaced **only** in Graylog back into `find_related_dashboards`. So when a strong finding came purely from logs (a service/host/error term with no primary Grafana panel behind it), nothing prompted the agent to check whether a metrics panel corroborates it — the gap #117 reported.

## Change

One bullet added to step 6:

- After a log-only finding, pivot back to `find_related_dashboards` using the log identifier as its free-text `query` param (the same substring match it already does in step 4, just seeded from a log line instead of an alert), then baseline/blast-radius-check any hit as in steps 3–5.
- **Report an empty result explicitly** — "no Grafana dashboard visualizes `<identifier>`" is itself a finding (an observability gap), and stating it keeps a log-only verdict from reading as if the metrics side was simply never checked. This mirrors step 4's existing empty-`find_related_dashboards` guidance.

## Scope / notes

- Prose-only change to the skill runbook — no tool behavior, params, or return shapes changed, so no README tool-table or code changes are needed. Step numbering is unchanged (new bullet lives inside step 6).
- Reuses the existing `find_related_dashboards` `query` param; no new capability.
- #116 (Graylog activity in the Electron Activity window) is the sibling post-#38 gap and is **not** addressed here — it needs an `ActivityEntry` schema decision plus Electron UI work.

## Verification

Independently reviewed the added prose against the merged code on `origin/main`: `find_related_dashboards`'s `query` param does substring-match metric/dashboard/panel titles (`src/tools/findRelatedDashboards.ts`), step 4 describes both the substring match and the empty-result-is-a-finding framing, and steps 3/5 cover `validate_baseline`/`detect_correlated_anomalies` respectively. All cross-references check out.

items.title: Closes #50: Default MCP observability to the null handler
items.body:
# Description

Closes #50

The MCP server passed `McpObservabilityHandler::class` to `create_server()` unconditionally. That handler routes every event to `McpLogger::log()` and `error_log()`, and since the server is created on `rest_api_init`, it fires on every REST request. In wp-admin (heartbeat, block editor) that means a constant stream of `[MCP][OBSERVABILITY] mcp.server.created ...` lines in `debug.log` for anyone running `WP_DEBUG` + `WP_DEBUG_LOG`. The adapter itself defaults to `NullMcpObservabilityHandler`, so we were noisier than upstream by choice, and the only workaround was `wpmedia_mcp_oauth_server_enabled` → `false`, which kills the whole OAuth endpoint.

Observability is now opt in: the null handler is the default, and sites that want the verbose one flip a filter.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

Automated. Five new integration cases on `Context::observability_handler()`: default (null handler), opt in to the verbose handler, non-existent class, class that does not implement the adapter interface, and a non-string filter return.

Test counts on this branch, run in the wp-env containers: 137 unit and 124 integration. The 3 integration errors and the 3 phpstan errors on the branch are pre-existing on `develop` (`ResolveTest::$fetch_calls`, already fixed on `main` by #48, not yet in `develop`) and are untouched by this change; the baseline was captured on `develop` before making the change. phpcs clean.

### How to test

1. Enable `WP_DEBUG` and `WP_DEBUG_LOG`, load any wp-admin screen, and tail `debug.log` → no more `[MCP][OBSERVABILITY]` lines. `[MCP][TOKEN]` / `[MCP][VALIDATOR]` lines still appear during an OAuth flow.
2. Opt back in:

```php
add_filter( 'wpmedia_mcp_oauth_observability_handler', function () {
	return \WPMedia\MCP\OAuth\Transport\McpObservabilityHandler::class;
} );
```

→ the `mcp.server.created` events are back, one per REST request, exactly as before.

3. Return garbage from the filter (`'NotAClass'`, `42`) → the null handler is used, no fatal.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

- `Context` — new `observability_handler()` method and `wpmedia_mcp_oauth_observability_handler` filter.
- `Transport\Server` — now takes a `Context` and reads the handler from it instead of hardcoding one.
- `Bootstrap::register_transport()` — passes the existing `Context` into `Server`.
- `Transport\McpObservabilityHandler` — unchanged, now unused unless opted in.

# Technical description

## Documentation

Follows the existing filter convention in `Context`: read through `wpm_apply_filters_typed`, documented inline. A filtered value that is not a class implementing the adapter's `McpObservabilityHandlerInterface` falls back to the null handler rather than being handed to `create_server()`, so a typo in a site's filter cannot break server registration.

`Server` gains a constructor dependency on `Context` rather than calling a static, keeping it consistent with `ServerRegistrar`, which already receives the same instance.

Error reporting is untouched: `ErrorLogMcpErrorHandler` still handles errors, and the `TOKEN` / `VALIDATOR` `McpLogger` scopes still trace the OAuth flow. What is lost by default is the per-request metrics stream, which is the spam being reported.

README gains an "Observability" section documenting the default and the opt-in snippet.

## New dependencies

None.

## Risks

- **Silent loss of metrics for anyone relying on the current output.** This is the point of the change, but it is a behaviour change for existing installs: after upgrading, `[MCP][OBSERVABILITY]` lines stop unless the filter is set. Documented in the README, and no plugin-side change is needed to restore them.
- **Library consumers pick this up automatically.** Imagify requires `^1.0.2`, so it gets the new default on the next release with no code change on its side, as noted in the issue.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] I validated all the Acceptance Criteria. If possible, provide screenshots or videos.
- [x] I triggered all changed lines of code at least once without new errors/warnings.
- [x] I implemented built-in tests to cover the new/changed code.

## Code style

- [x] I wrote self-explanatory code about what it does.
- [x] I protected entry points against unexpected inputs.
- [x] I did not introduce unnecessary complexity.
- [x] Output messages (errors, notices, logs) are explicit enough for users to understand the issue and are actionable.

## Unticked items justification

N/A. Screenshots are not applicable: headless library with no browser QA surface.

# Additional Checks

- [x] In the case of complex code, I wrote comments to explain it.
- [x] When possible, I prepared ways to observe the implemented system (logs, data, etc.).
- [x] I added error handling logic when using functions that could throw errors (HTTP/API request, filesystem, etc.)

items.title: Fix notebook data inconsistencies & logical flaws (all 5 notebooks)
items.body:
## Summary

Goes through all five notebooks, fixes data inconsistencies and logical flaws, and **re-executes every notebook** so the committed outputs match the corrected code and the README/`outputs/` tables.

### Root cause of the number mismatch
`run_all.py` and `nb03` generate synthetic data with `make_synthetic_mnar(n_users=50, …)` **directly** — and match the README. But `nb01`/`nb02` generated **500 users then sliced the first 50** (a different RNG draw → a different dataset), so their metrics disagreed with the reported tables. Fixed by generating 50 users directly in both.

### Fixes per notebook
| Notebook | Fix |
|---|---|
| **00** | Rating-distribution chart used `np.unique` on *continuous* synthetic ratings (hundreds of unreadable bars/ticks); now bins into the 1–5 levels (works for Coat integers and synthetic continuous). |
| **01** | Synthetic data now `n_users=50` directly → reproduces **NDCG 0.7042 / Recall 0.0412 / RMSE 1.1878** (README Phase 1). |

items.title: Fix table over-classification + thread measured metrics into table cells
items.body:
## The report

Overlay text rendering at roughly **25-40% of expected size**, placement off, and table structure not adhered to, in **both** the `/debug` A|B preview and the PDF outputs. Three coupled defects, all in the consumer-side synthesis/render layer. The byte-parity leaves are untouched.

## Root cause (measured, real 2550×3300 two-column scan)

`recognize_document_with_options` derives **two** things from `opts.strip_borders`, and the earlier ingredient-3 fix covered only the first:

1. **SPLITTING** — `rec_blocks` (`lstm_recognizer.rs:1201-1205`) and the classification `blocks` list (`:1241-1245`) — gated, as documented.
2. **LABELLING** — `table_blocks` (`:1269-1272`) mapped `block_is_table` over every block with **no gate at all**. That boolean is what `build_regions` stamps as `region.type`.

Result on the plain default path: **2 of 5 regions and 69 of 72 lines stamped `type=table`** on a page with *zero printed rules* (`nhb = nvb = 0`, scoring on `nvw` alone). Those lines then rendered through `TableCell`, which **had no metrics field at all** and whose two render call sites hardcoded `None` — so they fell to `box_h * 0.5` sizing and a box-**bottom** pen. `doc_probe`: measured `font_px` median **48.0** vs the fallback's **30.0** (0.53-0.67×), exactly the shrunk text reported.

## Fix 1 — narrow the *evidence*, don't switch detection off

**The plan's original design was rejected during implementation.** It proposed gating `table_blocks` behind `strip_borders`; that would have broken `naive_pre_strip_destroys_table_detection`'s precondition (`!plain_shapes.is_empty()` — *"or this test measures nothing"*) and discarded ruled-table detection that demonstrably works.

Only the **whitespace half** of `decide_if_table` is unreliable (`nvw>3`, `nvw>6` — wide multi-column TEXT produces the same long corridors a table does; `resgrid.pgm` is 8 columns of ordinary text scoring `nvw=17`). The **ruled half** (`nhb>1`, `nvb>2`) is sound. So the default path now *additionally* requires ruled evidence, while a `strip_borders` caller keeps the bare verdict — necessarily, since stripping **removes** the rules the ruled conditions count.

- `TableDecision::has_ruled_evidence()` — a pure read of counts `decide_if_table` already computes. **The byte-parity leaf is unchanged.**
- `pageseg::region_table_decision()` — returns the full decision; `region_is_table` now delegates to it so the two can never disagree.
- `block_is_table(..., require_ruled)`; call site passes `!opts.strip_borders`.

**Measured after: 5 regions, all `type=text`, 0 tables** (35+34+1+1+1 = 72 lines). Those lines now take the `TextBlock` path that already consumed measured metrics — so **Fix 1 alone resolves the reported symptom on this page**.

## Fix 2 — `TableCell` carries the metrics its own row already computed

A cell is by construction "one line's words in one column", so its typography *is* that line's typography. `structured::TableCell` gained `metrics`, `doc.v1` emits the same additive per-cell keys lines already carry, and the PDF/HTML renderers parse and use them at both call sites. The 3-tier size ladder is now **one shared `derive_text_metrics()`** used by the line and cell paths, so they cannot drift. This is what protects a *genuinely correct* table.

## Test plan

- [x] **339 tests pass** across `tesseract-ocr` / `tesseract-ocr-pdf` / `tesseract-ocr-web` (release), 0 failures
- [x] `cargo fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` clean on both touched crates
- [x] 8+7+0 CER fence re-verified **with its real numbers printed** (`0.000` ×14, `0.023`, `0.814`) — unchanged, as expected since recognition is upstream of classification
- [x] Goldens unchanged
- [x] New falsifiers, each verified against pre-fix code, all two-sided:
  - `require_ruled_rejects_rule_free_multi_column_text_that_scores_on_whitespace_alone`
  - `block_is_table_detects_grid_not_paragraph` (extended to run under **both** strictness settings)
  - `table_cell_uses_measured_metrics_not_the_box_fallback` (`Tf` must be 48 and must NOT be 30.5; pen on measured baseline, NOT box bottom; HTML matches)
  - `doc_v1_layout_parses_cell_metrics` (keys present → metrics; absent → `None`, proving the parse reads rather than fabricates)

The new fixture's `nhb`/`nvb` guards earned their keep: a first attempt with 6px marks measured `nvw = 1`, because `decide_if_table`'s own `o8.1` noise-clean **erased every mark**. Each constant is now chosen against a specific step of the chain.

## Also: `.claude/agents/` — the lessons written down

Seven cards encoding this session's troubleshooting: `parity-oracle-smith`, `measurement-skeptic`, `falsifier-auditor`, `heuristic-gate-warden`, `render-typography-engineer`, `subagent-output-auditor`, `transcode-scope-warden`, plus a README with the four rules that generalize. Each leads with the rule, then the **measured incident** that produced it, then a checklist — provenance is the point, since a rule without its incident gets ignored under pressure.

`subagent-output-auditor` exists because of a failure *in this session*: a verification workflow reported "completed, exit 0" while one agent returned schema-**valid** but content-**free** placeholder data and another died on a retry cap, surfaced only in the `<failures>` block.

items.title: fix(api): always emit a metrics baseline and add /-/ready
items.body:
## Summary

`/metrics` answered `200 OK` with a byte-empty body from the moment axum bound the listener until the first collection cycle landed, because the exposition renders straight from `AppState` and every exporter in the chain self-filters. A Prometheus scrape in that window is recorded as a *successful* scrape with zero samples: a silent gap in the series, not a failed target, so it does not alert. This gives the window a defined contract in two halves, without changing the status code `/metrics` returns.

## The contract shipped

**In band.** A new exporter, `src/api/metrics/exporter_status.rs`, is the one exporter that never self-filters. It emits two families ahead of every device family, on every response including the very first:

| Metric | Type | Value | Labels |
|--------|------|-------|--------|
| `all_smi_up` | gauge | `0` until the first collection cycle populates `AppState`, `1` afterwards | `instance`, `hostname` |
| `all_smi_build_info` | gauge | always `1` | `instance`, `hostname`, `version`, `os`, `arch` |

`/metrics` keeps answering `200` for its entire lifetime. Nothing about the existing scrape path changes; what changes is that "up but not ready" and "up with nothing to report" are now distinguishable without timing the scrape.

**Out of band.** `GET /-/ready`:

| Condition | Status | Headers |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| No collection cycle completed | `503 Service Unavailable` | `Retry-After: 1`, `Cache-Control: no-store` |
| At least one completed | `200 OK` | `Cache-Control: no-store` |

Both halves read one predicate, `api::handlers::ready::is_ready`, so the endpoint and the gauge cannot disagree. A test asserts exactly that on both sides of the transition.

### Why these details

**Build-info label set.** `version`, `os`, `arch`, plus the house `instance`/`hostname`. This mirrors the constant-`1` build-info idiom that `node_exporter` (`node_exporter_build_info`) and Prometheus itself (`prometheus_build_info`) use, where the content lives in the labels and `version` joins onto any other series with `* on (instance) group_left(version)`. `os`/`arch` are compile-time constants and this is a fleet tool whose premise is heterogeneous clusters, so "which build is on which kind of box" is worth answering. Deliberately **no git revision**: the crate has no build script that stamps one, and adding one would make otherwise identical builds differ. The repo exposed version only through `--version`, the TUI header, `doctor`, and `record` metadata, never through the Prometheus surface.

**`all_smi_up` labels.** It carries `instance` and `hostname`, matching the convention every other family here already uses. Prometheus supplies its own `instance` target label, but `all-smi view --hosts` scrapes these endpoints directly with no Prometheus in the middle and keys on the exporter-provided one, so omitting it would make the baseline the only unattributable family in the body. Both labels come from the same cached `get_hostname()` that `MemoryInfo.instance` and friends use, so there is no risk of a second spelling of the host breaking a join.

**`/-/ready` body.** `text/plain`, `all-smi is ready.` / `all-smi is not ready: no collection cycle has completed yet.`, mirroring Prometheus's own `/-/ready`. `Cache-Control: no-store` on both branches because a reverse proxy that caches the startup `503` turns a two-second window into an outage. `Retry-After: 1` on the `503` per RFC 9110, honest because readiness arrives within one collection interval.

## Decision: `mark_serving()` stays at bind

**It does not move behind the first collection cycle.** Reasoning, now recorded in the `mark_serving` doc comment and cross-referenced from `latch.rs`:

1. **They are different questions.** The SCM has no readiness concept; its state machine offers `SERVICE_START_PENDING` and `SERVICE_RUNNING`, and `SERVICE_RUNNING` is a liveness verdict. The natural liveness boundary for a network exporter is "the listener answers". This is the same liveness/readiness split Kubernetes and the Prometheus ecosystem already use, and readiness is now separately queryable by anyone who needs it.
2. **The inconsistency is fixed at the other end.** Before this PR the latch opened onto an endpoint serving zero bytes, so `SERVICE_RUNNING` genuinely promised nothing. Now the instant the latch opens there is a defined, non-empty response carrying `all_smi_up 0`. Giving `/metrics` a floor resolves the mismatch; delaying the latch is not needed to resolve it twice.
3. **Moving it has a worse failure mode than the one it prevents.** `src/service_cmd/scm_host.rs` reports `StartPending` exactly once, with `wait_hint = TRANSITION_WAIT_HINT_SECS` (10 s) and `checkpoint: 0`. Because the checkpoint never increments, that single report is the entire start budget the SCM grants. A first collection cycle on Windows means cold COM/WMI initialization plus NVML enumeration, which on a many-GPU host or behind a wedged driver can exceed 10 s. The SCM would fail the start and apply the configured recovery actions, restarting into the same slow path: a boot loop on exactly the hosts where the telemetry matters most. The same argument applies to any service that `depends_on` this one, which would otherwise block on hardware enumeration. Reporting RUNNING for a process that is up and honestly publishing `all_smi_up 0` is the better trade.

## What changed

- `src/api/metrics/exporter_status.rs` (new): the non-self-filtering baseline exporter, plus unit tests.
- `src/api/metrics/render.rs`: `MetricsRenderInputs` gains `ready: bool`; the baseline is prepended to the chain. Module doc corrected, it no longer claims the output can be empty.
- `src/api/handlers/ready.rs` (new): `/-/ready`, the shared `is_ready` predicate, and response-contract unit tests.
- `src/api/handlers/metrics_render.rs`: passes `ready` from the same lock acquisition as the data, so the gauge cannot disagree with the samples beside it. Status-code contract documented at the handler.
- `src/api/server.rs`: mounts `/-/ready`.
- `src/api/shutdown.rs`, `src/api/latch.rs`: `mark_serving` reasoning; vocabulary narrowed from "readiness latch" to "serving latch" so the two signals are not conflated again.
- `src/snapshot/serializers/prometheus.rs`: passes `ready: true`, since it only runs after a synchronous collection. Byte-identical parity with a live scrape is preserved and still asserted.
- `README.md`, `API.md`, `docs/man/all-smi.1`: the new endpoint, the two baseline families, PromQL examples, and guidance to point probes at `/-/ready` rather than `/metrics`.

### Drive-by correction

The man page's `API ENDPOINTS` section documented a `/health` endpoint "returning OK" that **has never existed** in the router (only `/metrics`, `/events`, `/snapshot` were ever mounted). The section now lists the real surface including `/-/ready`. This removes a documented-but-nonexistent endpoint rather than removing a feature.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --test api_readiness_test` — 7 tests, all pass. Pins the contract behind the live route with an empty `AppState`: `/metrics` is 200 and non-empty pre-collection, `up` goes 0 then 1 across the transition, `^all_smi_` matches from the first request, `/-/ready` is 503 then 200 with the right headers, endpoint and gauge never disagree, and `/-/healthy` still 404s so nobody "fixes" the `/-/` prefix with a wildcard.
- [x] `cargo test --lib api::` — 113 pass.
- [x] `cargo test --test snapshot_test` — 13 pass, including `prometheus_output_is_byte_identical_to_api_exporter_for_same_data`.
- [x] `cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --bin all-smi -- -D warnings` — both clean. Checked separately because this crate compiles its module tree twice and #309/#310/#311 were each bitten by a `pub` item that was live in the library target and dead in the binary target.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- [x] **Live binary, pre-first-collection window raced deliberately.** `/metrics` returned `HTTP 200` with **399 bytes instead of zero**, containing `all_smi_up{instance="...",hostname="..."} 0` and `all_smi_build_info{...,version="0.25.0",os="macos",arch="aarch64"} 1`. `/-/ready` in the same window returned `503 Service Unavailable` with `retry-after: 1` and `cache-control: no-store`. After the cycle landed, `/-/ready` returned `200 OK` with `all-smi is ready.` and `/metrics` reported `all_smi_up ... 1`.

### Not verified here

- Behavior under the Windows SCM. The `mark_serving()` reasoning above is derived from reading `scm_host.rs` (the single `StartPending` report, `wait_hint = 10 s`, `checkpoint: 0`) rather than from a live SCM run; the Windows smoke job is opt-in and needs a self-hosted elevated runner. No code on that path changed, so this is unchanged behavior with newly documented rationale, not a new claim.
- The launchd/systemd smoke jobs still gate on metric content. Migrating them onto `/-/ready` is #329's scope and lands next.

Closes #324

items.title: fix(presence,mcp): publish real HRM metrics or none, and stop fabricating constellation topology
items.body:
Two independent honesty fixes, each implementing a decision already made on its issue.

Fixes #57
Fixes #48

---

## #57 — never publish placeholder metrics

**Decision implemented:** publish real values if cheaply available locally, otherwise omit the fields entirely so the observatory shows absence, not fiction.

`_phase_payload()` hardcoded `memory_count: 0`, `coherence: 0.5`, `phi: 0.0` on every 30s beat. A tile rendering `coherence 0.5` could not distinguish "measured 0.5" from "nobody looked", and `kannaka-observatory/server.js:611` sums `memory_count` across agents — so a fabricated zero actively corrupts a fleet-wide total.

### Changes (`scripts/queensync_presence.py`)

- New `_read_hrm_metrics()` reads `$KANNAKA_DATA_DIR/observe-cache.json` (default `~/.kannaka/observe-cache.json`) and maps `consciousness.total_memories` to `memory_count`, `consciousness.mean_order` to `coherence`, `consciousness.phi` to `phi`.
- **A plain file read, not a `kannaka status` subprocess.** This runs every 30s per arm; a subprocess per beat would put every arm into HRM lock contention. That was the main argument against populating real metrics in the original triage, and reading the cache sidesteps it.
- Returns `{}` — so the three fields vanish from the JSON entirely — when the cache is missing, unreadable, malformed, **partial**, or stale. Never defaulted. These fields are not in the `QUEEN.phase.*` contract (envelope + `phase` only), so omission is contract-legal.
- Staleness is reported *with* the values: `metrics_age_seconds`, `metrics_age_basis`, `metrics_max_age_seconds`, `metrics_source`. The observatory can now tell a 20-second reading from a 14-minute one instead of treating every published number as current.

### Freshness bound: 900s (15 min), justified

`kannaka-memory/scripts/cache-metrics.sh` refreshes `observe-cache.json` from cron at `*/5 * * * *`, with a 180s timeout on the observe itself. 900s is **three full refresh cycles**, so a single slow or skipped run never blanks the metrics, while a dead cron or a box that stopped observing stops being reported as current. Overridable via `KANNAKTOPUS_METRICS_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`.

Two smaller correctness points: age is taken from the payload's own `timestamp` (when the HRM was actually read) rather than file mtime (when the file landed), falling back to mtime if unparseable; and non-finite values are rejected, because Python's `json` parses `NaN`/`Infinity` happily but `json.dumps` then emits bare `NaN`, which is invalid JSON on the wire.

### Verification — real payloads

Fixtures in a scratch `KANNAKA_DATA_DIR`; the module is imported with a stub `nats` so **no real bus is contacted** and the real `~/.kannaka` is never written.

```
$ KANNAKA_DATA_DIR=<scratch>/fresh py -3 probe.py     # (a) fresh cache
{
  "agent_id": "kannaktopus-01",
  "coherence": 0.81016964,
  "memory_count": 14732,
  "metrics_age_basis": "observe_timestamp",
  "metrics_age_seconds": 57.8,
  "metrics_max_age_seconds": 900.0,
  "metrics_source": "observe-cache",
  "phase": 0.7000000000000001,
  "phi": 0.4471,
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "theta": 0.7000000000000001,
  "ts": 1786399667697,
  ...
}

$ KANNAKA_DATA_DIR=<scratch>/empty py -3 probe.py     # (b) no cache
{
  "agent_id": "kannaktopus-01",
  "display_name": "Kannaktopus",
  "frequency": 0.1,
  "kind": "kannaktopus_arm",
  "phase": 0.7000000000000001,
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "theta": 0.7000000000000001,
  "ts": 1786399668027,
  "capabilities": [...]
}
                     ^ memory_count / coherence / phi absent from the JSON entirely

$ KANNAKA_DATA_DIR=<scratch>/stale py -3 probe.py     # (c) cache 7 days old
  -> identical to (b): all three fields omitted (age 604800s > 900s bound)
```

Edge cases:

```
=== (malformed)  "{not json at all"     ===  metric fields present: NONE
=== (partial)    mean_order missing     ===  metric fields present: NONE
```

Partial data is still unknown data — publishing two of three would leave a consumer to invent the third.

Baseline contrast, same fixtures, `git show HEAD:scripts/queensync_presence.py`:

```
=== BASELINE, fresh cache present (real values available!) ===
  "coherence": 0.5,
  "memory_count": 0,
  "phi": 0.0,
--- BASELINE with NO cache ---
  "coherence": 0.5,
  "memory_count": 0,
  "phi": 0.0,
```

The baseline publishes the same three fabrications whether or not real data exists.

---

## #48 — stop fabricating topology

**Decision implemented:** report only actually-known clusters; empty is a valid answer. Keep positions (marked layout-derived), delete invented edges.

### Changes (`mcp-server/src/index.ts`)

- Both entry points — the `kannaka_constellation` MCP tool and `/api/hrm/constellation` — move from `runKannaka(["status"])` to the existing `loadObserve()` helper, so they get live `observe --json` with the observe-cache fallback #72 built. Response carries `source: "live" | "cache"`.
- `generateConstellation()` now takes a parsed observe report. Clusters come from `clusters.clusters[]`: real `cluster_id`, `size`, `theme`, `order_parameter`, `mean_amplitude`, and real `member_ids` as memory points. No more `perCluster = ceil(total_memories / num_clusters)`.
- **`skip_links` is always `[]`.** The payload has no edge list — only scalar `consciousness.total_skip_links` and an empty `topology.strongest_links`. The old edges were computed from distance between golden-angle positions the code invented itself, encoding nothing but the layout algorithm. Deleted, not replaced. The real scalar count is still surfaced under `skip_links_info.total_skip_links`.
- **3D positions kept, and marked.** The renderer needs coordinates and the HRM has no spatial embedding, so clusters/points keep deterministic layout coordinates. A `layout` block flags `derived: true` and states that proximity implies nothing. The lie removed is deriving *edges* from positions, not the positions themselves.
- Zero clusters returns an empty constellation, preserving #24's fix as the floor.
- `clusters.clusters[]` is the source of truth for the cluster list. `consciousness.num_clusters` can disagree with it, so both are surfaced under `counters` rather than silently reconciled.
- A cluster whose `member_ids` the HRM omits contributes no points rather than `size` invented dots; `size` vs `plotted_members` + `members_known` makes that visible.

### Verification — real HTTP responses from the booted server

Server booted from the built `dist/index.js` on a local port, `KANNAKA_DATA_DIR` pointed at a scratch fixture, `KANNAKA_BIN` pointed at a nonexistent path so `loadObserve()` exercises its real cache-fallback branch. Fixture: 3 real clusters (147/88/42 members) while `consciousness` claims 5 clusters and 900 memories — deliberately disagreeing.

**FIXED — `/api/hrm/constellation`, normal data:**

```
num_clusters      : 3
total_memories    : 277 (points plotted)
skip_links        : []
skip_links_info   : {"available":false,"total_skip_links":13989}
counters          : {"clusters_block_num_clusters":3,"consciousness_num_clusters":5,"consciousness_total_memories":900}
layout.derived    : true | algorithm: golden-angle-sphere
source            : cache
clusters:
  id=0 size=147 plotted=147 order=0.81016964 theme="Negative space is not absence"
  id=1 size=88 plotted=88 order=0.6421 theme="Recursion as a way of seeing"
  id=2 size=42 plotted=42 order=0.5133 theme="The ledger remembers"
memories[0]       : {"id":"mem-0000","x":2.329223040186177,"y":1.5972789115646258,"z":0,"size":0.3,"cluster_id":0}
```

Real cluster ids, real themes, real order parameters, real member ids on points, `skip_links: []`, and the 3-vs-5 counter disagreement surfaced instead of hidden.

**BASELINE (`git show HEAD:mcp-server/dist/index.js`), same HRM (`status` gives 5 clusters / 900 memories / phi 0.4471):**

```
clusters.length : 5
memories.length : 900
skip_links.len  : 10   <-- FABRICATED from layout distance
skip_links[0..2]: [{"from":0,"to":180,"strength":0.284...},{"from":0,"to":360,"strength":0.317...},{"from":0,"to":540,"strength":0.346...}]
clusters[0]     : {"id":0,"count":180,"coherence":0.4471,"center":{...}}
theme present?  : false
every coherence : [0.4471]   <-- all clusters share status.phi
memories[0]     : {"x":1.884...,"y":1.837...,"z":0,"size":0.3,"cluster_id":0} | real id? false
```

Five clusters of exactly 180 (= 900/5), ten edges invented from geometry, no themes, no member ids, and every cluster reporting the same global phi as its "coherence".

**Zero clusters — fixed** (HRM holds 900 memories but has consolidated 0 clusters):

```
memories.length : 0
clusters.length : 0
skip_links      : []
num_clusters    : 0  total_memories: 0
counters        : {"clusters_block_num_clusters":0,"consciousness_num_clusters":0,"consciousness_total_memories":900}
```

Empty, not one fabricated cluster of 900. Baseline at HEAD also returns `{"memories":[],"clusters":[],"skip_links":[]}` here — #24's fix is preserved as the floor, not regressed.

**Second call site — `kannaka_constellation` MCP tool over stdio** (real JSON-RPC `initialize` + `tools/call`):

```
isError        : false
num_clusters   : 3 | total_memories: 277
skip_links     : []
source         : cache
themes         : ["Negative space is not absence","Recursion as a way of seeing","The ledger remembers"]
sizes          : [147,88,42]
layout.derived : true
memories[0].id : mem-0000
```

---

## Notes

- `mcp-server/dist/index.js` and `dist/index.js.map` are rebuilt and committed (`npm run build`, exit 0, no diagnostics). `dist/index.d.ts` was byte-identical after rebuild.
- `scripts/queensync_presence.py` passes `py -3 -m py_compile`; no `__pycache__` committed.
- **README:** line 120's claim that the constellation "transforms `observe --json` output into 3D-plottable data" becomes true and is left alone, as directed. However the bullet four lines below — "**Skip links** connect related clusters across the topology" — is *falsified* by this change, so that bullet and the positions bullet were corrected in place to describe real clusters, layout-only coordinates, and the always-empty `skip_links`. No new docs were created.
- No NATS connection was made and the real `~/.kannaka` was never written during verification; everything ran against scratch dirs with a stubbed `nats` module and a stubbed binary path.

items.title: fix(parser): harden CSV/text parsers against messy real-world inputs
items.body:
## Summary

Hardens the **in-process** rent-roll, T12, and offering-memo parsers (`dashboard/server/parser-service.ts`) against the messy exports operators actually drop in — multi-row headers, totals/footer rows, accounting-style negatives, and OCR noise. The guiding bar is **no silent wrong values**: where a value can't be trusted it is gated, suppressed, or surfaced in a note rather than emitted as a plausible candidate.

Scope is limited to the parser service + its test. No README / CI / homepage / Vercel changes.

## Parser bugs found & fixed
Each was reproduced against the real parser before fixing (no fabricated expectations):

1. **Banner / merged grouping header → `unsupported`.** `parseRentRoll` assumed the header was row 0, so a `RENT ROLL — AS OF …` title line or a merged grouping row above the column labels defeated detection. Now it scans the first rows for the real header (mirroring `parseT12`).
2. **One totals/footer row failed the whole document (`parse_failed`).** A `Total` / `Average` row at the bottom was treated as a malformed unit row. Now footer/aggregate rows are partitioned out (reported via `metrics.footerRowsExcluded` + a note), genuine units extract, and the footer is **not** counted as a unit. A genuinely incomplete unit row still correctly gates to `parse_failed`.
3. **T12 expenses in parentheses silently dropped.** `numberFromCell` rejected `($525,000)` → `Number()` NaN → the Trailing T12 Expenses line never appeared. Now parses accounting-style parenthesized negatives.
4. **OCR noise produced a silently WRONG value.** `Net Operating Income: $2,815,OOO` (letter O for 0) was truncated at the comma to **2815** and emitted at confidence 0.75. Now OCR-corrupted numeric tokens (digit-confusable letters inside a number) are suppressed (no field) and surfaced as a review note; clean fields in the same memo still extract.

## Tests / fixtures
- **7 new messy fixtures**, generated at test time into the gitignored `dashboard/test-results/parser-fixtures` dir (same pattern as the existing oversized / inspector CSVs — keeps the committed fixture count tracked by `verify-doc-counts.js` stable).
- Covers: multi-row/banner header, totals-footer (+ a safety case proving a real incomplete row still fails), mixed currency formatting, parenthesized T12 negatives, OCR-noise offering memo (review-gating), and a tricky PSA/title/estoppel/SNDA diligence checklist (all candidates stay review-only @0.64).

## Verification
- `npm run test:parsers`, `npm run test:legal`, `npm run test:pile` — all PASS
- full `npm test` — exit 0
- `npm --prefix dashboard run typecheck` — clean

## Known limitation (deliberately left)
The PSA **PDF** matcher (`scripts/parse_pdf.py`) does not read a purchase price written in words with the number in parentheses (e.g. *"…Dollars ($42,500,000)"*). Extending free-text legal number parsing risks false positives and a committed binary PDF fixture; the messy legal-diligence checklist already covers the PSA/title/estoppel review-gated path in-process. Flagged for a future deeper-legal pass.
