items.title: Review fixes: twelve verified defects from the PR #3 review
items.body:
> **Why this is a separate PR.** PR #3 was merged at `5e1f188` while this review round was in progress. These five commits were pushed to `learned-decision-layer` but landed after the merge, so **none of the fixes below are on `main`**.

CodeRabbit raised 18 findings on PR #3. Each was **reproduced against the code before being fixed** — several turned out to be more serious than reported, and one was a defect in my own work from that PR. Twelve are fixed here; six are triaged with reasons.

## The three that matter most

### `_resolve_rules` labelled one season and returned another's rules

Both branches called `_load_context`, which parses whatever bootstrap payload is newest in bronze. Reproduced by pinning a 2022-23 snapshot with a goalkeeper goal worth **6**:

```
ask 2022-23 -> source_season='2022-23'  exact=True  scoring.version='2022-23'  GKP goal = 10
```

Every label agreed and the numbers were another season's. That is worse than the bug the function was written to fix — it turned a silent substitution into an asserted one, in the one module whose entire purpose is "constants are read, never transcribed".

**My own tests from PR #3 missed it** because they asserted `source_season` — the one thing that was right. They now assert a *value* that differs between the pinned seasons, using a deliberately wrong goalkeeper-goal value so a failure message is unmistakable.

After: `2022-23 -> 6`, `2024-25 -> falls back to 2022-23, 6`, `2026-27 -> 10`.

### A leaking feature could be registered

`validation_status` was hardcoded to `ValidationStatus.LEAKAGE_PASSED`, and `is_registrable` is exactly `status is LEAKAGE_PASSED`. So a program the point-in-time harness **rejected** was written into the registry as a usable feature.

This is an incomplete fix of mine from the foundation tranche: that work made `FeatureEvaluation.leakage_passed` honest and stopped there. That field gates the acceptance *verdict*; this one gates *registration*. They are two fields guarding two things and were fixed one at a time.

### Three metrics were permanently zero, reported as measurements

`metrics.py` read `getattr(o, "bench_points", 0)` and two siblings off `GameweekOutcome` — which never had those fields. `score_squad` returns `simulate_squad(...).total` and discards the decomposition, so the parts were unreachable. `walk_forward` now keeps the `SquadScore`.

The plan for this work said these must never appear "as a zero that reads like a measurement". They did.

## The rest

| # | defect | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `_manifest_for` set only `code_version`, leaving `git_dirty` at its `False` default | `reproducible` is `bool(code_version) and not git_dirty`, so **every** manifest claimed reproducibility, including from a dirty tree |
| 4 | All three `xg models` commands passed the bare `ActiveSchema.from_catalogue()` | The rules-drift check is guarded by `if active.rules_snapshot_hash and ...`, so the one **blocking** check that catches a model fitted under one scoring system and priced under another was inert on every surface that could run it — the check `docs/ml/model_artifacts.md` advertises |
| 16 | The reordered-schema diff zipped `active ∩ needed` against `needed ∩ available` | `available` includes extension features that `active.feature_names` does not, so the lists differed in length and `zip(strict=False)` truncated. With one extension feature and an identical order it reported a reordering that had not happened |
| 12 | `RunKey.condition` omitted `end_gameweek` | A GW6-25 walk and a GW6-38 walk shared a condition, and statistics average replicates within a condition before pairing — so a 20-week and a 33-week result were averaged and paired as one number. `policy_seed` still omits it deliberately, so the shorter walk is a prefix of the longer; both halves asserted |
| 15 | Template ownership reads gameweek `g-1` | At `g=1` that frame is empty, every player filled to zero, and the greedy fill returned whichever fifteen the frame ordered first — an arbitrary squad entering a report labelled "what the crowd owned". Now refuses |
| 14 | The budget floor priced every remaining slot at the *current* position's cheapest player | Slots belonging to other positions were priced wrong in both directions. Reachable, not currently reached |
| 9 | `actual_prices` used `group_by(...).agg(last())` | No order is promised within a group and a double gameweek gives a player two rows, so the price fed to squad value and selling price was nondeterministic. Now sorted by kickoff, degrading honestly on frames without those columns |
| 1 | The API did not filter null prices where the CLI did | `int(None)` raises, taking down every endpoint for that gameweek rather than dropping one player |
| 18 | `test_the_declared_stochastic_set_matches_the_selectors` iterated a fixture defined in the test file | It asserted only that the test author's own three-policy fixture is self-consistent — true by construction. Now iterates the shipped presets and checks both directions |
| 8 | `rules_snapshot_hash(scoring, squad: object)` carried a `type: ignore` | A suppression standing in for a type that was available all along; no cycle to avoid |

## The headline is unmoved

2024-25 GW6-25 after every change: **+363 / +326 / +305 / +187 / 0 / −17 / −215** — identical to before, verified by re-running the backtest. These correct provenance and reporting, not scoring.

## Triaged, not fixed

- **#6 — the team-news sweep reads outside the FPL API, and that is your decision.** `interpreter/news.py` calls Anthropic's `web_search`, so it reads press coverage, and that tool is a paid feature. D6 says *"Official FPL API only, zero budget. No scraping, no paid providers."* It is not a scraper, but "official FPL API only" it is not. The two halves were decided separately: form signals and the LLM extras were kept, and the D6 relaxation that would have permitted a non-FPL source was declined. I documented the tension in `docs/README.md` with what limits the blast radius — off by default, needs an extra and a key, ±15% clamp, source URL required — rather than deleting a feature you chose or quietly rewording a binding decision. **Either D6 gains a stated exception for the sweep, or the sweep goes.**
- **#13 — the 1-4-4-2 starting split is hardcoded.** Real, but `min_play` alone cannot derive it: the positional minimums sum to 7, not 11, so the remaining four slots need a distribution rule. Deriving it hastily risks changing which players start in the headline squad. Left for a change that can be measured.
- **#10 — `write_report` can leave a partial artifact set** if `render_summary` raises. Each file is individually atomic and the aggregates are recomputed from `runs/*.json` every pass, so a partial set is detectable and self-healing rather than corrupting.
- **#5** — the clustering doc already states FPL-only sourcing and names its approximations; no change warranted.
- **#17** — `__setstate__` hygiene; the appended-with-defaults fields already cover the pickle-compatibility case.

## Verification

```
make lint && make types && make boundaries && make banned-strings
uv run pytest -m "not network and not e2e"     # 1220 passed
uv run xg backtest --season 2024-25 --from 6 --to 25 --model .data/models/early.pkl
```

ruff clean · mypy clean on 195 files · import-linter 7/7 · **1220 passed**

---

## Second review round — five more, including one I reintroduced

CodeRabbit re-reviewed the fixes themselves and found six issues. Five were real.

**I reintroduced the mislabelling I had just fixed, one branch further in.** When *nothing* is pinned, `_resolve_rules` falls back to the live bronze snapshot — but reported `source_season=chosen`, which in that branch is `DEFAULT_SEASON`, so `caveat` read *"resolved from the 2026-27 pinned snapshot"* for a file that does not exist. `RulesResolution` gains `pinned: bool`; the fallback now names the season it was asked about and a caveat that says "live bronze snapshot". Tested in both directions.

| defect | consequence |
|---|---|
| **Three more API price sites unguarded** | `adjust_predictions(prices=...)` appears four times in `service.py`; only one was fixed. `int(None)` fails the whole request rather than dropping one player |
| **`actual_prices` could drop a player who had a price** | After sorting, `last()` returns null when the final row's `value` is null, and the comprehension then filters that player out entirely — even when an earlier leg of a double gameweek carried a price. Now `drop_nulls().last()` |
| **An all-null ownership column is as empty as no rows** | The template-squad guard checked `is_empty()`, but a frame that exists with `selected` entirely null fills to zero just the same and returns an arbitrary fifteen |
| **The registration gate had no test for the status that matters** | `register_feature` was tested with `STATIC_PASSED` only. Now parametrised over every non-passing status, so `REJECTED_LEAKAGE` — the one the hardcoded `LEAKAGE_PASSED` made unreachable — is covered. The gate was always right; its input was lying |

**Not fixed:** the budget reserve ignores club capacity. It is a *lower* bound on remaining cost, and ignoring capacity keeps it a valid one — merely loose. Tightening it would accept more feasible squads, which is an optimisation rather than a correctness fix, and it risks moving which players start.

Headline re-verified after every change: **+363 / +326 / +305 / +187 / 0 / −17 / −215**. **1220 passed.**

items.title: fix(rust): install a metrics reader so init_metrics actually exports (closes #772)
items.body:
Closes #772.

`init_metrics` built an `SdkMeterProvider` with **no reader at all** and returned
`Ok(())` for every exporter type. Metrics recorded through `MetricsMiddleware`
went nowhere — no error, no output, nothing at the collector. A caller could not
distinguish "metrics are flowing" from "metrics are silently discarded", because
the API reported success either way.

## What changed

**`"otlp"` and `"stdout"` now install a real exporter** behind a
`PeriodicReader` on a 60s interval (`EXPORT_INTERVAL`, matching the OTel spec
default for `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`, stated explicitly so the delivery
latency is visible in the code rather than inherited).

**`"prometheus"` now returns an error** instead of `Ok(())`. `opentelemetry-prometheus`
was removed from this crate over vulnerable transitive dependencies, so the
scrape endpoint that `Ok(())` promised can never exist. The error message says so
and points at the workaround (export OTLP, let a collector expose `/metrics`).

**An absent endpoint defers to the environment.** `endpoint.filter(|e| !e.is_empty())`
means `None` (or `""`) lets the exporter resolve `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`
→ `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` → the spec default, rather than an explicit empty
string suppressing all three.

**Docs corrected — 12 references, including 2 compiled doctests.** Every
`init_metrics("prometheus", None)` in `README.md`, `docs/API.md`,
`docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`, `docs/observability.md`, the module doctest, and the
`MetricsMiddleware` doctest pointed at the dead exporter; the two doctests would
now fail to pass. `docs/observability.md`'s "Accessing Prometheus Metrics" section
was rewritten to scrape the collector. `docs/OTEL_CONVENTION.md` known-gap 4
changed from "`init_metrics` exports nothing" to "no Prometheus scrape endpoint in
Rust".

Also updated `observability/mod.rs`: the `# Metrics are not yet exported` section
became `# Shutdown is mandatory`, because installing a periodic reader makes
`shutdown_observability()` (added in #774) load-bearing for metrics too — a missed
flush is now total silent loss of the last interval.

## Testing

`agenkit-rust/tests/test_observability_metrics_export.rs` (new, own binary) binds
`127.0.0.1:0`, points `init_metrics` at it, records through `MetricsMiddleware`,
calls `shutdown_metrics()`, and waits on an `mpsc` channel for the accept thread.

It deliberately does **not** assert that `init_metrics` returned `Ok` — the
pre-fix code returned `Ok` too. Only the connection distinguishes them. Verified
negatively: reverted to the no-op and confirmed the test fails with

```
no TCP connection was made to the configured OTLP metrics endpoint
http://127.0.0.1:51429 — no reader/exporter is installed, so nothing is exported
for any exporter type (#772)
```

`test_init_metrics_prometheus` previously asserted `is_ok()`, i.e. it locked in
the bug; it is now `test_init_metrics_prometheus_is_rejected`. The old weak
assertions survive as `test_shutdown_metrics_returns_promptly` with a comment
naming what it does not cover.

The old comment justifying the no-op claimed a reader caused test hangs. That was
stale, not load-bearing: `PeriodicReader` exports from its own OS thread, so init
does not block. Verified empirically (suite completes in 0.01s) rather than
assumed.

Verified locally on this branch, post-rebase: 46 observability tests pass
(13 metrics + 1 metrics-export + 15 tracing + 1 otlp-export + 16 others),
25 doctests pass, `cargo clippy --lib --features opentelemetry` clean on
`src/observability/`, examples build, and `make test` green (exit 0, 291s).

> Note: `agenkit-rust/tests/` is not executed by CI or by `make test` — CI runs
> `cargo test --lib` with `continue-on-error: true`. Both regression tests here
> were run by hand. That gap is filed as #773.

items.title: Add real-data loader, single-user inference, ranking metrics (MAP/MRR), e2e test, and reproducible outputs
items.body:
## Summary
Pushes the project past "synthetic demo" into something with real, runnable
capability — while making the committed data → outputs → README chain
reproducible for the first time.

### New capability
- **Real data**: `data/load_movielens.py` converts a MovieLens export into the
  repo's rating/movie format (contiguous 1-based IDs, comma genres, 1–5 ratings,
  unknown-movie drop). Pure function + `--indir/--outdir` CLI, no network.
- **Inference**: `src/recommend.py` trains on all ratings and prints a top-K
  table for one `--user`, reusing the existing models/reporting/io modules.
- **Richer evaluation**: MAP@K, MRR@K, and a bootstrap confidence-interval
  helper added to `src/metrics.py` and reported alongside Precision/Recall/NDCG.

### Reproducibility (integrity fix)
All files in `outputs/` are regenerated from the committed `data/` using the
pinned versions in `requirements.txt`. The README's baseline, alpha-sweep,
best-alpha, and sample-recommendation tables now match those regenerated
numbers, so the repo reproduces what it documents.

### Tests
- `tests/test_movielens_loader.py`, `tests/test_recommend.py` cover the new modules.
- `tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py` runs the full pipeline via subprocess on tiny
  generated data and asserts all 12 outputs plus metric/recommendation schemas.
- New-metric unit tests added to the existing metrics/alpha-sweep tests.

### Docs
- README gains a MovieLens section, single-user recommend instructions, updated
  project tree, and MAP/MRR rows.
- New `MODEL_CARD.md` (intended use, data, evaluation, limitations).

## Verification
- `ruff`, `black --check`, `mypy src` all clean.
- Full suite: 33 tests pass.
- Precision/Recall/NDCG values unchanged; MAP/MRR are additive.

## Notes
No CI changes needed — new tests are auto-discovered by `unittest discover`,
and the smoke-test's metric-range checks are unaffected by the additive metrics.
No new runtime dependencies.

items.title: science: add BioProBench skill (with review fixes) — supersedes #36
items.body:
## Summary

Supersedes #36. This branch carries **@YuyangSunshine's original five commits unchanged** — she is
the author of the BioProBench skill and of the upstream benchmark it wraps — plus two review commits
that fix defects found in a multi-agent review of that PR.

#36 could not be merged as-is: it was a fork PR whose CI had never been approved to run, so two
deterministic lint failures and a set of scoring bugs were never surfaced. Everything below was
reproduced by executing the real code, not by reading it.

On licensing: the four vendored `Scripts/*.py` come from
[bioprotocolbench](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprotocolbench), which @YuyangSunshine owns.
No non-commercial notice is required; the files carry only a one-line provenance comment.

## What the review commits fix

**The skill did not exist in production.** It was committed as `SKILL.MD`. The loader matches the
literal `child / "SKILL.md"` and skips with a bare `continue` — no log. macOS APFS is
case-insensitive, so it worked on the author's machine and vanished on every Linux CI runner.
Independently, setuptools compiles `MANIFEST.in`'s `*.md` **without** `re.IGNORECASE`, so the
uppercase file was also dropped from the wheel and sdist on *every* platform — a `uv build` produced
`skills/bioprobench/` containing `kernel.py` and the `Scripts/` payload but no `SKILL.md` at all.
Verified after the rename on a real case-sensitive APFS volume (all 33 skills discover) and in the
built wheel (33 × `SKILL.md`, bioprobench included).

**CI lint failed two ways.** `pre-commit` reformatted all five new `.py` files, and
`scripts/check_directory_readmes.py` exited 1 with five violations. Both now pass.

**`import kernel` hard-failed and downloaded at import time.** The guard was
`except ImportError: raise ImportError(...)` — a re-raise, so seven third-party packages that ship in
no bundled env were hard requirements. `nltk.download('punkt')` and `nltk.download('wordnet')` ran at
module scope: network I/O plus a write outside the workspace, inside a sandboxed kernel. Heavy deps
are now lazy per task, so PQA/ORD/ERR no longer drag in the GEN-only torch stack, and the download
moved out of import (and asks for `punkt_tab`, which is what `word_tokenize` needs on nltk ≥ 3.8.2 —
GEN could not have succeeded before). `Scripts/` is loaded privately via `importlib` instead of
`sys.path.append`, which had published three generic top-level module names into the shared
persistent kernel and bypassed the skill gate.

**Four scoring bugs that returned plausible-looking wrong numbers.** None of them raised:

- **ERR** compared JSON-decoded labels with the identity operator (`g is False`), so labels encoded
  as `0`/`1` or `"true"`/`"false"` collapsed precision/recall/F1 to exactly 0 — while accuracy stayed
  *correct*, because that line used `==` and `True == 1`. Same four items: bool labels → `f1=0.8`;
  identical labels as ints → `f1=0`. Nothing in the output distinguished "the model detected no
  errors" from "the label dtype was int". Labels are now normalized, and unrecognized ones reach
  `failed_rate` instead of being scored.
- **ERR** appended predictions and labels in two separate statements, so an item missing
  `is_correct` permanently misaligned every later prediction against the wrong label.
- **ORD** raised `KeyError` outside the per-item handler, so one malformed permutation aborted the
  whole run and discarded every other item's result. A 2-item file with a perfect item 1 returned
  `{'error': "...: 'X'"}` instead of `Exact_Match 0.5`. Ranks were also keyed by step *text*, losing
  pairs when a protocol repeats a step string; they are keyed by index now.
- **PQA** treated the last whitespace token as the confidence unconditionally, so a bare correct
  answer such as `0.3` was consumed as its own confidence and scored **wrong** with a fabricated
  confidence of 0 — and not counted in `Failed_Rate`.

Also: GEN emitted bare `NaN` (not valid JSON); an empty input reported `"status": "success"` over
all-zero metrics; caller-controlled `model_name` was interpolated unsanitized into an output path.

**Documentation and catalog.** Added YAML frontmatter — without it `origin` degraded to `"unknown"`
and the progressive-disclosure summary (the only thing the model sees before loading a skill) was the
truncated BibTeX citation blockquote. Closed a truncated ` ```python ` fence, corrected the documented
API and the input contract (the response file must already merge in ground truth — a plain
model-output file scored 0% and reported success), added the six bilingual READMEs, registered
`bioprobench/` in the catalog, and bumped the bundled-skill count 32 → 33.

**Tests.** `tests/test_bioprobench_skill.py` (27 tests) pins the ERR encoding and PQA confidence
regressions. `scikit-learn` was added to the `science` extra so the two PQA end-to-end tests actually
execute in CI instead of skipping in every environment (25 passed / 2 skipped → 27 passed).

## Known limitations, stated plainly

- **GEN was never executed against its real dependencies.** The sentence-transformers/torch stack plus
  two model checkpoints is not something the offline test environment supports, so only its
  aggregation logic is verified — not the end-to-end path.
- **The PQA no-`&` fallback remains ambiguous** for a multi-word answer whose last token happens to be
  an integer (`incubate for 30`). That is inherent to a format with no separator, and is no worse than
  before.
- `trigger_batch_inference` and `run_llm_judge_evaluation` send data off-machine and take a raw API
  key. That is what those functions are for; it is documented in `SKILL.md` and unchanged here.

## Area

- [x] Skills / science runtime
- [x] Tests / harness / CI
- [x] Docs
- [x] CLI / config / packaging

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Documentation

## Verification

Ran:

```text
uv run pre-commit run --all-files          # all hooks pass
python3 scripts/check_directory_readmes.py # exit 0
uv sync --locked --extra science && uv run pytest   # exit 0
uv build                                   # wheel + sdist contain skills/bioprobench/SKILL.md
```

Plus, on a real case-sensitive APFS volume, the repo's own `SkillLoader` discovers all 33 skills
including `bioprobench`, with `origin: openai4s` and a capability description rather than the citation
blockquote.

Not run:

```text
GEN end-to-end against sentence-transformers / torch
```

Reason:

```text
Requires the torch-scale stack plus two model checkpoints; not supported by the offline test
environment. See "Known limitations" above.
```

## Checklist

### Diff Readiness

* [x] I reviewed and understand the full diff.
* [ ] This PR is small and single-purpose. — it is not: it carries the original feature plus its
  review fixes. Kept together deliberately so the fixes are reviewable against the code they fix.
* [x] No unrelated formatting, broad rewrite, or drive-by refactor is included.
* [x] Hotspot files were edited surgically if touched. *(none touched)*
* [x] `openai4s/server/webui/vendor/` and `tests/fixtures/` were not reformatted.

### Tests

* [x] Relevant tests or manual checks were run and listed above.
* [x] No new test requires live LLM, network, GPU, SSH, Docker, lab hardware, or secrets.
* [x] No tests were deleted without tracked replacements.
* [x] Kernel / host-RPC / gateway changes include focused contract coverage. *(none touched)*

### Core Dependency Policy

* [x] No hard third-party import was added to the core engine, LLM client, or stdlib web server.
* [x] Optional science imports are guarded at every in-tree use site; the skill sidecar imports
  lazily per task and never at module scope.
* [x] New dependencies are documented and justified — `scikit-learn` in the `science` extra, so the
  PQA tests run rather than skip.

### Public Disclosure and Security

* [x] No secrets, API keys, tokens, real credentials, private data, or local absolute paths.
* [x] No unpublished research roadmap or unreleased result is disclosed.
* [x] Docs do not overstate isolation, sandboxing, privacy, or security guarantees.

### Docs

* [x] Docs match actual code behavior.
* [x] User-facing behavior changes are reflected in docs.
* [x] `README.md` and `README_zh.md` stay in sync.

items.title: fix: land stranded P0 bug fixes, add test CI, and implement the coherence audit
items.body:
Sweeps up five things that were sitting unfinished: four P0 bug fixes stranded in a stale worktree, generated artifacts polluting every diff, no test CI, and both halves of an accepted-but-unimplemented coherence design. The doc fixes at the end are drift the new tests found.

## 1. Four P0 bug fixes

Written seven weeks ago, never opened as a PR, replayed onto current `main`. Each was verified still present in `main` before being picked, and the cherry-picks are byte-identical to the originals.

| Bug | Effect |
|---|---|
| `slim_handoff_enabled` declared on the dataclass but never read by `load_config` | the `config.toml` key was silently ignored |
| `CronBackend.install()` / `SystemdBackend.install()` returned fabricated labels | reported success for scheduler jobs that were never installed |
| Metrics outbox claim did SELECT-then-UPDATE with no lock | two `lh` processes read the same pending rows and double-sent |
| No `timeout` on the engram save subprocess | a hung engram hung the hook indefinitely |

The scheduler one is the worst of the four: a backend that lies about having installed jobs is more dangerous than one that does not exist.

## 2. Untrack `graphify-out/`

Four generated artifacts were tracked. `graph.json` alone churns ~42,000 lines whenever the tool runs, and `.graphify_root` stores the absolute path of whichever directory it ran from, so any worktree left permanently dirty. Removed from the index with `git rm --cached`, kept on disk, gitignored. Confirmed `context_inject.py` already degrades to an empty string when the directory is absent, so a fresh clone is unaffected.

## 3. Test CI

The repo had no test workflow. `docs.yml` and `release-please.yml` both trigger only on push to `main`, so **no pull request ran anything** — the two PRs merged before this one were validated solely by a human running the gate locally.

`.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs pytest and ruff across Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 on every PR and on push to `main` (a squash merge produces a commit no PR run ever tested), plus a `docs` job running `mkdocs build --strict` — the third leg of non-negotiable #4, which no PR was running either.

## 4. Coherence audit — Piece A: deterministic tests

Implements the accepted design in `specs/designs/2026-06-20-coherence-audit-design.md`, which had been sitting unbuilt. Three tests under `tests/docs/` now fail the gate when a public doc names something the code does not have:

- `test_cli_reference_coherence.py` — every `lh <command>` written **anywhere under `docs/**`** exists in the click tree (245 invocations checked)
- `test_hooks_doc_coherence.py` — documented hooks vs `_BUILTIN_HOOKS`, asserted in **both** directions
- `test_config_reference_coherence.py` — documented config fields exist on their dataclasses (19 anchors, exact-count guarded)

Direction is `doc ⊆ code`. Each extractor ships with a self-test proving it flags a planted bad name, plus tests pinning each conservatism branch — those branches are what stop a doc phrasing change from breaking everyone's build, so they are not left untested.

## 5. Coherence audit — Piece B: `/coherence-audit`

A slash command for the semantic half no exact rule can decide: ADRs and the backlog describing behavior the code no longer has. Reports findings and appends unresolved ones to `failures.jsonl`, whose schema was read out of `persist_results()` rather than invented. It never auto-edits ADRs, designs, or docs.

## Drift the new tests found, and fixed

Not hypothetical — these were live:

- `docs/getting-started/first-run.md` — `lh profile ls` and `lh profile deploy`, neither of which exists
- `docs/getting-started/migrating.md` — `lh scheduler ls`
- `docs/reference/config.md` — the hooks example used PascalCase event keys while the same page used snake_case elsewhere, named an unregistered hook `session-context`, and wrote `scripts = ["lh hook <name>"]`. That last one matters: `resolve_script_names` resolves **bare** names and **silently skips** what it cannot resolve, so anyone copying the documented example got hooks that did nothing and said nothing.
- Six sentences across `README.md`, `docs/index.md`, `docs/reference/cli.md`, `docs/reference/config.md`, `docs/how/metrics-ingest.md`, `docs/architecture/overview.md` and `docs/getting-started/migrating.md` claimed working systemd/cron scheduler support. Fixing the fabricated-success bug turned those claims into user-visible lies.

## One bug found by review, not by tests

`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` landed in the outbox claim with no rollback path. A failure between the BEGIN and the commit stranded the connection in a transaction holding a RESERVED lock; the next claim then raised "cannot start a transaction within a transaction" and other processes hit "database is locked". Now rolls back and re-raises. `except BaseException` is deliberate — `KeyboardInterrupt` does not subclass `Exception`, and Ctrl-C on a long-running drain is exactly when you do not want a stranded lock.

## The CI found a real bug on its first run

Worth recording, because it is the whole argument for the workflow. The first run went red with four failures that pass on macOS. None came from this branch. One root cause: **the runner has no `config.toml`, and a developer machine does.**

Three of them were a production bug. In `post_tool_use_sync_claude`, the `load_config(config_file())` call sat inside the fail-soft `except Exception: pass` that exists to guard the *sync*. On any machine without a config, `ConfigError` was swallowed, `sync_profiles` was never reached, and the hook exited 0 having synced nothing — the same fabricated-success shape as the scheduler backends this PR fixes. It now falls back to the default adapter, mirroring what `context_inject.py` already did.

The fourth was a genuinely non-hermetic test: a black-box subprocess inherited the real environment, so a config-gated section only appeared because the author's own config enabled it, and the test wrote `hooks.log` into the author's real agent directory. It now gets its own `HOME` and config.

The Linux condition was reproduced locally (`LH_CONFIG_DIR=<empty dir>` gives exactly `4 failed, 982 passed`) before either fix. CI is green on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

## Verification

Locally: 986 passed, `ruff check src tests` clean, `mkdocs build --strict` clean, working tree clean.

On CI: green on all four checks — `docs`, and `test` on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. That is the suite's first run on Linux and the workflow's first run at all.

## Known follow-ups, deliberately not in this PR

- `specs/adrs/013-scheduler-unified-backends.md` still describes systemd and cron writing units and crontabs in the present tense. Real drift, but rewriting an accepted ADR's Decision destroys the record — this needs a status call or an addendum, and it is exactly the kind of finding `/coherence-audit` exists to surface.
- `sinks/worker.py` documents "Never raises to the caller" while `outbox_claim` can propagate; `cli/metrics_cmd.py:110` calls `sink.drain` unwrapped where line 59 wraps it. Both pre-existing, confirmed against the pre-fix tree.
- `CronBackend.uninstall()` / `SystemdBackend.uninstall()` still return `[]`, so uninstall stays quiet while install is now loud. Harmless today because those backends never installed anything, but asymmetric.
- `ruff` runs once per Python matrix leg. ~15s each, judged not worth a second job.
- `tests/unit/test_builtin_context_inject.py::test_context_inject_returns_json` and `::test_context_inject_includes_git_info` still run the hook as a subprocess with no `env=`, so they inherit the real `HOME` and write `hooks.log` into the developer's actual agent directory on every test run. Pre-existing; the same leak was closed for the one test this PR touched.
- `context_inject.main()` is inconsistent about `cfg is None`: graphify and proposals default *on*, qmd suggest defaults *off*, even though the dataclass declares `qmd_suggest_enabled: bool = True`. The declared default is unreachable on an unconfigured machine. Needs a deliberate call — flip it, or document it as opt-in.

items.title: fix(profile): record the compute CPU of a partial cohort slice
items.body:
Stacked on #307. Fixes a bug that #305 introduced in `--profile` accounting. No behavioural change and no cost in a normal build.

## The bug

Cohort slicing gave step 1 a second exit. A cohort that is still accumulating slices seeds and extends its slice, then returns early, because `mem_pestat` needs the whole cohort before pairing and SAM can run. That path saved only `proc_wall`:

```c
if (!ret->cohort_complete) {
    tprof[MEM_PROCESS2][0] += __rdtsc() - tim;
    if (sp_enabled()) ret->prof.proc_wall = sp_wall() - sp_p0;   /* <- and nothing else */
    return ret;
}
```

`g_ktfor` is reset at every step-1 entry, so the slice's `proc_cpu` / `compute` / `encode` / `thr_busy_*` were not merely omitted from that chunk's row — they were destroyed. Nothing else ever reads them.

The result is a profiler that under-reports compute CPU in proportion to how much slicing is happening, and since the aggregate row is derived from the per-chunk rows, the in-`PROCESS()` budget cannot be made to balance at all. This is how it surfaced: I was trying to decompose the 16→64 thread-scaling loss and the numbers would not add up.

At `-t 64` the ramp covers ~40 % of a run's bases, so ~40 % of the compute CPU was missing. Forcing every cohort to slice 4 ways makes it starker — **0.0190 of 0.0851 CPU sec recorded, 78 % discarded**:

```
sliced chunk 40: 12600 bases but proc_cpu=0.0000
sliced chunk 41: 25000 bases but proc_cpu=0.0000
sliced chunk 42: 50000 bases but proc_cpu=0.0000
...
sliced: 10/50 rows report compute CPU, 0.0190 CPU sec total
```

## The fix

Both exits now go through `sp_harvest_proc()`. That is the point of extracting it rather than copying six assignments: a third exit cannot silently drop the harvest, which is exactly how this happened — the whole-cohort path was already correct and the new path was written beside it.

Every call sits inside `if (sp_enabled())`, which is a compile-time `0` unless built with `STAGE_PROF=1`, so a default build is unaffected. Verified: the default build compiles with no `unused-function` warning and `--profile` remains absent from its usage.

## Test

`test/regression/profile_slice_cpu.sh` asserts that every chunk which read bases reports `proc_cpu > 0`. That is a boolean rather than a threshold — a chunk that ran `kt_for` cannot have consumed zero CPU — so there is nothing to tune and nothing to flake.

Two things make it sharp rather than merely present:

- `BWA_MEM3_COHORT_SLICE_ALL=1` slices every cohort instead of only the first, turning a handful of partial slices into 40.
- It refuses to pass vacuously: if slicing produced no partial cohorts, the partial-cohort exit was never entered and the test fails with that explanation instead of reporting a green pass.

Verified both directions on the same binary:

| | rows reporting compute CPU | recorded |
|---|---:|---:|
| unfixed | 10 / 50 | 0.0190 CPU sec |
| fixed | 50 / 50 | 0.0933 CPU sec |

Reads are generated from the committed reference inside the test, so no fixture is added.

It runs from the existing `profiling-build` CI job, since a default build has no `--profile` to assert on. `test/regression/README.md` notes that requirement, because running this script against a default build fails rather than skips.

## Review notes

- `sp_harvest_proc` is placed just above `kt_pipeline` and takes the `sp_wall()` reading from step-1 entry as an argument, so it stays a pure copy-out with no hidden state.
- A slice that only seeds and extends never enters `mem_aln2sam`, so its `encode` is legitimately `0` and `compute` is the whole of `proc_cpu`. The comment says so, because a reader comparing a slice row against a steady-state row will otherwise wonder why `encode` is empty on one and not the other.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved profiling accuracy for partial cohort slices by ensuring processing and compute CPU metrics are fully reported, including early-exit cases.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression coverage for compute CPU accounting in sliced profiling runs.
  * Added validation that profiling output includes complete, non-empty processing metrics.

* **Documentation**
  * Documented the build requirements and CI coverage for the new profiling regression test.

items.title: feat(statistics_llm): add vocab_size parameter for unbiased tail-mass estimation
items.body:
## Problem

The `entropies_approx` and `fastdetectgpt_scores_approx` functions estimate entropy / variance from top-N logprobs by approximating the contribution of the (unobserved) probability mass outside the top-N. The previous heuristic assumed the tail mass `M` was split into `K = M / p_bound` categories each with probability `p_bound = min(p_min, M)`, where `p_min` is the smallest top-N probability.

This heuristic makes a **specific and brittle** assumption about the tail distribution:

- For typical LLM vocabularies (V = 30k-130k) and top-N=100, `K` is usually much smaller than `V - N`, so the heuristic **underestimates** the tail entropy / second moment.
- When `p_min` is very small (peaky top-N distributions, e.g. after a near-deterministic token), `K` can exceed `V - N` and the heuristic **overestimates** instead.
- Either way, the result depends on `p_min` in a way that doesn't reflect the actual tail distribution.

The bias propagates into both metrics:

- `entropies_approx`: the reported entropy is biased (direction depends on `p_min`).
- `fastdetectgpt_scores_approx`: the per-position variance (used as the z-score denominator) is biased, inflating or deflating the score magnitude.

This affects the FastDetectGPT classifier thresholds reported in the dataset README (via `stat_readme.py` -> `readme.py:_build_classifier_section`), which are derived from these biased scores.

## Fix

Add an optional `vocab_size` parameter that switches to a **uniform-tail** assumption: the tail mass `M` is distributed uniformly over `vocab_size - N` tokens. This is the maximum-entropy tail distribution (so it's an upper bound on the true tail entropy / second moment) and is a natural top-N analogue of the full-softmax computation in the Fast-DetectGPT reference implementation (`baoguangsheng/fast-detect-gpt::get_sampling_discrepancy_analytic`).

**Clarification (post-review):** The Fast-DetectGPT reference implementation does **not** use a tail-mass heuristic at all — it operates on the **full softmax** over the entire vocabulary, so there is no `vocab_size - N` to subtract. The uniform-tail assumption in this PR is our adaptation for the top-N-only setting (where some tail approximation is unavoidable), not something inherited from the reference. The reviewer's correction on this point is acknowledged with thanks.

### Changes

- New helper `_tail_moments(p, vocab_size)` that returns `(h_tail, e2_tail, M)` and supports both heuristics. The behaviour for `vocab_size=None` matches the previous code exactly (backwards-compatible).
- `entropies_approx` and `fastdetectgpt_scores_approx` grow a `vocab_size` parameter (default `None` = old behaviour).
- `StatConfig` grows an `llm_vocab_size` field (default `None`).
- `scripts/stat.py` passes `stat_config.llm_vocab_size` through to both metric calls.
- `config/stat.toml` documents the new option with a commented-out example for Llama-3.2 (vocab=128256).

## Why this matters — sanity check

A quick test with top-3 logprobs summing to 0.77 (tail mass 0.23) shows:

```
entropy (concentrated-tail, default): 1.47
entropy (uniform-tail, V=128k):       3.90
entropy (uniform-tail, V=50k):        3.68

fastdetectgpt (concentrated-tail):   +0.90
fastdetectgpt (uniform-tail, V=128k): +0.62
```

The FastDetectGPT score magnitude changes meaningfully depending on the heuristic, which directly affects which side of the classifier threshold a text falls on.

## Backwards compatibility

- Default behaviour (`vocab_size=None`) is byte-identical to the previous code. No existing config or call site needs to change.
- Users who want the more principled approximation can set `llm_vocab_size` in `config/stat.toml`.

## Relationship to other PRs

- **PR #36** (Binoculars model-assignment fix) also rewrote `fastdetectgpt_scores_approx` to use the paper-correct z-score-of-totals formula (replacing the previous per-position-z-score mean). This PR's `_tail_moments` change is purely on the inner variance-estimation side and composes cleanly with #36's outer aggregation fix. Both are needed.
- **PR #33** (top-p outlier tolerance) and **PR #37** (BERTScore / perplexity NaN) are unrelated — neither touches the tail-mass heuristic.

## Rebase note (2026-07-21)

Rebased onto current `main` to resolve a conflict with PR #36's rewrite of `fastdetectgpt_scores_approx`. Resolution: kept main's (#36's) paper-correct docstring and z-score-of-totals implementation, layered PR #32's `_tail_moments` helper and `vocab_size` parameter on top. All PR #32 code changes (`_tail_moments`, `vocab_size` parameter, `DEFAULT_VOCAB_SIZE`, `StatConfig.llm_vocab_size`, `stat.toml` documentation) are intact and verified by smoke test.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Does not change the default behaviour. The old concentrated-tail heuristic is preserved as the default for backwards compatibility. A follow-up PR could flip the default to uniform-tail with `DEFAULT_VOCAB_SIZE = 128000` (defined but currently unused) once we're confident in the new behaviour.
- Does not address the `1e-12` epsilon in `log(p + 1e-12)` (separate numerical-stability concern).
- Does not address the NaN propagation in `readme.py:_build_summary_statistics` (separate issue — `np.mean` of a column with any NaN returns NaN).

items.title: Add EEG brain-age regression task on TUH data
items.body:
## What & why

Adds an **age-regression downstream task** (EEG brain age) alongside the existing classification tasks, plus the metadata extraction it needs. Opt in with `data.dataset=TUAB_AGE`; nothing changes for existing runs.

The question this started from was *where TUH exposes patient age*. It turns out to be already present in every EDF file you have.

## Where the age comes from

TUH **no longer distributes clinical reports**, so the EDF header is the only source of demographics — and it's a complete one. The standard *local patient identification* field (bytes 8:88) holds it directly:

```
aaaaantl F 01-JAN-0000 aaaaantl Age:42
 subject sex dob        subject   age
```

**MNE cannot give you this.** `raw.info['subject_info']` returns only `{his_id, sex, last_name}` — the DOB is anonymized to `01-JAN-0000`, so there is nothing to subtract a birth year from. Raw-byte parsing is mandatory; `make_TUAB.py` uses MNE and so never saw the age.

### Validation

On TUAB v3.0.0 the parser finds an `Age:` field in **all 2,993 recordings (100%, 0 missing)**, and the parsed values reproduce the corpus `AAREADME.txt` DEMOGRAPHICS tables **exactly** — every age decade bucket per split × label, and every gender count. That agreement is the evidence the byte offsets are right.

Sentinels are excluded, never trained on: `Age:999` is TUH's HIPAA redaction for 90+ (its 12 files match the README's "90-100" row exactly, per split and label), and `Age:0` is ambiguous. Usable ages 1–89: 2,978 recordings, mean 49.1, std 17.4.

## No re-preprocessing

Processed window filenames map 1:1 onto EDF stems, so ages join onto the **existing** pickles via an `age_metadata.json` sidecar. Both prep steps are read-only w.r.t. the ~409k pickles and take seconds, not a multi-hour MNE pass.

## Subject-disjoint splits (fixes a leak)

The shipped `processed/` split has **16 subjects in both train and val**: `make_TUAB.py` splits subjects independently within `normal/` and `abnormal/`, and 54 train subjects appear as both. It's also unseeded. For age this leaks badly — a subject's age is near-constant (measured within-subject spread: mean 1.4 years; 194 of 443 multi-file subjects have spread 0).

`age_splits.py` rebuilds train/val by subject with a fixed seed and asserts zero overlap on **both save and load**. TUAB's official eval set is untouched.

| split | subjects | recordings | windows | age mean ± std |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | 1,650 | 2,145 | 294,253 | 48.9 ± 17.8 |
| val | 412 | 556 | 75,717 | 48.1 ± 15.8 |
| test | 251 | 274 | 36,728 | 49.9 ± 17.8 |

## Task plumbing

`nb_classes == 1` already means "binary" across ~20 call sites, so the task lives on `DatasetBundle.task` / `FinetuneModelConfig.task` rather than being inferred. It selects the criterion (Huber by default), the metrics, the absence of a sigmoid, and lower-is-better model selection on MAE. **The head needs no new model code** — `nb_classes=1` is already `nn.Linear(embed_dim, 1)`, and the checkpoint loader already drops a mismatched head.

Targets are z-scored by the loader with **train-split** stats and de-normalized once before metrics, so errors read in **years**. Alongside MAE/RMSE/R²/Pearson, the metrics include the brain-age diagnostics `age_bias_slope` (residual-vs-true slope — the regression-to-the-mean signature) and `mae_corrected`.

Split **by subject**, aggregate **by recording**: the corpus README warns a subject may appear more than once *with different ages*, so age is a property of the session, not the subject. These are independent knobs and both are set deliberately.

## Two bugs found while verifying

Reviewers may care about these most, since one affects existing runs:

1. **CV dropped the target normalization.** `_build_split_dataset` rebuilds fold loaders positionally, so `target_stats` was lost; folds emitted raw ages that were then de-normalized a *second* time, inflating MAE ~18×. Such state is now carried across the rebuild. Regression-tested.
2. **`enable_window_ids` didn't recurse into `ConcatDataset`.** A CV fold is a `ConcatDataset` whenever its groups span several source loaders, so **every CV run — classification included — silently reported per-window metrics as if they were per-case.** It now recurses through `Subset` and `ConcatDataset`. Regression-tested.

## Verification

- **547 tests pass (72 new).** The 2 `test_model_graph.py` failures are **pre-existing** — they fail identically on a clean tree (a graphviz environment issue), confirmed by stashing.
- On the real corpus: both prep CLIs; a plain fine-tune and a 3-fold CV run (Huber criterion logged, MAE in years, case aggregation firing, empty `subject_overlap`).
- An untrained head correctly reproduces the **predict-the-cohort-mean baseline** — `pred_mean` 49.9 with `pred_std` 0.05, and MAE exactly `|49.88 − 26| = 23.88`. That's a precise check that de-normalization is right.
- A TUAB **classification** run still emits its full 65 classification metrics unchanged (`class_acc`, `roc_auc`, confusion matrix, accuracy-based selection), with no regression keys.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The one shared-code-path change is `TUHLoader.label_fn`, now `(sample, filename)` — the age is keyed by recording, not stored per window. TUAB/TUEV `label_fn`s ignore the new arg; covered by an explicit classification-unchanged test.
- Group-id helpers now derive ids from the **basename**, because a pooled split stores files as `<subdir>/<name>.pkl` so each split stays one loader rather than a `ConcatDataset`. Behaviour for flat filenames is identical.
- `TUABAgeLoader` filters unlabelled windows **at construction**, because `TUHLoader.__getitem__` swallows `KeyError` and substitutes a different window — a missing age would otherwise corrupt targets invisibly.
- All 10 existing default JSONs gained the new fields (additive only; the config loader enforces exact field-set parity).
- The parser is corpus-agnostic and scales unchanged to TUEG v2.0.2 (26,846 sessions, ages 2 days–106 yrs) for ~10× more labels.
- `make_TUAB.py` is deliberately untouched; its unseeded/leaky split remains a pre-existing issue for the classification task, worth a separate fix.
- A model predicting the train mean scores MAE ≈ 14; published EEG brain-age benchmarks land around **7–8 years**, which is the target.

See `docs/age_regression.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: #5405: correct stale ServiceMonitor gating doc + lock gating with a regression test (false-positive premise)
items.body:
## Problem

#5405 reported the kubernetes-live ServiceMonitor as **dangling** — rendering without its backing metrics Service whenever `observability.prometheus.enabled` is false — because `deploy/helm/eshu/templates/servicemonitor.yaml`'s `kubernetesLiveCollector` block (~line 506) reads as gated only on `{{- if .Values.kubernetesLiveCollector.enabled }}`, while the sibling metrics Service requires both `kubernetesLiveCollector.enabled` **and** `observability.prometheus.enabled`.

**That reading is a false positive**, and it traces to a stale doc: `go/internal/collector/kuberneteslive/README.md` (from PR #5396) claimed the ServiceMonitor "renders whenever the collector is enabled — gated only on `kubernetesLiveCollector.enabled`."

The per-block `if` at line 506 is not the effective gate. `servicemonitor.yaml` opens at line 1 with a **file-wide** `{{- if and .Values.observability.prometheus.enabled .Values.observability.prometheus.serviceMonitor.enabled }}` that is not closed until the file's final line — every one of the 23 per-collector blocks, this one included, is nested inside it. So the ServiceMonitor's effective gate is `kubernetesLiveCollector.enabled AND prometheus.enabled AND serviceMonitor.enabled` — a strict **subset** of the Service's `kubernetesLiveCollector.enabled AND prometheus.enabled`. It can never render without the Service.

Empirical proof (unmodified `origin/main`):

| flags | Service | ServiceMonitor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prometheus.enabled=false` | ✗ | ✗ (0 rendered) |
| `prometheus.enabled=true`, `serviceMonitor.enabled=false` | ✓ | ✗ |
| both + `serviceMonitor.enabled=true` | ✓ | ✓ (1 rendered) |

## Fix

No functional Helm change — the template is already correctly (and more strictly) gated. This PR fixes the **documentation bug** that caused the false report and locks the behavior:

- `go/internal/collector/kuberneteslive/README.md` — corrected to describe the file-wide guard and the actual effective gate.
- `go/internal/runtime/helm_live_collectors_contract_test.go` — new `TestHelmKubernetesLiveCollectorServiceMonitorGatingMatchesService` (the truth table above): prometheus off → neither renders; prometheus on / serviceMonitor off → Service only; both on → both. Verified to **fail** against a scratch template with the outer guard removed, and **pass** against the real one — a genuine regression guard so the ServiceMonitor can never drift to render without its Service.

Per #5405's "OR document an intentional reason it differs" acceptance path.

## Proof

- `helm template` with each flag combination above — counts as tabulated.
- `helm lint deploy/helm/eshu` — clean.
- `go test ./internal/runtime/ -run TestHelm -count=1` — green (incl. the new test); `mkdocs build --strict` — succeeded. `make pre-pr`: all gates passed. Self-review: P0=0, P1=0, P2=0.

Closes #5405.

items.title: fix: enable the admin API by default again, disable via CADDY_ADMIN=off
items.body:
## Summary

Re-enables Caddy's admin API by default on the standalone instance, and makes disabling it work through both `CADDY_ADMIN=off` and the Caddyfile-native `admin off` global option. **We are changing the default back to admin ON because that matches Caddy's own default** — and we use Caddy's own constant for it (`caddy.DefaultAdminListen`, i.e. `localhost:2019`, loopback only, not exposed externally), so the value tracks upstream and is spelled out in the generated config.

## Background

v2.13.0 (#817/#819) moved the local config push in-process (`caddy.Load`) and, since the local instance no longer needs the admin API to reload, disabled the admin endpoint for local loads. That was a silent behavior change: anything relying on the admin endpoint after startup broke — e.g. a Docker healthcheck or a scrape hitting `localhost:2019/metrics`. Reported in #820.

## Change

The plugin only sets the local instance's admin config when the config leaves it absent; anything explicit is respected untouched:

- **Default (nothing set):** admin listens on `caddy.DefaultAdminListen` (`localhost:2019`). Loopback only.
- **`CADDY_ADMIN=<address>`** sets the local admin listen (also unix sockets, e.g. `unix//run/caddy-admin.sock`). Still used for remote servers' admin listen too.
- **`CADDY_ADMIN=off`** disables the admin API, at bootstrap and on every reload. Caddy itself has no disable semantics for this variable (in vanilla Caddy, `off` becomes an invalid listen address and errors), so the plugin applies it. Mirrors the Caddyfile's `admin off`.
- **An explicit admin config from labels or a base Caddyfile is respected untouched** — including `admin off` (e.g. label `caddy.admin: off`), previously overridden back on. Local loads happen in-process and don't need the admin endpoint. An explicit config also wins over `CADDY_ADMIN=off`.
- **Remote controlled servers always keep a reachable admin endpoint** (`tcp/<server>:2019`) — controller pushes require it, so `admin off` is still overridden there. Caddy's own default wouldn't work for them: it binds loopback on the remote host, unreachable for the controller.
- The in-process `caddy.Load` push from #817 is kept — admin on/off is now independent of how config is loaded.

## Tests

Both paths (bootstrap `buildCaddyAdminConfig` + reload `prepareServerConfig`) × all cases (nothing set / address / off / label off):

- `TestParseAdminEnv` — `off` (case-insensitive/trimmed) → disabled; any other value → listen address (unix sockets kept as-is).
- Bootstrap: `TestBuildCaddyAdminConfig` / `TestBuildCaddyRunConfig` / `TestBuildCaddyLoggingConfig` — default is `caddy.DefaultAdminListen`; `CADDY_ADMIN` address sets the listen; `CADDY_ADMIN=off` disables and drops the admin logger.
- Reload: `TestPrepareServerConfig` — local default is `caddy.DefaultAdminListen`; `CADDY_ADMIN` address sets the listen; `CADDY_ADMIN=off` and config `admin off` disable locally; explicit config listen wins over `CADDY_ADMIN=off`; remote always stays on.
- Integration: `TestIntegration_LocalPushUsesCaddyLoad` (admin off, still loads in-process) and `TestIntegration_LocalPushEnablesAdmin` (admin reachable after a local load).

items.title: Stable Audio 3 engine, Qwen rewriter, --record, --loop, and the docs to match
items.body:
Nine commits: the engine swap to **Stable Audio 3**, the Qwen prompt-rewrite
stage it requires, a `--record` terminal booth, a real seamless-loop wrap
(`--loop`), and a docs pass bringing README/AGENTS back in line with the code.

## What changed

| | |
|---|---|
| `--engine sa3` | **Stable Audio 3** replaces Stable Audio Open as the default for SFX *and* music. Full-band — measured cutoff at Nyquist (22.1 kHz) on raw WAV, vs ACE-Step's hard 16 kHz VAE ceiling. |
| Qwen rewriter | SA3's official workflow runs an LLM over the description first, under four category-specific system prompts (`sa3_reprompt.json`, verbatim from ComfyUI). On by default. |
| **`--loop`** | Crossfades a track's tail back over its head so it loops seamlessly. Measured: tail **−39.4 dB → +0.7 dB** relative to body. |
| `--record` | A recording booth in the terminal — reads the same `key \| text` manifest `--narrate` does, and masters takes through the same chain, so a hand-voiced pack and a generated one are interchangeable per line. |
| loudness | `--lufs` (EBU R128) and `--true-peak` ceilings; attenuate-only, so a high-crest transient can never be pushed into clipping. |
| `--ogg-quality` | default 8, and the `%` in its help string escaped — it was breaking *every* invocation. |
| `tools/spectral-check.py` | measures spectral cutoff, to catch hollow output that every other check passes. |

## Stable Audio 3 has four independent ways to silently produce noise

All four were hit here, and none of them fail loudly — you get a valid WAV of
the correct length containing static:

| Setting | Correct | What the wrong value sounds like |
|---|---|---|
| precision | `--force-fp32` | buzzing / radio static |
| checkpoint | `medium` | scrambled, "record scratching" |
| sampler / steps / cfg | `lcm` / 8 / 1.0 | noise; 50 steps gives clacking |
| prompt | Qwen-rewritten | valid audio, poor musical content |

`soundmon.py` now sets all of these automatically for `--engine sa3`. The one
that can't be — `--force-fp32`, a server-launch flag — is documented prominently.

## Loops: the intuitive fix was worse than doing nothing

A track that plays continuously has a hole at the seam. The obvious cause is
post-processing — silence-trimming and de-click fades touching the endpoints —
so the obvious fix is `--no-trim --fade-ms 0`. **Measured, that makes it worse:**

| endpoint policy | tail vs body |
|---|---|
| trim on, 5 ms fade | −30.4 dB |
| trim off, no fade | **−66.6 dB** |

Trimming was *helping*. The real cause is that **the model composes an ending** —
a 60 s request returns a 60 s piece of music with a decay. No endpoint policy
fixes that, because the hole is musical content, not processing damage.

`--loop` constructs the loop instead: `O[0:X] = S[0:X]·fade_in + S[T:L]·fade_out`,
so `O[T-1]` into `O[0]` is `S[T-1]` into `S[T]` — adjacent samples of the
original take. Contiguous by construction, verified bit-exact at the wrap points.
`--loop` forces `trim` on and `fade_ms` to 0 itself, so the bad combination
can't be reproduced from outside.

## The lesson that mattered most

**1,122 files passed every automated check** — duration, peak, LUFS, true-peak,
readability — while sounding, to the person who could actually hear them, like
"trash". The envelope check didn't catch it either; fp16 noise has a perfectly
plausible envelope.

AGENTS.md now says this outright: an agent working here cannot hear the output,
every metric is a proxy, and audio must not be reported as working on metrics
alone. Audition early and in small batches — a 1,100-file run that turns out to
be noise costs hours; three files cost minutes.

The loop bug is the same lesson in miniature: a plausible cause was asserted and
acted on without measuring. The measurement took two minutes and reversed the
conclusion.

## Also documented

- **A fast-failing farm box eats the queue** — dynamic dispatch hands work to
  whoever is free, and a box that fails in 2 s frees up far more often than one
  that succeeds in 90 s. One broken machine took 30 of 46 jobs.
- **Model swapping, not sampling, is the cost** on an 8 GB card: 75.6 s/asset
  with the rewrite inline vs ~4 s with rewrites pre-computed.

items.title: Hardened no-hallucination pipeline, natural conversation, advanced evals, and UX polish
items.body:
# Hardened no-hallucination pipeline, natural conversation, advanced evals, and UX polish

This PR promotes the completed take-home implementation from `dev` to `main`: the full retrieval/verification hardening, a natural-conversation layer, a three-script evaluation stack proving the no-hallucination guarantee end-to-end, live-verified chat UX improvements, and a README rewritten as a complete technical presentation of the system.

## Retrieval quality: hybrid fusion + cross-encoder reranking

- Dense (Pinecone) and lexical (Postgres full-text) retrieval fused per company via reciprocal-rank fusion, then reranked with a local cross-encoder (`BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3`) from a wide pool (30) down to the final evidence set (10) — `backend/app/agent/{hybrid_tool,reranker,reranked_tool}.py`, wired in `main.py`. Fail-open on reranker errors, with dropped chunks recorded for debuggability.

## No-hallucination verification, proven live

- **`scripts/eval_baseline.py`** — the 3 required Thai acceptance questions + 5 refusal/clarify probes against the live stack: **8/8 passing**.
- **`scripts/eval_ragas.py`** — RAGAS quality scoring (faithfulness floor, answer relevancy, context recall/precision) behind an optional `eval` dependency group.
- **`scripts/eval_advanced.py`** (new) — 15 adversarial + naturalness probes: estimate-baiting, prompt injection, mixed-coverage comparisons (Apple vs. Siemens), multi-turn year exploits via history, Thai out-of-coverage, NULL-metric acknowledgment, unit traps, false premises, negative net income phrasing, repeated-refusal wording variation, and grounded investment answers. All ground truth is recomputed from `data/financial_data.sql` at runtime.
- **Verify-node fixes found by the adversarial suite**: sign-insensitive grounding (a "loss of $2,722,000,000" now grounds against SQL's `-2722000000` — magnitude still can't be fabricated), rounded chunk-paraphrase matching (a draft's "$342.7 billion" now grounds against a filing's literal `342,745` millions figure), and prose "10-K" designator stripping. All regression-tested.
- **Synthesis-prompt fixes found by the adversarial suite**: false premises are corrected instead of adopted (asking why revenue "declined" when it grew now gets a correction, not a fabricated decline narrative), and figure scale words come from the actual USD values instead of echoing a user's wrong "million/billion".
- Router prompt fix: canonical short company names ("Amazon", not "Amazon.com, Inc.") so the deterministic coverage gate resolves covered companies reliably.
- Throughout every eval run — including the failures that drove fixes — **zero fabricated numbers reached a user-visible answer**; every failure mode was fail-closed (refusal or verify veto).

## Natural, dynamic conversation

- **No parroted refusals**: each refusal reason ships three deterministic phrasing variants per language (en/th), selected by counting prior refusals in the conversation — a second refusal acknowledges the repetition and steers toward answerable questions. Zero LLM calls, zero new facts, so the no-hallucination guarantee is untouched.
- **Investment questions handled gracefully**: "Should I invest in Apple?" now routes to data and returns a grounded, balanced read of actual financial trends with a mandatory not-personalized-advice disclaimer, instead of a blunt scope refusal. Uncovered companies still fail closed through the unchanged coverage gate.
- Synthesis tone guidance: professional and conversational, no projection wording for reported actuals, natural phrasing for NULL metrics.

## Chat UX (verified live in the browser)

- **Per-node progress status** — a fixed-id `data-status` SSE part streams "Querying financial data… → Searching 10-K filings… → Writing the answer…" under animated typing dots, removing the dead air between the route badge and the first token.
- **Distinct refusal/clarify rendering** — refusals appear in a destructive-tinted callout with a warning icon; clarifications in a neutral outlined callout with a question icon.
- Verified end-to-end in the running app: grounded answers with correct figures and sources, refusal callout, and varied repeat-refusal wording all confirmed via browser walkthrough.

## Docs

- README rewritten as a full technical presentation: the seven-layer no-hallucination defense, LangGraph architecture with a mermaid diagram, conversation-quality features, four-tier evaluation strategy, auth design, config surface, trade-offs, and roadmap.
- Evidence-driven Option B (re-ingestion) design doc added to `docs/` for the roadmap.

## Test/verification summary

- Offline unit suite: **200 passed** (all stubbed, $0).
- Live `eval_baseline.py`: **8/8**. Live `eval_advanced.py`: **15/15** (11/15 on the full pre-fix run; the 4 failing cases each drove a fix above and pass on rerun).
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` succeeds.
- Browser walkthrough on `http://localhost:3000`: registration → grounded SQL answer → refusal callout → varied repeat refusal → hybrid comparison answer, all correct.

items.title: M1 — retrieval and eval harness
items.body:
Hybrid retrieval over the semantic index, the eval runner, and the first committed baseline. Closes the M1 exit criterion in PRD §8: metrics reported for both question groups, baseline committed.

## The numbers

```
aggregate_set_f1  1.000   drift tripwire, not a result — see below
recall_at_5       0.350   class 5: 0.500 · class 6: 0.125
mrr_at_10         0.232   class 5: 0.351 · class 6: 0.052
```

`evals/baselines/main.json`, config `d487120aa413`, corpus `master@95f8322ee1dc`.

**recall@5 of 0.350 is weak and is committed as-is rather than tuned toward.** `gold_chunks` were chosen by reading issue threads, never by querying the retriever, so the number is honest. The diagnosis is below.

**Set-F1 is 1.0 by construction.** With no agent choosing the query, classes 1–4 dispatch the very `gold_query` that generated the ground truth. It stays in the run because it still catches a `FactsStore` change or a re-ingest at a different revision, and the output labels it as a drift tripwire. It measures the system only at M2, when tool selection picks the query.

## The finding worth reading

Exact chunk recall@5 is 0.350; **parent-document recall@5 is 0.900**. The retriever finds the right conversation and the wrong comment.

q043 ("Do websocket routes work on APIRouter, or only on the FastAPI app?") returns 8 of its top 10 from `issue:98` — exactly the thread the answer lives in — with the gold `issue:98#comment-0` at rank 17. The ranking signal is sound; the granularity is wrong.

TRD §17.3 asked for this A/B "at M1". It now has a number to beat. Two questions (q044, q047) miss even at parent level — both ask a general capability question whose answer sits in a specifically-titled thread — and expansion will not help them.

## What's here

- `app/retrieval/hybrid.py` — the `Retriever` protocol per §6.1–6.3. Dense HNSW at `ef_search=100`, sparse `ts_rank_cd`, RRF `k=60` untuned per ADR 3, `HYBRID_ENABLED` as ablation axis A.
- `evals/runner.py` — scorers, `--json` baseline output, and `--question <id> --explain` for manual inspection. That flag is how the §17.3 measurement was found.
- `evals/baselines/main.json` — first baseline, stamped `milestone: M1`.
- `tests/test_hybrid.py`, `tests/test_runner.py` — 23 new tests.

Two failure modes here are silent rather than loud, and both are covered: `SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search` outside a transaction is a no-op that leaves `ef_search` at 40, and a sparse query that skips `tsv_input` never reaches the decomposed identifier tokens ingest wrote (ADR 12). A test asserts "http exception" still reaches `HTTPException`.

## Doc changes

TRD §14 assumed an orchestrator emitting SSE, tools, and citations — all M2 — while PRD §8 makes a committed baseline an M1 exit criterion. M1 could not satisfy both.

- **§14.1** — the runner has two shapes; the scorer table gained a `From` column; set-F1's M1 meaning is recorded.
- **§14.2** — `corpus_ref` in the hash is the resolved `symbolic@sha`. The section exists to make cross-corpus comparison impossible by accident, and `master` hashes identically after every re-ingest.
- **§14.3** — baselines carry a `milestone`. M1 has three metrics; M2 will have six with set-F1 meaning something different.
- **§17.3** — measured.
- **§17.8** — new. M6 frontend stack undecided; §11.2's SSE contract is the only hard constraint and no client has exercised it yet.

No PRD change — §5.6 and the M6 milestone are deliberately stack-agnostic.

## Also

`fix(dev)` commit is a pre-existing break, separable from M1: the project has no `build-system` and is never installed into the venv, so bare `pytest` died at conftest import while `python -m pytest` worked. The README documents the former.

## Verification

```
uv run ruff check .                     clean
uv run pytest                           295 passed (272 existing + 23 new)
uv run python evals/build_gold.py --check   ground truth still reproduces from the pin
uv run python evals/runner.py           the table above
```

No network and no API key: embeddings are local, so every metric here is deterministic and reproducible in CI.

items.title: ROX-35889: fix OpenShift SCC for monitoring chart
items.body:
## Description

Fixes OpenShift installs of the internal `deploy/charts/monitoring` chart ([ROX-35889](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ROX-35889)). Discovered during testing of https://github.com/stackrox/roxie/pull/252.

### Problems

- When installing, Helm reported a successful install, but the Alertmanager and kube-state-metrics pods never became Ready.
- Those subchart pods (prometheus, grafana, alertmanager) run as UID and fsGroup `65534` by default. OpenShift `restricted-v2` rejects that identity because it is outside the namespace UID range.
- Only the parent `monitoring` ServiceAccount was allowed to use SCC `nonroot-v2`. The Alertmanager and kube-state-metrics ServiceAccounts were not, so admission never selected a compatible SCC.
- The Prometheus container was OOMKilled under fixed memory limits. With no memory limit it settled around 5Gi RSS on the test cluster.
- A raw `helm` install failed when `${MONITORING_ENABLE_PSP}` was left unsubstituted, because Helm treated that string as true and rendered a PodSecurityPolicy that modern clusters no longer have.
- OpenShift's image-registry controller writes `imagePullSecrets` on ServiceAccounts. Helm server-side apply also manages that field, which caused upgrade conflicts.
- kube-state-metrics repeatedly logged failures for `autoscaling/v2beta2` HorizontalPodAutoscaler, an API that current clusters no longer serve.
- The chart still used Helm v2-style `requirements.lock` while declaring Chart.yaml `apiVersion: v2`, which triggers Helm warnings.

### Approach
- Bind `<release>-alertmanager` and `<release>-kube-state-metrics` to the existing namespace-scoped `nonroot-v2` Role
- Override subchart securityContexts to UID/GID `1000`/`2000` (aligned with the parent Deployment); Alertmanager pod-level `runAsUser` covers the configmap-reload sidecar
- Prometheus: `2Gi` memory request, no memory limit, keep `1000m` CPU limit
- Default `enableMonitoringPSPs: false`
- Put Docker Hub `imagePullSecrets: stackrox` on Pods (not the monitoring SA) to keep Hub auth without SA field-manager conflicts
- Drop the kube-state-metrics `horizontalpodautoscalers` collector
- Migrate `requirements.lock` → `Chart.lock`
- Expand the chart README (envsubst / `--set`, OpenShift `--force-conflicts`)


## User-facing documentation

- [x] [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/stackrox/stackrox/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) is updated **OR** update is not needed
- [x] [documentation PR](https://spaces.redhat.com/display/StackRox/Submitting+a+User+Documentation+Pull+Request) is created and is linked above **OR** is not needed

Internal-only deploy chart; no product docs/CHANGELOG.

## Testing and quality

- [x] the change is production ready: the change is [GA](https://github.com/stackrox/stackrox/blob/master/PR_GA.md), or otherwise the functionality is gated by a [feature flag](https://github.com/stackrox/stackrox/blob/master/pkg/features/README.md)
- [ ] CI results are [inspected](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1d5ga073jkv4CO1kAJqp8MPGpC6E1bwyrCGZ7S5wKg3w/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w4ercgtcg0xp)

Internal engineer tooling chart (not product GA surface).

### Automated testing

- [ ] added unit tests
- [ ] added e2e tests
- [ ] added regression tests
- [ ] added compatibility tests
- [ ] modified existing tests

No chart unit/e2e harness for this internal chart; validated manually on OpenShift.

### How I validated my change

- `helm template` with and without OpenShift API capabilities (SCC RoleBinding gated; no PSP when default false)
- Fresh install / upgrade of release `test-monitoring` on OpenShift cluster
- Confirmed Ready: `monitoring`, `test-monitoring-alertmanager-0`, `test-monitoring-kube-state-metrics`
- Prometheus no longer OOMKilled; RSS ~5Gi with no memory limit
- Grafana/Prometheus logs healthy aside from minor/non-blocking noise
- Used `--force-conflicts` once for residual kube-state-metrics SA `imagePullSecrets` SSA conflict (upstream chart always emits that field)

Partially generated by AI.

#### Manual testing steps and results

1. `helm uninstall test-monitoring` (old release)
2. `helm upgrade --install` from stackrox3 chart (`--force-conflicts`, PSP off, dummy PagerDuty key)
3. Checked pods Ready + SCC / securityContext / resources

##### Checks

| Check | How | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install succeeds | `helm -n stackrox list` → `deployed` | pass |
| monitoring Ready | `kubectl get deploy monitoring` → `1/1` | pass |
| alertmanager Ready | `kubectl get sts …-alertmanager` → `1/1` | pass |
| kube-state-metrics Ready | `kubectl get deploy …-kube-state-metrics` → `1/1` | pass |
| Subchart SCC = `nonroot-v2` | pod annotation `openshift.io/scc` | pass (AM + KSM) |
| SAs bound to `nonroot-v2` | `RoleBinding/monitoring-use-scc` subjects | pass (3 SAs) |
| UID/fsGroup `1000`/`2000` | pod/container `securityContext` | pass |
| No mem limit / `2Gi` request | deploy prometheus resources; `top` ~5Gi | pass |
| No PSP rendered | no `PodSecurityPolicy` object | pass |
| Pull secret on Pod, not SA | deploy `imagePullSecrets`; SA has dockercfg only | pass |
| No HPA collector | KSM `--resources=` omits `horizontalpodautoscalers` | pass |

**Note:** Alertmanager has no Grafana UI / Route (`exposure: none`). ClusterIP `:9093` only; use port-forward to open the AM UI.


[ROX-35889]: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ROX-35889?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

items.title: finance: rebuild the SaaS metrics workbook on real data
items.body:
## Why

The July 2026 workbook (`GovHub_SaaS_Metrics` in Drive, created 2026-07-05) reported **$1,085 MRR, 5 paying customers, 4,250 organic clicks and 10,000 cold emails sent**. None of it was real — it was placeholder data written to exercise the formulas, labelled "ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE DATA" in the README, and never overwritten with actuals. Those figures would not have survived the first request for a Stripe export.

This replaces every one of them with a queried, cited value.

## What the data actually says (2026-08-13)

| | Workbook claimed | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| MRR | $1,085 | **$0** |
| Paying customers | 5 | **0** |
| Cold emails sent | 10,000 | **0** |
| Signups | — | 30 (9 external, 21 founder alias / test) |
| Activated | — | 21 |
| Proposals generated | — | 30 |

**Zero paying customers is not a conversion problem.** Every row in the `plans` table has a null `stripe_price_id` for both monthly and annual, so no code path can charge a card. 26 trials expired with no way to pay. Trial → paid is 0% structurally, not behaviourally.

### Genuinely strong

- **1 → 114 organic keywords in eight weeks** (Semrush, `us` database)
- **`govwin`** — 9,900 searches/mo, $12.59 CPC — sits at **position 23** and already carries **70% of organic traffic**. Moving it into the top 10 is the highest-leverage SEO action available.
- **70% activation rate** (21/30), against a 40–60% benchmark
- Anthropic API peaked at **$26.75/mo**. Margin is not the constraint.
- Total burn: **$393.98/mo**

## Changes

- `docs/GovHub_SaaS_Metrics_v2.xlsx` — 11 tabs, 824 formulas, zero formula errors
- `scripts/finance/build-saas-workbook.py` — the generator. Every actual is a named constant carrying the query or file it came from, so the workbook is reproducible rather than hand-maintained.
- `docs/saas-metrics-workbook.md` — data sources, findings, and the open items

### Two new tabs

**Funnel** — channel → visitor → signup → activated → engaged → paid, with the conversion rate at every step, broken out per channel (SEO / cold email / vendor-PR / direct).

**Calculator** — scenario engine over conversion rates, pricing and tier mix, churn, CAC and CLTV, plus four sensitivity grids (LTV and LTV:CAC across churn × ARPA; new customers across trial→paid × volume; months-to-$10k-MRR). At its defaults: CAC $1,266 · LTV $4,026 · LTV:CAC 3.2x · payback 6.3 months.

The Calculator imputes **$5,000/mo of founder time** to sales & marketing by default. At $0 the CAC is only the software bill and LTV:CAC lands near 65x, which is not a presentable number. The cell is a documented lever.

Actuals and modelled figures are kept in **separate columns** on every tab so the two cannot be confused again.

## Open items for the author

1. **Supabase is absent from the cost list** but the GovProp project is `ACTIVE_HEALTHY` in production — free tier (capacity risk) or a missing cost line? Stubbed at $0 pending an answer.
2. **Vendor/PR outreach has no tracking.** 48 emails sent via Resend, `email_events` has 0 rows, so that channel's funnel contribution is unmeasurable. Wiring the Resend webhooks would fix it cheaply.

## Verification

`recalc.py` (LibreOffice) reports `status: success`, `total_errors: 0` across 824 formulas. Cross-sheet references and computed outputs were spot-checked against the source queries.
